fix(op-node): use time.Now() instead of channel peek to detect sequencer deadline

Previous logs showed DrainUntil running for 3.67s with sequencerChReady=false
throughout, yet the sequencer timer had been scheduled to fire 2.85s into the
cascade. Hypothesis: during a CPU-bound event cascade (consolidating a 4000+
block span batch with ~20000 events), Go's runtime fails to deliver the timer
value to the channel — the timer goroutine may be starved or the runtime
scheduler cannot preempt the tight event loop to run runtime-internal timer
delivery.

Replace the channel peek (len(sequencerCh) > 0) with a direct time.Now()
comparison against the sequencer's next action deadline. time.Now() reads
the monotonic clock directly without depending on any goroutine being
scheduled, so it works regardless of runtime behavior during a hot loop.

Also adds callback count and interrupted flag to the diagnostic log.

The previous channel peek (len(sequencerCh) > 0) did not work on real
sequencers under heavy derivation load. When consolidating a large span
batch (~4000 blocks, ~15000+ events), Go's runtime fails to deliver the
timer value to the sequencer channel during the CPU-bound event cascade,
even though the callback was invoked between every event.

empty throughout, but wall clock had passed the seal deadline long before.

Replace the channel peek with a direct time.Now() comparison against the
sequencer's next-action deadline. time.Now() reads the monotonic clock
directly and does not depend on runtime goroutine scheduling or timer
channel delivery.

Also: when DrainUntil is interrupted, run the sequencer action directly
rather than deferring to the main select loop, because:
  - The timer channel may still not have a value
  - planSequencerAction would see nextAction == prevTime and skip
    resetting the timer

Add an Info log when the interrupt path fires, so operators can see
when starvation is being avoided.

Verified on production test sequencer: seal now happens within 50ms of
the deadline even during 4000-block span batch consolidations.

fix(op-node): prevent hot-loop interrupting on stuck sequencer deadline

When RunAction cannot advance nextAction (e.g. stuck waiting for a
ForkchoiceUpdateEvent to set latestHead), the deadline stays in the
past. Without a guard, every subsequent DrainUntil would interrupt
again on the same deadline, call RunAction, which re-emits
RequestForkchoiceUpdate — filling the event queue until it panics
with the 10000-event sanity limit.

Track the last deadline we interrupted on and skip interrupting
again on the same deadline. If RunAction doesn't advance it, let
normal event processing handle the state change.

Also remove drain_interrupt_test.go — the tests covered the
len(ch) > 0 peek pattern we replaced with time.Now(), so they don't
exercise any mechanism we now rely on. The existing
TestDrainUntilCancel / TestDrainUntilExcl already cover DrainUntil
mechanics.

Verified locally: TestChallengerResponseDelay/NoDelay and
TestOutputAlphabetGame_ChallengerWins pass with the fix.

* fix(flashblocks): wait for builder P2P sync during rapid block driving

When driveViaTestSequencer builds blocks rapidly, the sequencer EL
produces blocks faster than P2P can propagate them to the builder EL
(op-rbuilder). Under CI load, the builder receives an FCU referencing
a parent block it hasn't synced yet, causing "missing parent header" →

has synced the block before driving the next one. This also benefits

test(contracts): skip VerifyOPCM_Run_Test on coverage only, not unoptimized (#20143)

* fix(contracts): skip ZKDisputeGame in VerifyOPCM when feature disabled

#19685 added zkDisputeGameImpl to VerifyOPCM's implementations map but
forgot the corresponding skip path for when DEV_FEATURE__ZK_DISPUTE_GAME
is off. OPCM returns address(0) for zkDisputeGameImpl in that case, so
VerifyOPCM treats the 0-byte deployed code vs 13.5KB expected artifact
as a verification failure.

This broke contracts-bedrock-tests-develop on every matrix cell that
doesn't set ZK_DISPUTE_GAME (11 of 12), but wasn't caught at merge time
because the -develop job runs post-merge only and isn't in
required-contracts-ci.

Three tests were failing on develop for the same root cause:
- test_run_succeeds — VerifyOPCM_Failed, ZK ref mismatches artifact
- test_run_implementationDifferentInsideImmutable_succeeds — same
- test_run_implementationDifferentOutsideImmutable_reverts — panic 0x11
  (vm.randomUint(0, implCode.length - 1) underflows when ZK ref's code
  is empty)

Fix mirrors the existing SuperDisputeGame skip path:
- VerifyOPCM.s.sol: skip-or-fail branch inside _verifyOpcmContractRef
  plus _isZKDisputeGameEnabled / _isZKDisputeGameImplementation helpers.
- VerifyOPCM.t.sol: skip the ZK ref in the byte-scramble loops when
  the feature is off so implCode.length == 0 doesn't underflow, and
  unconditionally skip ZK in test_runSingle_succeeds (mirrors the
  existing super-games skip with TODO).

* test(contracts): skip VerifyOPCM_Run_Test on coverage only, not unoptimized

These three tests compare a locally-compiled deployed address to a
locally-compiled artifact on disk. Both sides come from the same build,
so the comparison holds under any Foundry profile. Coverage mode does
break it (the coverage run instruments the deployed code but not the
on-disk artifact), but an unoptimized profile like liteci does not.

#19332 mechanically renamed every skipIfCoverage() → skipIfUnoptimized()
in this file while introducing the liteci profile. That over-broadened
the skip: on PRs we now run liteci via contracts-bedrock-tests, and
VerifyOPCM_Run_Test short-circuits there, so the script's correctness
is only exercised post-merge by contracts-bedrock-tests-develop. That
is how the ZK-dispute-game skip miss from #19685 slipped past merge
and landed red on develop.

Reintroduce skipIfCoverage() as a distinct helper and apply it to the
three tests whose only real compiler-output dependency is coverage
instrumentation:
- test_run_succeeds
- test_run_implementationDifferentInsideImmutable_succeeds
- test_run_implementationDifferentOutsideImmutable_reverts

The other skipIfUnoptimized() uses in this file are left alone — some
of them genuinely depend on optimized bytecode (e.g. immutable-variable
tests, preimage-oracle checks with fixed selectors) and are worth
auditing separately if/when someone wants to widen the PR coverage.

Stacked on fix/verifyopcm-zk-dispute-skip so the PR-level liteci run
doesn't go red on non-ZK matrix cells; land that one first.

fix(op-node,op-batcher): fix maxSafeLag stall, resume, and channel timeout

The `--sequencer.max-safe-lag` feature was effectively non-functional due to
a state-management bug in the sequencer, compounded by a missing timeout
re-check in the batcher.

## Root Cause (op-node)

In `onForkchoiceUpdate`, the maxSafeLag check ran **before** the head-advancement
block. When a new block was confirmed (`UnsafeL2Head > latestHead`), the
head-advancement block unconditionally set `nextActionOK = true`, immediately
overriding the `nextActionOK = false` set by the maxSafeLag check. The sequencer
continued producing blocks regardless of the safe-head lag.

## Fix (op-node)

Move the maxSafeLag check to **after** the head-advancement block so it can
properly override `nextActionOK = true`. Additionally:

- **Stall/resume tracking**: Introduce a `stalledByMaxSafeLag` flag so the
  recovery branch only resumes sequencing when the stall was caused by
  maxSafeLag specifically. Without this, the resume logic would interfere with
  other `nextActionOK = false` states (pipeline reset, L1-derivation backoff,
  mid-seal wait).

- **Safe head catch-up recovery**: When the safe head catches up (gap drops
  below maxSafeLag), the sequencer automatically resumes via the
  `else if d.stalledByMaxSafeLag` branch. Uses `d.active.Load()` to match the
  resume pattern used throughout the file.

- **Runtime disable**: If an operator sets `maxSafeLag = 0` while the sequencer
  is stalled, the outer `else if d.stalledByMaxSafeLag` branch detects this and
  resumes immediately, preventing a permanent stall.

- **Lifecycle cleanup**: `stalledByMaxSafeLag` is cleared in `forceStart`,
  `onReset`, and `Stop` to prevent stale state across lifecycle transitions.

## Root Cause (op-batcher)

When the sequencer stalls and stops producing blocks, the batcher quickly
consumes all pending blocks into a channel (`pendingBlocks = 0`). In
`getReadyChannel`, the `pendingBlocks() == 0` early-return path skips
`registerL1Block()` — the only call site that checks channel duration timeout.
The channel never times out, never closes, and the data is never submitted to
L1, leaving the safe head permanently stuck.

## Fix (op-batcher)

When `pendingBlocks == 0` but a non-full channel exists, still call
`registerL1Block()` to re-evaluate the channel duration timeout. If the channel
times out, flush it immediately. Respects the `ignoreMaxChannelDuration` flag
for consistency with the normal path.

## Scenarios Covered

| Scenario | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| Gap exceeds maxSafeLag | Sequencer stalls, stops producing blocks |
| Safe head catches up | Sequencer auto-resumes |
| Batcher running, sequencer stalled | Channel times out via batcher fix, data submitted, safe head advances |
| Batcher restarted during stall | New channel created, data submitted quickly |
| maxSafeLag disabled at runtime | Sequencer resumes immediately |
| Pipeline reset during stall | Flag cleared, reset proceeds normally |
| Conductor failover | forceStart clears flag, new leader starts clean |

Fixes ethereum-optimism/optimism#17936

fix(op-supernode): address review must-fix items for backfill

Four data/lifecycle issues spotted while reviewing #19973 that block
running this package under -race and that are latent panic/corruption
sources under stress.

1) Race on Interop.runtimeActivationTimestamp.
   The field is written by runLogBackfill (log_backfill.go) and read
   by observeRound, buildRewindPlan, verifyCanAddTimestamp, and the
   RuntimeActivationTimestamp test accessor. Sibling lifecycle fields
   (backfillAttempts, backfillCompleted, pauseAtTimestamp) were already
   atomic for exactly this reason; this one was missed. Any test that
   reads the accessor from a different goroutine than Start's backfill
   loop trips -race even though the semantic hand-off (backfill ends,
   then main loop runs) is otherwise safe.

   Fix: promote runtimeActivationTimestamp to atomic.Uint64 and update
   all five read sites plus the two write sites. Struct-literal test
   initialisations switch to .Store() after construction.

2) Race between Stop and in-flight backfill DB writes.
   Stop called i.cancel() and then immediately iterated i.logsDBs
   closing each entry. The backfill hot path (backfillChain ->
   sealBlockDataIntoLogsDB -> processBlockLogs) does not check i.ctx
   between chain.FetchReceipts and the subsequent db.SealBlock /
   db.AddLog calls, and logs.DB.Close does not acquire db.rwLock,
   so a Stop that arrives between "FetchReceipts returned" and
   "SealBlock flushed" would close the append-only store file out
   from under the writer.

   Fix: add i.done (closed by Start's defer) and have Stop wait on it,
   bounded by the caller's ctx, before closing any DBs. If Start never
   ran, done is nil and we skip the wait — preserving the "Stop before
   Start" no-op semantics.

3) Stop double-close.
   The pre-existing Stop closed only verifiedDB; this PR expanded it
   to close every logs.DB. A repeat Stop call therefore invoked Close
   on already-closed stores, which is neither idempotent nor
   panic-free on the underlying store.

   Fix: wrap the close loop in i.closeOnce (sync.Once). First Stop
   closes; subsequent Stops return the same first-error without
   touching the handles again.

4) Race on package-level errorBackoffPeriod / backoffPeriod.
   The two new retry-path tests (TestLogBackfill_RetriesWhenVirtualNodes
   NotReady and TestLogBackfill_RetriesStopOnContextCancel) each
   temporarily shrank the package-level errorBackoffPeriod to 10ms
   and restored it via t.Cleanup. When both ran in the same test
   binary, the Start goroutine of one test read the var while the
   other test's body or cleanup wrote it, producing the data race
   that makes the whole package fail under `go test -race`.

   Fix: remove the package vars, keep only defaultBackoffPeriod /
   defaultErrorBackoffPeriod constants, and seed two new instance
   fields (i.backoffPeriod, i.errorBackoffPeriod) in New. Tests
   mutate the instance field directly and no longer need Cleanup —
   scoped to the Interop that owns the Start goroutine.

Verified with `go test ./op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/
-race -count=3` — clean. Also verified the underlying store race is
real: logs.DB.Close (supervisor/backend/db/logs/db.go:660) calls
db.store.Close() without taking db.rwLock, while SealBlock /
AddLog take db.rwLock but delegate to db.store inside the lock.

fix(op-supernode): address review should-fix items for backfill

Four correctness-degrading behaviours and a batch of stale comments
flagged in the #19973 review. Each is independently shippable; grouped
here because they all tighten the edges of the backfill retry/resume
machinery.

1) Terminal error classification: ErrChainBehindBackfillLowerBound.
   The error's docstring says "Operator remediation is to clear the
   logs DBs and restart" — it is terminal, not transient. The previous
   retry loop treated every error as transient and spun every 2 s with
   "virtual nodes may not be ready yet", drowning logs and hiding the
   real action item.

   Fix: errors.Is check before the warn/sleep path. Returns with a
   wrapped error that restates the operator remediation inline, so
   the first log line the operator sees points at the right fix.

2) Silent coverage gap when logBackfillDepth grows across restarts.
   backfillChain unconditionally bumped startNum to latest.Number+1
   whenever the DB had blocks. If an operator raised logBackfillDepth
   between runs, the new T_lo mapped to a smaller block number — but
   the DB still started at the old (higher) virtual parent, and the
   bump skipped over the [new_T_lo_block, old_first_sealed) range
   without any log. logs.DB is append-only, so we cannot retroactively
   fill that range; the best we can do is surface it.

   Fix: before the startNum bump, compare FirstSealedBlock against
   the requested startNum. When the DB starts above T_lo, emit a Warn
   naming the chain, the first sealed block, the requested start,
   the gap size, and the remediation (clear data dir). The Warn is
   deliberate — not an error — so operators who know about the gap
   and don't care can ignore it.

3) Sub-second logBackfillDepth silently truncates to zero.
   LogBackfillLowerBound divides `depth / time.Second` (floor). A
   value like 500 ms produced sub = 0 and therefore T_lo = crossSafeTs,
   effectively no-op'ing backfill. The > 0 checks elsewhere wrongly
   reported that backfill "ran" — tests and operators both saw a
   green signal with zero work done.

   Fix: reject 0 < depth < 1s in CLIConfig.Check with an explicit
   error message that names the floor-to-zero behaviour, so operators
   see the problem at config time instead of in a silent no-op.

4) Leaked timers and uncancellable sleeps in the Start loop.
   `case <-time.After(i.errorBackoffPeriod):` inside a select with
   <-i.ctx.Done() leaks a live timer when the ctx wins the race.
   The main loop's `time.Sleep(i.errorBackoffPeriod)` / `time.Sleep
   (i.backoffPeriod)` cannot be cancelled at all — if ctx cancels
   during a sleep, we sleep out the full duration before noticing.

   Fix: replace both with clock.SystemClock.SleepCtx(ctx, d), which
   returns ctx.Err() on cancel and doesn't leave a timer pending. The
   retry-loop site also returns the wrapped error immediately so the
   caller's ctx propagates cleanly.

5) Stale comments.
   - logdb.go:126: isBackfill doc said "allow any ts >= activation";
     after the 1f813c4d7c misalignment fix the relaxation is
     "ts + blockTime > activation". Replaced with a doc that
     describes the actual anchor-window semantics.
   - logdb.go:236: processBlockLogs said the first block is "at
     activation timestamp"; with backfill it can be up to one
     blockTime before activation. Replaced with an accurate range.
   - acceptance/backfill/testutil.go, happy/happy_test.go: both
     referenced the retry-path sibling package that was deleted in
     commit 4c7f8e9764. Updated wording to describe the
     current (happy-only) layout.

chore(op-supernode): review nits — tighter backfill test coverage

Three targeted test additions/tightenings that turn previously-untested
code paths into regression-proof ones. No production code changes.

1) Config: zero, sub-second, and one-second-boundary cases.
   op-supernode/config/config_test.go:10 table only covered
   positive-with-activation, positive-without-activation, and negative.
   The "zero disables" default (touched on every startup that doesn't
   set the flag), the new sub-second rejection (from the should-fix
   commit in this series), and the exact 1s boundary were all
   uncovered. Regressions in any of these would have slipped through:
     - zero rejected -> every operator who doesn't set depth fails
       startup,
     - sub-second accepted -> silent no-op with backfill "enabled",
     - 1s rejected -> tightens the minimum past what operators can
       realistically set.
   Three new table rows pin each.

2) Flaky sleep -> Eventually in TestLogBackfill_RetriesStopOnContextCancel.
   The old test raw-slept 100ms between Start and cancel and asserted
   only that Start returned context.Canceled. On a loaded CI box the
   Start goroutine may not have entered the retry loop yet, so the
   test claimed to exercise "retries stop on cancel" while actually
   only exercising "cancel returns". Replaced with require.Eventually
   gated on backfillAttempts >= 2, so the retry path is demonstrably
   running before the cancel fires. Flake window shrinks from ~100ms
   to ~5ms polling.

3) Missing coverage of runtimeActivationTimestamp vs activationTimestamp.
   TestVerifyPreviousTimestampSealed sets activationTS and
   runtimeActivationTimestamp to the same value in every row, so the
   new split introduced by log backfill was untested: a regression
   that read activationTimestamp in the main-loop branch (instead of
   runtimeActivationTimestamp) would have passed the existing suite.

   Added TestVerifyCanAddTimestamp_RuntimeVsProtocolActivation with
   five cases that force the two fields apart (protocol=1000,
   runtime=1200) and exercise:
     - main-loop empty DB at runtime succeeds,
     - main-loop empty DB at protocol fails (catches the swap bug),
     - backfill empty DB at (activation - blockTime + 1) succeeds
       (the pairing anchor window),
     - backfill empty DB at activation succeeds,
     - backfill empty DB at (activation - blockTime) fails (the
       strict > boundary of the anchor window).

feat(op-alloy): add post-exec (0x7D) transaction type

Introduce the synthetic post-execution transaction envelope that will
carry block-scoped post-exec data appended by op-reth when it produces
a block.

- POST_EXEC_TX_TYPE_ID = 0x7D, POST_EXEC_PAYLOAD_VERSION = 1.
- PostExecPayload { version, block_number, gas_refund_entries }.
  Decode paths (Decodable2718::{typed_decode, fallback_decode},
  Decodable::decode, from_rlp_bytes) all funnel through
  decode_checked, which rejects unknown versions and trailing bytes.
- TxPostExec wraps the payload with EIP-2718 encoding, a canonical
  zero signature, and a zero signer address.
- OpTxEnvelope gains a PostExec variant with RPC-shaped serde so
  consumers decoding full transaction objects see the canonical input
  bytes.
- SDMGasEntry is the single refund-entry payload field today; the
  payload is intentionally open to additional post-exec fields later.
- Arbitrary impl pins `version = POST_EXEC_PAYLOAD_VERSION` so
  encode/decode roundtrip tests don't produce payloads that
  decode_checked would reject.

feat(alloy-op-evm): post-exec block executor and SDM warming inspector

Add the canonical post-exec block executor, along with the first
feature riding on it — SDM (Sequencer-Defined Metering) block-level
warming refunds, delivered by the SDMWarmingInspector.

- OpBlockExecutor gains three PostExecModes (Disabled / Produce /
  Verify(payload) / Invalid). Produce accumulates per-tx refund
  entries for the payload builder to append as a synthetic 0x7D tx;
  Verify validates an embedded payload against local replay;
  Disabled is the legacy path (byte-identical to pre-SDM).
- SDMWarmingInspector tracks first-warmer provenance for accounts
  and storage slots, emits exact refund attribution events for every
  re-touch past the EIP-2929 warm threshold, and suppresses claims
  from Deposit and synthetic PostExec tx kinds.
- Verify-mode validations reject duplicate payload indexes, payload
  entries targeting deposits or the 0x7D tx itself, and refunds that
  exceed the tx's raw gas. `apply_pre_execution_changes` debug_asserts
  the Produce hooks are wired so a downstream fork can't silently drop
  refunds.
- Canonical gas settlement credits the sender, debits the beneficiary
  and base-fee recipient by the refunded-gas component of their share,
  and commits the deltas when canonical gas falls below raw gas.
- beneficiary_gas_price can legitimately saturate at zero when a
  legacy tx's gas price equals basefee; inline comment documents the
  consensus-valid zero case.

feat(op-reth): add ConfigurePostExecEvm and post-exec-aware evm config

Extend op-reth's EvmConfig with the post-exec hooks the new
OpBlockExecutor expects. Downstream uses:

  entries via post_exec_executor_for_block + take_post_exec_entries.
- The replay RPC asks for the same Produce mode but on a stripped

feat(op-reth): add debug_replaySDMBlock rpc and post-exec-replay crate

Introduce reth-optimism-post-exec-replay, a new crate that counterfactually
re-executes a historical block under PostExecMode::Produce to derive what
the post-exec payload *would* have been, then compares it to any 0x7D tx
already embedded in the block and to the receipt-level opGasRefund
projection.

- debug_replaySDMBlock JSON-RPC handler exposes the replay result on a
  per-block basis. Compares synthesized refunds vs. embedded payload and
  vs. receipt refunds when requested. Documented as operator/debug
  tooling only — the debug namespace must not be exposed on public RPC,
  each call replays a whole historical block against live state and is
  unbounded in cost.
- Replay detects seven mismatch categories: duplicate payload index,
  payload-index-out-of-range, payload-targets-deposit,
  payload-targets-post-exec, payload-refund-mismatch,
  receipt-refund-mismatch, payload-refund-exceeds-raw-gas.
- strip_post_exec_tx_for_replay preserves the original tx index mapping
  so refund events can be attributed back to source-block positions.
- Semaphore::new(3) caps concurrent replays; per-call wall-clock and
  memory ceilings are a production-hardening gap tracked separately.

fix(kona): apply corrected MIPS64 target spec to offline-cannon build path

The cannon-builder:v1.0.0 Docker image ships with a MIPS64 target spec
that has target-c-int-width=64. The correct n64 ABI value is 32, and the
wrong value caused LLVM to miscompile str equality comparisons — the
branch on the memcmp return was eliminated, making str == str always
return false. Fixed upstream in commit 04ab310dc6 for the reproducible
prestate path, but kona-host-client-offline-cannon goes through
rust/kona/justfile's build-cannon-client and lint-cannon recipes which
invoke the baked image directly and never picked up the corrected spec.

Mount the already-corrected spec from rust/kona/docker/cannon/ over
/mips64-unknown-none.json inside the container so cargo resolves it
instead of the broken baked-in file. Same mechanism cannon-repro.dockerfile
uses at its COPY step, adapted for docker run.

fix(flashblocks): allow same block_number across payload_ids in stream test

TestFlashblocksStream asserted that within a single `block_number` the
flashblock `index` monotonically increased, but that is not the actual
invariant emitted by op-rbuilder / rollup-boost. A flashblock sequence
is identified by `payload_id`, not by `block_number`, and when the
sequencer rebuilds a block (new `payload_id` for the same
`block_number`) the stream starts a fresh sequence at `index=0` — the
rbuilder implementation explicitly documents that "a FlashBlock with
index 0 resets the set" (see
rust/op-reth/crates/flashblocks/src/sequence.rs).

Under CI load on the op-reth matrix, the sequencer frequently rebuilds
blocks during the startup catch-up phase (the logs show "FCU arrived
too late" and "Payload ID mismatch" errors while L2 time catches up
to wall-clock time), producing streams like
`(block=3, payload=A, idx=0..2)` followed by
`(block=3, payload=B, idx=0..k)`. The old test saw
`idx=1 → idx=0` on the same block number and failed with
`"0" is not greater than "1"`. Because rebuilds only happen when
block building races with the sequencer, the failure is timing-
dependent and only shows up as a flake — and mostly on the op-reth
matrix, which has slightly different payload propagation pacing
than op-geth.

This change rewrites the assertion to validate the real invariant:

  - A flashblock at `index=0` starts a new sequence (identified by
    `payload_id`).
  - Within a sequence, `block_number` is stable and `index` strictly
    increases.
  - Across sequences, `block_number` never decreases and the first
    index is always 0.

The test also now anchors on the first observed `index=0` flashblock
rather than requiring the very first message to be at index 0: the
websocket is opened eagerly during devstack setup, so the test may
start reading mid-sequence. Waiting for a clean anchor removes that
class of startup race without introducing any sleeps.

Fixes ethereum-optimism/optimism#19883

(40 sequential) and `go test -count=10 -parallel 4` (40 concurrent
across both flashblocks tests) — all 40+40 passed. Also ran with
`-race -count=2` to confirm no new data races.

fix(flashblocks): size flashblock client buffer for 30s of CI headroom

The previous buffer of numFlashblocks*2 (40 slots ≈ 8 s at the 200 ms
flashblock cadence defined in
rust/op-reth/crates/flashblocks/src/cache.rs) is too tight for CI.
Under load the test goroutine can be stalled for several seconds while
op-rbuilder, rollup-boost and the sequencer contend for CPU, and if
the channel fills the FlashblockClient drops messages (see the
"channel full, dropping flashblock" path in flashblock_client.go).
Dropped messages defeat the anchor+validate strategy introduced in
the previous commit by leaving gaps in the stream.

Grow the buffer to 150 slots (≈ 30 s at 200 ms cadence) — comfortable
headroom for realistic CI stalls, and still a trivial amount of
memory. Keep numFlashblocks = 20 unchanged: we still only validate
20 transitions, we just have more room to absorb bursts before the
consumer catches up.

  NIGHTLY := `grep -oE 'nightly-...' ../mise.toml | head -1`

exist, so NIGHTLY evaluated to an empty string.

../mise.toml resolves to /workdir/mise.toml — the monorepo mise.toml that
actually contains the nightly pin.

fix(kona): conditionally deploy `CrossL2Inbox` and dep set introduction  (#20147)

* Fixes #19311 (state divergence between `kona-node` and `op-node` on
single-chain Interop activation).

op-node emits 7 always-on Interop predeploy txs and 2 gated
`CrossL2Inbox` txs (gated on `len(depSet.Chains()) > 1`). kona-node was
emitting all 9 unconditionally, so single-chain deployments injected 2
extra deposit txs → divergent post-state from the first Interop block.

Go reference: `op-node/rollup/derive/interop_upgrade_transactions.go`
(split) + `attributes.go:178` (the gate).

This PR adds a new CLI flag on `kona-node`:

--interop.dependency-set      [env: KONA_NODE_INTEROP_DEPENDENCY_SET]

**You must supply this flag on any chain whose rollup config has
`interop_time` set.** The node will refuse to start otherwise, with a
clear error:

> Interop is scheduled for this chain (interop_time = Some(...)), but
> `--interop.dependency-set` was not provided. Supply the dependency-set
> JSON file matching op-node's `--interop.dependency-set` to avoid
> silent state divergence on interop activation.

Pre-interop chains (`interop_time = None`) are unaffected — the flag is
optional.

**Parity with op-node:** the flag name matches `op-node`'s
`--interop.dependency-set`, and the JSON schema is the same
(`kona-interop::DependencySet`). The env var name is
`KONA_NODE_INTEROP_DEPENDENCY_SET` rather than `OP_NODE_…` (different
binary).

  `Interop::cross_l2_inbox_deposits()` is a separate path for the 2
  gated txs.

  gates the CrossL2Inbox pair on `dependencies.len() > 1`, matching
  op-node's `attributes.go:178`.
- Constructor panics if

  divergence becomes a startup crash.

* fix(op-supernode): fail backfill when a chain is behind T_lo

runLogBackfill previously computed minLocalSafeTime over every chain,
including ones whose local-safe was behind T_lo in block space and
therefore got silently skipped by the "startNum > localSafeNum" branch.
After backfill, runtimeActivationTimestamp = minLocalSafeTime + 1; the
main loop then advanced past the unbackfilled range on the skipped
chain, leaving its [T_lo, minLocalSafeTime] logs unsealed. Any future
executing message that referenced an initiating message in that range
would be unverifiable.

By the supernode's own invariants (minCrossSafeTime <= every chain's
localSafeTime, and T_lo <= minCrossSafeTime) the skip branch is
unreachable in steady state; hitting it means SyncStatus and
TimestampToBlockNumber disagreed (chain still warming up, derivation
indexing lag, etc.). The right response is to fail the round and let
the retry loop re-query once the inconsistency resolves, rather than
silently lose logs.

Replace the skip branch with a fail-fast error that names the chain
and both block numbers. Fold localSafeTime into minLocalSafeTime only
after the consistency check, so the runtime-activation advancement
always reflects the set of chains whose logs DB is now populated up
to T_lo.

Rewrite TestLogBackfill_AsymmetricMultiChain as a healthy three-chain
case with asymmetric cross-safe and local-safe positions, and add
TestLogBackfill_FailsWhenChainBehindTLo to pin the new safety property.

fix(op-supernode): fall back to local-safe/finalized before interop activation (#20191)

Before this fix, super_authority.FullyVerifiedL2Head and FinalizedL2Head
returned (empty, false) whenever the interop verifier was registered but
had no entries in its verifiedDB. op-node's engine controller treats
(empty, false) as "verifier present, no answer" and resolves to genesis,
pinning SafeL2 and FinalizedL2 at block 0 until activation — while
LocalSafe continued to advance normally. Any network with interop
scheduled in the future saw this as a user-visible stall.

Both methods now consult VerificationActivity.IsActiveAt(ss.LocalSafeL2.Time)
before querying verifier state. When every registered verifier reports
inactive at the local-safe timestamp, they return (empty, true) so the
engine controller falls back to local-safe / local-finalized.

Using LocalSafeL2.Time for both heads is sound because FinalizedL2 <=
LocalSafeL2: if local-safe is still pre-activation, finalized is too.
Once a local-safe block crosses activation, the verifier-gated path
resumes.

Flips the 4 RED unit tests added in the previous commit to GREEN and
(by induction from the same root cause) TestPreNoInbox's CrossSafe /

fix(op-supernode): close interop activation gap in verified-head fallback (#20191)

Addresses the residual activation-gap flagged by wwared on #20215. The
previous fix (116dd19de6) handled the pure pre-activation stall by
short-circuiting super_authority to local-safe when every registered
verifier reports !IsActiveAt(LocalSafeL2.Time). That leaves a
transitional window once LocalSafeL2.Time crosses activationTimestamp
but before the interop verifier commits its first verifiedDB entry:
IsActiveAt is true, the fast-path no longer triggers, and
LatestVerifiedL2Block / VerifiedBlockAtL1 return (empty, 0). op-node's
engine controller treats (empty, false) from super_authority as "no
answer" and resolves to genesis, so SafeL2 and FinalizedL2 snap from a
growing local-safe head back to block 0 for the duration of the gap.

Fix the asymmetry at its root. Interop.VerifiedAtTimestamp is already
pre-activation-aware (returns true for ts < activationTimestamp);
LatestVerifiedL2Block and VerifiedBlockAtL1 were not. Both now fall
through to the chain's pre-activation boundary block (the L2 block at
activationTimestamp-1, verified by consensus alone) whenever verifiedDB
is empty. For the finalized head, the boundary is only surfaced when
its L1 inclusion is at or below the supplied L1 block — finalization
remains strictly L1-gated.

Post-fix behaviour across the activation spectrum:
- Pre-activation: verifiedDB empty, boundary ≈ latest local-safe →
  super_authority's IsActiveAt fast-path still short-circuits first
  (no L2 lookup); SafeL2 tracks LocalSafe unchanged.
- Activation gap: verifiedDB empty, boundary = last pre-activation
  block → SafeL2 sits at the boundary until the verifier catches up.
  No regression to genesis.
- Steady state: verifiedDB non-empty → behaviour unchanged.

The boundary lookup uses ChainContainer.OptimisticAt(activationTs-1)
and is recomputed on every call (no caching); lookup failures fall
back to (empty, 0) so the existing pre-activation IsActiveAt fast-path
still guards the common case without an L2 RPC.

Rejected the alternative of loosening EngineController's (empty, false)
branch to fall through to localSafeHead: post-activation, localSafeHead
contains blocks the interop verifier has not yet cross-verified and
could still invalidate; that would overpromise safety. The conservative
(empty, false) → genesis behaviour remains correct for its original
scenario.

Tests:
- op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop: new TestLatestVerifiedL2Block
  (5 subtests) and 4 new TestVerifiedBlockAtL1 subtests covering
  boundary-returned, boundary-L1-gated-by-finalizedL1, activation=0,
  unknown-chain, lookup-fails, and verifiedDB-non-empty-preserved.
- op-acceptance-tests: new TestActivationGap boots the devstack with a
  60s activation delay, snapshots SafeL2/FinalizedL2 pre-activation,
  awaits activation on both chains, then polls optimism_syncStatus at
  1Hz for 60s asserting neither head regresses below its pre-activation
  value — a direct end-to-end reproduction of the gap. Follows the
  TestPreNoInbox policy of landing alongside the fix without running
  locally.

super_authority_test.go is unchanged: the contract at that layer is
unchanged (pass-through of whatever the verifier returns). The existing
B1b / B2b "empty verifier → no fallback" cases still hold at the
authority layer; the semantic shift lives inside the Interop verifier,
which is where the pre-activation asymmetry originated.

feat(alloy-op-evm): post-exec block executor and SDM warming inspector

Add the canonical post-exec block executor, along with the first
feature riding on it — SDM (Sequencer-Defined Metering) block-level
warming refunds, delivered by the SDMWarmingInspector.

- OpBlockExecutor gains three PostExecModes (Disabled / Produce /
  Verify(payload) / Invalid). Produce accumulates per-tx refund
  entries for the payload builder to append as a synthetic 0x7D tx;
  Verify validates an embedded payload against local replay;
  Disabled is the legacy path (byte-identical to pre-SDM).
- SDMWarmingInspector tracks first-warmer provenance for accounts
  and storage slots, emits exact refund attribution events for every
  re-touch past the EIP-2929 warm threshold, and suppresses claims
  from Deposit and synthetic PostExec tx kinds.
- Verify-mode validations reject duplicate payload indexes, payload
  entries targeting deposits or the 0x7D tx itself, and refunds that
  exceed the tx's raw gas. `apply_pre_execution_changes` debug_asserts
  the Produce hooks are wired so a downstream fork can't silently drop
  refunds.
- Canonical gas settlement credits the sender, debits the beneficiary
  and base-fee recipient by the refunded-gas component of their share,
  and commits the deltas when canonical gas falls below raw gas.
- beneficiary_gas_price can legitimately saturate at zero when a
  legacy tx's gas price equals basefee; inline comment documents the
  consensus-valid zero case.

fix(op-supernode): guard chain container vn against torn interface read

Supernode.Start fires the Interop activity and chain-container goroutines
in parallel. Interop's checkChainsReady immediately calls c.OptimisticAt ->
c.SyncStatus, which reads c.vn while the chain container is concurrently
assigning it in its restart loop. A torn two-word interface read can yield
(type=*simpleVirtualNode, data=nil); the `c.vn == nil` guard returns false,
the method dispatches on a nil receiver, and v.mu.Lock() panics at offset
0x58 (the mu field inside simpleVirtualNode).

Protect c.vn with a sync.RWMutex and route all reads/writes through
getVN/setVN helpers so every method takes one consistent snapshot. Also
add nil-receiver guards on the *simpleVirtualNode methods as a defense
against typed-nil interfaces slipping through in tests or future refactors.

fix(op-acceptance-tests): stabilize TestReorgUnsafeHead

Before re-enabling op-node sequencing, wait for the CL's sync status to
reflect the test-sequencer's final committed unsafe head instead of
relying on a pair of 2-second sleeps.

The EL's unsafe head is updated synchronously by CommitBlock (engine
NewPayload + engine forkchoice update), but the op-node's StatusTracker
and Sequencer.latestHead are updated asynchronously via the event loop
when it drains the ForkchoiceUpdateEvent. Under CI load the 2s sleeps
were occasionally too short: StartSequencer read a stale LocalUnsafe
from SyncStatus, passed that stale hash to Sequencer.Start (which
validated it against its equally-stale latestHead), forceStart flipped
the sequencer active, and startBuildingBlock used the stale latestHead
as the parent for the next block -- silently reorging the EL off the
test-sequencer's conflicting fork and causing the assertion at line 114
to see identical hashes.

Note on the test job: despite the CI label "memory-all-kona-op-reth",
this test runs against op-node (the supernode preset hardcodes op-node
and the test-sequencer's opstack_commitBlockV1 RPC is only implemented
by op-node). kona-node tests in the same binary use a different preset.

The fix polls SyncStatus().UnsafeL2.Hash until it matches the EL's
current unsafe head. Within a single event-loop dispatch the handlers
run sequentially, so StatusTracker and Sequencer.OnEvent can complete
out of order; but by the time SyncStatus reports the expected hash,
either (a) the sequencer has already processed the same
ForkchoiceUpdateEvent, or (b) when it does, Sequencer.Start's internal
mutex serialises Start against OnEvent, so StartSequencer either
observes the fresh latestHead or fails fast with a visible "block hash
does not match" error rather than silently reorging. In the worst case
the poll times out with a clear message, replacing a silent failure
with an explicit one.

Refs ethereum-optimism/optimism#20198

fix(op-acceptance-tests): stabilize TestUnsafeGapFillAfterUnsafeReorg_RestartL2CL

ReorgTriggered only waits until the block at the reorg-target height has
been rewritten on the sequencer; it does not wait for the sequencer to
rebuild past the verifier's frozen unsafe head. The test then asserts
seq.Number > ver.Number, which races against the sequencer producing the
next block after the reorg. In failing CI (op-geth, pipeline 123064, job
4866963) both heads were observed at 18 because the sequencer had
reorged and rebuilt exactly up to the verifier's frozen height but had
not yet extended past it.

Capture the verifier's unsafe head immediately after stopping L2CLB (at
which point the verifier cannot advance — its CL is down and the preset
has NoDiscovery), then after ReorgTriggered returns wait for the
sequencer to reach verFrozen.Number + 1 before sampling the heads for
the assertion. This makes the seq > ver ordering structurally guaranteed
rather than racing with post-reorg block production.

Refs: ethereum-optimism/optimism#19936

fix(op-acceptance-tests): widen Matched budget on initial sync in UnsafeGapFillAfterUnsafeReorg_RestartL2CL

The two pre-reorg Matched calls used only 5 attempts (~10s). This assumes
the verifier is already in lockstep with the sequencer, which breaks when
the verifier starts late relative to the sequencer and has to catch up
tens of blocks — e.g. slow op-reth cold start or a gossipsub mesh that
takes time to form under CI contention. When this happens the sequencer
produces a burst of blocks to catch up to wall-clock genesis time, leaving
the verifier well behind. 10s is not enough to close that gap via gossip.

Bump both Matched budgets to 30 attempts (60s) — consistent with the
existing post-stop gap-close budget of 50 attempts — so the verifier can
finish catching up before the test perturbs the system. The happy path
still returns on first success, so fast runs are unaffected.

fix(flashblocks): allow same block_number across payload_ids in stream test

TestFlashblocksStream asserted that within a single `block_number` the
flashblock `index` monotonically increased, but that is not the actual
invariant emitted by op-rbuilder / rollup-boost. A flashblock sequence
is identified by `payload_id`, not by `block_number`, and when the
sequencer rebuilds a block (new `payload_id` for the same
`block_number`) the stream starts a fresh sequence at `index=0` — the
rbuilder implementation explicitly documents that "a FlashBlock with
index 0 resets the set" (see
rust/op-reth/crates/flashblocks/src/sequence.rs).

Under CI load on the op-reth matrix, the sequencer frequently rebuilds
blocks during the startup catch-up phase (the logs show "FCU arrived
too late" and "Payload ID mismatch" errors while L2 time catches up
to wall-clock time), producing streams like
`(block=3, payload=A, idx=0..2)` followed by
`(block=3, payload=B, idx=0..k)`. The old test saw
`idx=1 → idx=0` on the same block number and failed with
`"0" is not greater than "1"`. Because rebuilds only happen when
block building races with the sequencer, the failure is timing-
dependent and only shows up as a flake — and mostly on the op-reth
matrix, which has slightly different payload propagation pacing
than op-geth.

This change rewrites the assertion to validate the real invariant:

  - A flashblock at `index=0` starts a new sequence (identified by
    `payload_id`).
  - Within a sequence, `block_number` is stable and `index` strictly
    increases.
  - Across sequences, `block_number` never decreases and the first
    index is always 0.

The test also now anchors on the first observed `index=0` flashblock
rather than requiring the very first message to be at index 0: the
websocket is opened eagerly during devstack setup, so the test may
start reading mid-sequence. Waiting for a clean anchor removes that
class of startup race without introducing any sleeps.

Fixes ethereum-optimism/optimism#19883

Local verification: ran `go test -count=40 -run TestFlashblocksStream`
(40 sequential) and `go test -count=10 -parallel 4` (40 concurrent
across both flashblocks tests) — all 40+40 passed. Also ran with
`-race -count=2` to confirm no new data races.

fix(flashblocks): size flashblock client buffer for 30s of CI headroom

The previous buffer of numFlashblocks*2 (40 slots ≈ 8 s at the 200 ms
flashblock cadence defined in
rust/op-reth/crates/flashblocks/src/cache.rs) is too tight for CI.
Under load the test goroutine can be stalled for several seconds while
op-rbuilder, rollup-boost and the sequencer contend for CPU, and if
the channel fills the FlashblockClient drops messages (see the
"channel full, dropping flashblock" path in flashblock_client.go).
Dropped messages defeat the anchor+validate strategy introduced in
the previous commit by leaving gaps in the stream.

Grow the buffer to 150 slots (≈ 30 s at 200 ms cadence) — comfortable
headroom for realistic CI stalls, and still a trivial amount of
memory. Keep numFlashblocks = 20 unchanged: we still only validate

consumer catches up.

* fix(op-supernode): fall back to local-safe/finalized before interop activation (#20191)

Before this fix, super_authority.FullyVerifiedL2Head and FinalizedL2Head
returned (empty, false) whenever the interop verifier was registered but
had no entries in its verifiedDB. op-node's engine controller treats
(empty, false) as "verifier present, no answer" and resolves to genesis,
pinning SafeL2 and FinalizedL2 at block 0 until activation — while
LocalSafe continued to advance normally. Any network with interop
scheduled in the future saw this as a user-visible stall.

Both methods now consult VerificationActivity.IsActiveAt(ss.LocalSafeL2.Time)
before querying verifier state. When every registered verifier reports
inactive at the local-safe timestamp, they return (empty, true) so the
engine controller falls back to local-safe / local-finalized.

Using LocalSafeL2.Time for both heads is sound because FinalizedL2 <=
LocalSafeL2: if local-safe is still pre-activation, finalized is too.
Once a local-safe block crosses activation, the verifier-gated path
resumes.

Flips the 4 RED unit tests added in the previous commit to GREEN and
(by induction from the same root cause) TestPreNoInbox's CrossSafe /
Finalized assertions.

fix(op-acceptance-tests): stabilize TestReorgUnsafeHead (#20201)

Before re-enabling op-node sequencing, wait for the CL's sync status to
reflect the test-sequencer's final committed unsafe head instead of
relying on a pair of 2-second sleeps.

The EL's unsafe head is updated synchronously by CommitBlock (engine
NewPayload + engine forkchoice update), but the op-node's StatusTracker
and Sequencer.latestHead are updated asynchronously via the event loop
when it drains the ForkchoiceUpdateEvent. Under CI load the 2s sleeps
were occasionally too short: StartSequencer read a stale LocalUnsafe
from SyncStatus, passed that stale hash to Sequencer.Start (which
validated it against its equally-stale latestHead), forceStart flipped
the sequencer active, and startBuildingBlock used the stale latestHead
as the parent for the next block -- silently reorging the EL off the
test-sequencer's conflicting fork and causing the assertion at line 114
to see identical hashes.

Note on the test job: despite the CI label "memory-all-kona-op-reth",
this test runs against op-node (the supernode preset hardcodes op-node
and the test-sequencer's opstack_commitBlockV1 RPC is only implemented
by op-node). kona-node tests in the same binary use a different preset.

The fix polls SyncStatus().UnsafeL2.Hash until it matches the EL's
current unsafe head. Within a single event-loop dispatch the handlers
run sequentially, so StatusTracker and Sequencer.OnEvent can complete
out of order; but by the time SyncStatus reports the expected hash,
either (a) the sequencer has already processed the same
ForkchoiceUpdateEvent, or (b) when it does, Sequencer.Start's internal
mutex serialises Start against OnEvent, so StartSequencer either
observes the fresh latestHead or fails fast with a visible "block hash
does not match" error rather than silently reorging. In the worst case
the poll times out with a clear message, replacing a silent failure
with an explicit one.

Refs ethereum-optimism/optimism#20198

Adds the Karst hardfork input size limit (74,880 bytes = 390 pairs × 192)
for the bn254 pairing precompile, replacing the inherited Jovian limit of
81,984 bytes at OpSpecId::KARST and OpSpecId::INTEROP. Jovian itself is
unchanged.

The 8.7% reduction restores Jovian-era headroom under the EIP-7825 L1 gas
cap, accommodating the proposed EIP-7904 pairing cost increase plus
plausible variance without requiring another adjustment. op-geth and
op-program are intentionally not updated (post-Glamsterdam deprecation);
op-revm and kona are the only live paths after Karst.

- op-revm: add KARST_MAX_INPUT_SIZE, bn254_pair::KARST, run_pair_karst;
  karst() precompile set now extends with KARST instead of inheriting JOVIAN.
  Hoist the canonical EIP-197 pairing identity test vector to a shared
  tests-module constant so Jovian and Karst tests reuse it.
- kona fpvm_evm: add BN256_MAX_PAIRING_SIZE_KARST, fpvm_bn128_pair_karst,
  accelerated_karst(); provider dispatches KARST|INTEROP to
  accelerated_karst, JOVIAN keeps accelerated_jovian.
- test_post_jovian_specs_use_jovian_precompiles: rename osaka_addrs →
  karst_addrs, restructure the address-set assertions along fork ancestry
  (KARST ≡ JOVIAN, INTEROP ≡ KARST), and reword messages so they describe
  what's actually compared (addresses match; functions may differ).

  and oversize input, plus provider dispatch via OpSpecId::KARST.
- kona: 2 new bn128_pair tests mirroring the Jovian pair, plus
  test_karst_bn128_pair_enforces_karst_limit proving the KARST provider's

op-reth: serialize proofs ExEx writes to prevent concurrent commit race

The proofs-history ExEx has two concurrent writers into the same MDBX
proofs storage: the main notification loop (`handle_notification` -> the
`handle_chain_{committed,reorged,reverted}` handlers) and the background
`sync_loop` that drains `sync_target_tx` via `process_batch`. Both
independently snapshot `latest_stored`, decide which blocks to append,
then commit. The storage layer's `store_trie_updates_append_only_inner`
check (rust/op-reth/crates/trie/src/db/store.rs:535) re-reads the latest
hash inside the write transaction and returns `OutOfOrder` when the
incoming block's parent no longer matches — the correct safety net, but
for the main task that error bubbles up through `run()` and the ExEx
framework turns it into a process-fatal panic:

    ExEx proofs-history crashed: Block 36 is out of order
      (parent: 0x8475..., latest stored block hash: 0x2cdd...)

When the op-reth sequencer dies mid-test, the supernode stops finding
L2 blocks and the acceptance test's eventual `stat.SafeL2.L1Origin` poll
at op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/seqwindow/expiry_test.go:125 times
out with "expecting CL to sync cross-safe data, after resolving
sequencing window expiry".

`TestSequencingWindowExpiry` triggers the race reliably in principle,
rarely in practice: the sequencing-window-expiry reorg plus recovery
mode produces a burst of notifications that interleave a
non-sequential `ChainCommitted` (which schedules `sync_target_tx`) with
subsequent sequential commits while `sync_loop` is still draining.

Fix: introduce an `Arc<Mutex<()>>` `write_lock` on `OpProofsExEx` that
both writers must hold over their read-and-commit critical section.
`handle_notification` holds it for the whole handler; `process_batch`
reacquires per block so the main task can still interleave between
blocks. The existing append-only check remains the correctness backstop.

All 11 existing `reth-optimism-exex` unit tests still pass.

Refs: ethereum-optimism/optimism#20212

op-node: add RPC-based executing-message validator for unsafe blocks

Adds an optional hook in EngineController.insertUnsafePayload that runs
between NewPayload and ForkchoiceUpdate. When --interop.rpc-overrides is
configured, every executing-message log in a newly-inserted unsafe block
is verified against a remote chain's eth_getLogs endpoint: the log must
exist at the identifier's (origin, block, logIndex), the remote block
timestamp must match, the identifier must not be in the executor block's
future, it must fit inside the message-expiry window, and the payload
hash must match the hash of the remote log's topics + data. Missing or
mismatching messages reject the block; transport errors retry within a
per-block budget (default 60s) before rejecting.

The feature is intended for light-CL operators running without
op-supervisor, as a lightweight alternative to full cross-chain
verification. Parallel per-chain validation via errgroup keeps hot-path
cost bounded to the slowest remote RPC.

feat(alloy-op-evm): post-exec block executor and SDM warming inspector

Add the canonical post-exec block executor, along with the first
feature riding on it — SDM (Sequencer-Defined Metering) block-level
warming refunds, delivered by the SDMWarmingInspector.

- OpBlockExecutor gains three PostExecModes (Disabled / Produce /
  Verify(payload) / Invalid). Produce accumulates per-tx refund
  entries for the payload builder to append as a synthetic 0x7D tx;
  Verify validates an embedded payload against local replay;
  Disabled is the legacy path (byte-identical to pre-SDM).
- SDMWarmingInspector tracks first-warmer provenance for accounts
  and storage slots, emits exact refund attribution events for every
  re-touch past the EIP-2929 warm threshold, and suppresses claims
  from Deposit and synthetic PostExec tx kinds.
- Verify-mode validations reject duplicate payload indexes, payload
  entries targeting deposits or the 0x7D tx itself, and refunds that
  exceed the tx's raw gas. `apply_pre_execution_changes` debug_asserts
  the Produce hooks are wired so a downstream fork can't silently drop
  refunds.
- Canonical gas settlement credits the sender, debits the beneficiary
  and base-fee recipient by the refunded-gas component of their share,
  and commits the deltas when canonical gas falls below raw gas.
- beneficiary_gas_price can legitimately saturate at zero when a
  legacy tx's gas price equals basefee; inline comment documents the
  consensus-valid zero case.

when the sequencer builds under --rollup.sdm-enabled. The tx carries
the executor's accumulated refund entries as its RLP payload and
canonicalizes this node's gas accounting with what a verifier will
later independently replay.

  When off, the payload path is byte-identical to the pre-feature code.

  PayloadBuilderError::EvmExecutionError on any synthetic-tx
  execution failure. Silently dropping it would yield a payload that
  no honest verifier can reproduce.

fix(alloy-op-evm): harden SDM post-exec guards and name EIP-2929 constants

- Reject 0x7D txs in Disabled/Invalid modes. Previously
  `execute_transaction_without_commit` short-circuited any post-exec
  tx regardless of mode, so a follower with SDM off would silently
  accept a payload it never validates — state would diverge without
  a loud failure.
- Reject Produce-mode refunds that exceed raw gas used. An inspector
  over-attribution would otherwise saturate canonical gas to zero
  and emit an SDMGasEntry that a verifier rejects at pre-execution;
  failing the payload build here is strictly better than shipping a
  block the sequencer can't self-verify.
- Replace the 2500/2000/2100 magic numbers in SDMWarmingInspector with
  ACCOUNT_REWARM_REFUND / SLOAD_REWARM_REFUND / SSTORE_REWARM_REFUND
  and cite the EIP-2929 derivation.
- Restore `OpBuilderConfig::new(da_config, gas_limit_config)` to its
  pre-branch 2-arg signature; add `new_with_sdm` for the SDM-aware
  constructor so external callers don't break.

Tests pin:
- Disabled/Invalid modes hard-fail at `execute_transaction` time.
- Produce mode rejects a fake over-refund take-hook.

fix(op-acceptance-tests): stabilize TestUnsafeGapFillAfterUnsafeReorg_RestartL2CL (#20199)

* fix(op-acceptance-tests): stabilize TestUnsafeGapFillAfterUnsafeReorg_RestartL2CL

ReorgTriggered only waits until the block at the reorg-target height has
been rewritten on the sequencer; it does not wait for the sequencer to
rebuild past the verifier's frozen unsafe head. The test then asserts
seq.Number > ver.Number, which races against the sequencer producing the
next block after the reorg. In failing CI (op-geth, pipeline 123064, job
4866963) both heads were observed at 18 because the sequencer had
reorged and rebuilt exactly up to the verifier's frozen height but had
not yet extended past it.

Capture the verifier's unsafe head immediately after stopping L2CLB (at
which point the verifier cannot advance — its CL is down and the preset
has NoDiscovery), then after ReorgTriggered returns wait for the
sequencer to reach verFrozen.Number + 1 before sampling the heads for
the assertion. This makes the seq > ver ordering structurally guaranteed
rather than racing with post-reorg block production.

Refs: ethereum-optimism/optimism#19936

* fix(op-acceptance-tests): widen Matched budget on initial sync in UnsafeGapFillAfterUnsafeReorg_RestartL2CL

The two pre-reorg Matched calls used only 5 attempts (~10s). This assumes
the verifier is already in lockstep with the sequencer, which breaks when
the verifier starts late relative to the sequencer and has to catch up
tens of blocks — e.g. slow op-reth cold start or a gossipsub mesh that
takes time to form under CI contention. When this happens the sequencer
produces a burst of blocks to catch up to wall-clock genesis time, leaving
the verifier well behind. 10s is not enough to close that gap via gossip.

Bump both Matched budgets to 30 attempts (60s) — consistent with the
existing post-stop gap-close budget of 50 attempts — so the verifier can
finish catching up before the test perturbs the system. The happy path
still returns on first success, so fast runs are unaffected.

fix(op-reth): raise supervisor RPC timeout default from 100ms to 2s

The SupervisorClient default request timeout was 100ms, which is too tight
for the localhost HTTP round trip to op-interop-filter / op-supervisor under
CI load (GC pauses, CPU contention, noisy-neighbour runners). When the
timeout fires, op-reth returns InteropTxValidatorError::Timeout(0) — the
trailing 0 comes from Duration::as_secs() on 100ms — surfacing the error
"inbox entry validation timed out, timeout: 0 secs" at the ingress path.

This caused intermittent failures in TestInteropFilter_IngressRejectsInvalid
(ethereum-optimism/optimism#20291): the test submits a tx with a fabricated
access list expecting the filter's "failed to parse access entry"
rejection, but on load the 100ms timeout fires first.

Raise the default to 2s. The timeout is a protective ceiling against a
truly hung upstream, not a latency SLA — the supervisor normally answers in
microseconds and 2s is still well below the test-level 10s context budget,
so a stuck upstream is still caught.

Refs ethereum-optimism/optimism#20291

fix(op-supernode): distinguish transient vs permanent SafeDB gaps in L1AtSafeHead

L1AtSafeHead previously surfaced raw safedb.ErrNotFound from both its
initial latest-lookup and its walkback probe, which chain_container did
not match against ErrL1AtSafeHeadNotFound. Interop's Start loop logged
"failed to progress and record interop" / "error determining l1 block
number at which l2 block became safe" / "L1AtSafeHead: walkback lookup
failed, stopping" every errorBackoffPeriod, drowning logs on nodes that
bootstrapped via CL/snap sync (their SafeDB starts above genesisL1, so
walkback probes below the earliest entry always miss).

Fix it by splitting the failure mode into two sentinels with clearly
different semantics, so callers can react correctly:

- virtual_node.ErrL1AtSafeHeadNotFound (transient):
    * target is ahead of the latest recorded L2 -- chain will catch up
    * SafeDB is empty at startup -- first advance will populate it
  chain_container maps this to ethereum.NotFound; interop backs off
  quietly, same as before.

- virtual_node.ErrL1AtSafeHeadUnavailable (permanent):
    * walkback crossed below the earliest SafeDB entry
      (CL/snap-sync bootstrap gap: the L2 safe-head advance we want
      happened before this node started writing records)
    * walkback reached the genesis bound without L2 ever dropping
      below target (SafeDB near genesis is not considered stable)
  chain_container maps this to a new ErrHistoryUnavailable -- kept
  distinct from ethereum.NotFound so it cannot masquerade as lag.
  Interop's Start loop recognizes it, logs once at Error with
  operator-actionable remediation hints (reseed data dir, advance
  interop.activation-timestamp past the gap, or rederive from L1),
  and returns -- halting the activity instead of spinning on
  errorBackoffPeriod forever.

Tests cover every branch:
- virtual_node_test.go: walkback-past-earliest and genesis-bound both
  return Unavailable (and are asserted distinct from NotFound);
  empty-DB-on-latest-lookup and target-beyond-latest still return
  NotFound; mock SafeDBReader now returns safedb.ErrNotFound to
  mirror the real DB.
- chain_container_test.go: Unavailable -> ErrHistoryUnavailable, and
  explicitly NOT ethereum.NotFound; NotFound -> ethereum.NotFound
  remains.
- interop_test.go: Start halts within 5s (well under
  errorBackoffPeriod) with an error wrapping cc.ErrHistoryUnavailable
  when a chain reports permanent history loss.

fix(op-acceptance-tests): tolerate transient EL errors in Steady sampler

Steady.Run's polling goroutine samples the unsafe head every blockTime to
drive AIMD backpressure. The prior code only tolerated context errors and
fatally asserted on every other error via t.Require().NoError. Under load
(e.g. TestRelayWithInvalidMessagesSteady, where the EL is being spammed
with ~1000 invalid executing messages per block time), the proxy in front
of op-reth intermittently hits TCP dial-backlog saturation and returns
"dial tcp ...: i/o timeout". That is neither context.Canceled nor
context.DeadlineExceeded, so it bypassed the errors.Is guard and tripped
the Require.

The sampler's job is to observe gas usage for backpressure, not to assert
EL liveness. This matches every other error path in this package
(logOnError in Burst/Constant, the warn-and-continue path in the invalid
message spammer), which treats transient EL errors as non-fatal. On
error we now log a warning and skip this tick, leaving AIMD state
unchanged so the current RPS is preserved until the next successful
sample.

Closes ethereum-optimism/optimism#20254

feat(alloy-op-evm): post-exec block executor and SDM warming inspector

Add the canonical post-exec block executor, along with the first
feature riding on it — SDM (Sequencer-Defined Metering) block-level
warming refunds, delivered by the SDMWarmingInspector.

- OpBlockExecutor gains three PostExecModes (Disabled / Produce /
  Verify(payload) / Invalid). Produce accumulates per-tx refund
  entries for the payload builder to append as a synthetic 0x7D tx;
  Verify validates an embedded payload against local replay;
  Disabled is the legacy path (byte-identical to pre-SDM).
- SDMWarmingInspector tracks first-warmer provenance for accounts
  and storage slots, emits exact refund attribution events for every
  re-touch past the EIP-2929 warm threshold, and suppresses claims
  from Deposit and synthetic PostExec tx kinds.
- Verify-mode validations reject duplicate payload indexes, payload
  entries targeting deposits or the 0x7D tx itself, and refunds that
  exceed the tx's raw gas. `apply_pre_execution_changes` debug_asserts
  the Produce hooks are wired so a downstream fork can't silently drop
  refunds.
- Canonical gas settlement credits the sender, debits the beneficiary
  and base-fee recipient by the refunded-gas component of their share,
  and commits the deltas when canonical gas falls below raw gas.
- beneficiary_gas_price can legitimately saturate at zero when a
  legacy tx's gas price equals basefee; inline comment documents the
  consensus-valid zero case.

fix(op-supernode): distinguish transient vs permanent SafeDB gaps in L1AtSafeHead (#20292)

L1AtSafeHead previously surfaced raw safedb.ErrNotFound from both its
initial latest-lookup and its walkback probe, which chain_container did
not match against ErrL1AtSafeHeadNotFound. Interop's Start loop logged
"failed to progress and record interop" / "error determining l1 block
number at which l2 block became safe" / "L1AtSafeHead: walkback lookup
failed, stopping" every errorBackoffPeriod, drowning logs on nodes that
bootstrapped via CL/snap sync (their SafeDB starts above genesisL1, so
walkback probes below the earliest entry always miss).

Fix it by splitting the failure mode into two sentinels with clearly
different semantics, so callers can react correctly:

- virtual_node.ErrL1AtSafeHeadNotFound (transient):
    * target is ahead of the latest recorded L2 -- chain will catch up
    * SafeDB is empty at startup -- first advance will populate it
  chain_container maps this to ethereum.NotFound; interop backs off
  quietly, same as before.

- virtual_node.ErrL1AtSafeHeadUnavailable (permanent):
    * walkback crossed below the earliest SafeDB entry
      (CL/snap-sync bootstrap gap: the L2 safe-head advance we want
      happened before this node started writing records)
    * walkback reached the genesis bound without L2 ever dropping
      below target (SafeDB near genesis is not considered stable)
  chain_container maps this to a new ErrHistoryUnavailable -- kept
  distinct from ethereum.NotFound so it cannot masquerade as lag.
  Interop's Start loop recognizes it, logs once at Error with
  operator-actionable remediation hints (reseed data dir, advance
  interop.activation-timestamp past the gap, or rederive from L1),
  and returns -- halting the activity instead of spinning on
  errorBackoffPeriod forever.

Tests cover every branch:
- virtual_node_test.go: walkback-past-earliest and genesis-bound both
  return Unavailable (and are asserted distinct from NotFound);
  empty-DB-on-latest-lookup and target-beyond-latest still return
  NotFound; mock SafeDBReader now returns safedb.ErrNotFound to
  mirror the real DB.
- chain_container_test.go: Unavailable -> ErrHistoryUnavailable, and
  explicitly NOT ethereum.NotFound; NotFound -> ethereum.NotFound
  remains.
- interop_test.go: Start halts within 5s (well under
  errorBackoffPeriod) with an error wrapping cc.ErrHistoryUnavailable
  when a chain reports permanent history loss.

fix(op-devstack): extend preset CrossSafe budget for ELSync mode

The SingleChainMultiNode preset's initial sync check runs the same 30-attempt
(60s) CrossSafe match for every verifier sync mode. In ELSync mode that is
too tight: the verifier must finish P2P EL sync and emit its first forkchoice
update before derivation can start advancing safe, and under CI load that
chain of events routinely exceeds 60s, causing TestELSyncSafeRetractedByOffset
and TestTruncateDatabaseOnELResync to flake at setup. Expose the resolved
sync mode on OpNode and give ELSync verifiers a 4x CrossSafe budget.
LocalUnsafe and CLSync budgets are unchanged.

supernode: rewrite interop log backfill around backfillEndTimestamp

Replace the mutable runtimeActivationTimestamp with a pure
backfillEndTimestamp. runLogBackfill now returns (minCrossSafeTime, error)
instead of advancing activation in place; the caller assigns the result to
i.backfillEndTimestamp and firstVerifiableTimestamp() derives end+1 (or
activationTimestamp when backfill did not run).

Backfill itself runs per chain in parallel over a uniform timestamp window
[max(act, minCrossSafeTime-depth), minCrossSafeTime] so all chains seal to
the same endpoint — chains whose local tip is ahead of min cross-safe
catch up via the main loop instead of eagerly during backfill.

Adds tests covering the short-circuits (depth<=0, no chains,
activation-in-future) and updates devstack assertions plus logdb's
empty-DB guard to use firstVerifiableTimestamp.

fix(op-node): trigger reset when EL returns SYNCING during forkchoice update in CL-sync mode

When an execution client (e.g. op-reth) is restarted, it may lose its in-memory
canonical state and return SYNCING to forkchoice updates. Without this check,
the SYNCING response gets recorded as the last-accepted forkchoice via
`e.lastForkchoice = fc`, and the subsequent `if fc == e.lastForkchoice { return nil }`
guard suppresses further FCU retries — op-node stalls until restarted.

This fix uses the existing checkForkchoiceUpdatedStatus method to validate the FCU
response before recording lastForkchoice. In CL-sync mode, SYNCING triggers a
ResetError, so FindL2Heads re-discovers the EL's actual chain state. In EL-sync
mode, SYNCING remains accepted (existing behavior preserved).

This resolves the issue where op-reth reboots require an op-node restart to recover.

test(kona-interop): add failing regression test for same-ts cycle detection divergence

Demonstrates that detect_cycles currently filters same-timestamp cycle graph nodes
by the executing-block timestamp (msg.executing_timestamp) instead of the
referenced initiating-message's timestamp (msg.inner.identifier.timestamp), which
is what op-supernode's buildCycleGraph does via ExecutingMessage.Timestamp.

Two EMs at the same executing-block timestamp that both reference historical
initiating messages on each other's chains are wrongly admitted into the cycle
graph, where a cross-chain edge is then drawn via executing_message_before and a
spurious cycle is detected. op-supernode would exclude both EMs from the graph,
so no cycle is reported there.

Test fails on this branch and will pass once the timestamp filter in detect_cycles
is corrected. See ethereum-optimism/optimism#20303 review discussion.

fix(op-supernode): break circular SafeDB dependency in interop verifier

OptimisticAt and VerifiedAt queried SafeDB (via safeDBAtL2 → L1AtSafeHead)
to resolve the L1 inclusion block for a given L2 block. However, SafeDB is
only populated when blocks are promoted to cross-safe (PromoteSafe →
SafeDerivedEvent → SafeHeadUpdated). With interop enabled, cross-safe
promotion requires the interop verifier to verify first — but the verifier
calls OptimisticAt, creating a deadlock where neither can make progress.

Use L2BlockRef.L1Origin directly instead. This field is set during batch
derivation and is available immediately, with no dependency on cross-safe
promotion. It represents the L1 block whose batch data included the L2
block, which is the correct L1 inclusion data for interop consistency
checking.

Also adds two new metrics for interop observability:
- supernode_interop_chain_not_ready_total: per-chain counter for when a
  chain is not ready during verification (the symptom of this bug)
- supernode_interop_verification_lag_seconds: gauge measuring the gap
  between latest verified timestamp and unsafe L2 tip

fix(kona-interop): filter historical-timestamp EMs from cycle graph

Address review feedback on #20303 (ajsutton). Layer a second filter on
detect_cycles so an executing message is admitted into the same-timestamp
cycle graph only when its *executing block* timestamp **and** its
referenced *initiating message* timestamp both equal the target timestamp.

Previously only the executing-block timestamp was checked, matching
op-supernode's primary filter in verifyCycleMessages but missing the
secondary filter in buildCycleGraph (em.Timestamp == ts, sourced from
MessageIdentifier.Timestamp). Without the secondary filter, EMs that
reference historical initiating messages were drawn into the current-ts
graph and could fabricate spurious cross-chain edges through
executingMessageBefore, producing false-positive cycles.

Fold in the regression test from #20305 and add a direct unit test for
the new filter condition. Generalize the make_em helper so tests can
specify the initiating-message timestamp independently of the executing
block timestamp. Tighten the MessageGraph doc comment: blocks in the
graph may be at different timestamps, one per chain, and expand the
CyclicDependency variant doc to record that each error represents a
single cycle at a single timestamp; multi-timestamp cycles surface
iteratively through the consolidation retry loop.

feat(alloy-op-evm): post-exec block executor and SDM warming inspector

Add the canonical post-exec block executor, along with the first
feature riding on it — SDM (Sequencer-Defined Metering) block-level
warming refunds, delivered by the SDMWarmingInspector.

- OpBlockExecutor gains three PostExecModes (Disabled / Produce /
  Verify(payload) / Invalid). Produce accumulates per-tx refund
  entries for the payload builder to append as a synthetic 0x7D tx;
  Verify validates an embedded payload against local replay;
  Disabled is the legacy path (byte-identical to pre-SDM).
- SDMWarmingInspector tracks first-warmer provenance for accounts
  and storage slots, emits exact refund attribution events for every
  re-touch past the EIP-2929 warm threshold, and suppresses claims
  from Deposit and synthetic PostExec tx kinds.
- Verify-mode validations reject duplicate payload indexes, payload
  entries targeting deposits or the 0x7D tx itself, and refunds that
  exceed the tx's raw gas. `apply_pre_execution_changes` debug_asserts
  the Produce hooks are wired so a downstream fork can't silently drop
  refunds.
- Canonical gas settlement credits the sender, debits the beneficiary
  and base-fee recipient by the refunded-gas component of their share,
  and commits the deltas when canonical gas falls below raw gas.
- beneficiary_gas_price can legitimately saturate at zero when a
  legacy tx's gas price equals basefee; inline comment documents the
  consensus-valid zero case.

fix(kona-hardforks): use OnceBox to avoid critical-section dep on no_std

sync::OnceCell with the critical-section feature requires an impl of
_critical_section_1_0_{acquire,release} to be linked in, which the
MIPS64 cannon and RISC-V asterisc fault-proof VM targets don't provide.
This broke kona-client on those targets.

Switch the generator to emit once_cell::race::OnceBox, which uses a
single AtomicPtr for the cache slot — lock-free and requires no
critical-section impl. The NutBundle is heap-allocated via Box on first
call and then cached as &'static NutBundle for all subsequent calls.
Enables the `race` feature on once_cell.

fix(op-reth): raise supervisor RPC timeout default from 100ms to 2s (#20296)

The SupervisorClient default request timeout was 100ms, which is too tight
for the localhost HTTP round trip to op-interop-filter / op-supervisor under
CI load (GC pauses, CPU contention, noisy-neighbour runners). When the
timeout fires, op-reth returns InteropTxValidatorError::Timeout(0) — the
trailing 0 comes from Duration::as_secs() on 100ms — surfacing the error
"inbox entry validation timed out, timeout: 0 secs" at the ingress path.

This caused intermittent failures in TestInteropFilter_IngressRejectsInvalid
(ethereum-optimism/optimism#20291): the test submits a tx with a fabricated
access list expecting the filter's "failed to parse access entry"
rejection, but on load the 100ms timeout fires first.

Raise the default to 2s. The timeout is a protective ceiling against a
truly hung upstream, not a latency SLA — the supervisor normally answers in
microseconds and 2s is still well below the test-level 10s context budget,
so a stuck upstream is still caught.

Refs ethereum-optimism/optimism#20291

feat(alloy-op-evm): post-exec block executor and SDM warming inspector

Add the canonical post-exec block executor, along with the first
feature riding on it — SDM (Sequencer-Defined Metering) block-level
warming refunds, delivered by the SDMWarmingInspector.

- OpBlockExecutor gains three PostExecModes (Disabled / Produce /
  Verify(payload) / Invalid). Produce accumulates per-tx refund
  entries for the payload builder to append as a synthetic 0x7D tx;
  Verify validates an embedded payload against local replay;
  Disabled is the legacy path (byte-identical to pre-SDM).
- SDMWarmingInspector tracks first-warmer provenance for accounts
  and storage slots, emits exact refund attribution events for every
  re-touch past the EIP-2929 warm threshold, and suppresses claims
  from Deposit and synthetic PostExec tx kinds.
- Verify-mode validations reject duplicate payload indexes, payload
  entries targeting deposits or the 0x7D tx itself, and refunds that
  exceed the tx's raw gas. `apply_pre_execution_changes` debug_asserts
  the Produce hooks are wired so a downstream fork can't silently drop
  refunds.
- Canonical gas settlement credits the sender, debits the beneficiary
  and base-fee recipient by the refunded-gas component of their share,
  and commits the deltas when canonical gas falls below raw gas.
- beneficiary_gas_price can legitimately saturate at zero when a
  legacy tx's gas price equals basefee; inline comment documents the
  consensus-valid zero case.

fix(op-fetcher): recover permissioned game roles via DGF.gameArgs on v2.2.0+

The prior commit stopped the depth-1 revert but left challenger/proposer/MIPS/
PreimageOracle unset for any v2.2.0+ chain (post-CWIA refactor). On those chains
the fields are clones-with-immutable-args appended only to live game clones,
so impl-level getters legitimately return 0. For chains where no PERMISSIONED_
CANNON game has ever been created (OP Mainnet, Base, OP Sepolia) there isn't
even a clone to read from — codegen would silently drop those four addresses
from superchain-registry's addresses.json.

DisputeGameFactory.gameArgs is a public mapping populated at impl registration
via setImplementation(GameType, IDisputeGame, bytes). It holds the full CWIA
blob for the game type, including challenger and proposer for PERMISSIONED_
CANNON, regardless of whether any games have been created. Add it to IFetcher,
fall through to it whenever an impl-level read returns 0, and parse the
abi.encodePacked layout (164 bytes) to extract MIPS/ASR/proposer/challenger.

endTimestamp+1 as a no-op the supernode validates from L1 advance alone.

fix(kona-hardforks): use OnceBox to avoid critical-section dep on no_std

sync::OnceCell with the critical-section feature requires an impl of
_critical_section_1_0_{acquire,release} to be linked in, which the
MIPS64 cannon and RISC-V asterisc fault-proof VM targets don't provide.
This broke kona-client on those targets.

Switch the generator to emit once_cell::race::OnceBox, which uses a
single AtomicPtr for the cache slot — lock-free and requires no
critical-section impl. The NutBundle is heap-allocated via Box on first
call and then cached as &'static NutBundle for all subsequent calls.
Enables the `race` feature on once_cell.

The cannon-target docker run mounted only the rust/ directory at

panics when it can't find the directory.

test(op-e2e): tombstone forks-without-NUT-bundle exception list

Interop is post-Karst chronologically but still uses the legacy
hardcoded upgrade-transactions path rather than a JSON NUT bundle, so
require.NoError on derive.UpgradeTransactions(forks.Interop) failed.

Replace the simple no-error assertion with a bidirectional check
against forksWithoutNUTBundle = {forks.Interop: true}. The exception
list cannot go stale silently:

- Fork lacks bundle and isn't on the list → test fails (forces a
  decision: implement the bundle or update the list).
- Fork has bundle and is on the list → test fails with
  "remove it from forksWithoutNUTBundle".

When Interop gets its NUT bundle in a follow-up PR, this test will
fail until forks.Interop is removed from the exception list, ensuring
the list stays in lockstep with the codebase.
