feat(kona-interop): add cycle detection to MessageGraph (#20303)

* feat(kona-interop): add cycle detection to MessageGraph

MessageGraph validated executing messages independently via
check_single_dependency, which cannot detect circular dependencies
between same-timestamp cross-chain messages. op-supernode rejects
these cycles using Kahn's topological sort; kona accepted them.

Add cycle detection to MessageGraph::resolve() that runs before
per-message validation. The implementation matches op-supernode's
buildCycleGraph/checkCycle semantics: intra-chain sequential edges,
cross-chain edges via executingMessageBefore, and Kahn's algorithm
to identify cycle participants while sparing bystander chains.

- Add CyclicDependency error variant to MessageGraphError
- Add executing_log_index to EnrichedExecutingMessage for graph construction
- Handle CyclicDependency in the consolidation retry loop
- Fix test_derive_and_resolve_simple_graph_with_cycles to assert rejection
- Add tests for triangle cycles, one-way deps, and bystander chains

Closes #20196

* improve tests

* fmt/clippy

* fix(kona-interop): filter historical-timestamp EMs from cycle graph

Address review feedback on #20303 (ajsutton). Layer a second filter on
detect_cycles so an executing message is admitted into the same-timestamp
cycle graph only when its *executing block* timestamp **and** its
referenced *initiating message* timestamp both equal the target timestamp.

Previously only the executing-block timestamp was checked, matching
op-supernode's primary filter in verifyCycleMessages but missing the
secondary filter in buildCycleGraph (em.Timestamp == ts, sourced from
MessageIdentifier.Timestamp). Without the secondary filter, EMs that
reference historical initiating messages were drawn into the current-ts
graph and could fabricate spurious cross-chain edges through
executingMessageBefore, producing false-positive cycles.

Fold in the regression test from #20305 and add a direct unit test for
the new filter condition. Generalize the make_em helper so tests can
specify the initiating-message timestamp independently of the executing
block timestamp. Tighten the MessageGraph doc comment: blocks in the
graph may be at different timestamps, one per chain, and expand the
CyclicDependency variant doc to record that each error represents a
single cycle at a single timestamp; multi-timestamp cycles surface
iteratively through the consolidation retry loop.

* test(kona-interop): add op-supernode parity cycle-detection cases (#20354)

Mirrors four boundary cases from op-supernode's cycle_test.go that did not
have Kona equivalents:

- triangle with missing leg (cycle_test.go:454-462)
- diamond pattern (cycle_test.go:268-287, from TestCheckCycle)
- bystander chain refs absent chain (cycle_test.go:418-426)
- multi-hop one-way dependency (cycle_test.go:428-434)

All added at the existing `test_detect_cycles_*` layer using the existing
`make_em` helper — no new test scaffolding. Diamond layout co-locates the
sink EM on the same chain as one of its parents so the intra-chain edge
provides the second incoming dependency.

fix(op-node): trigger reset when EL returns SYNCING during forkchoice update in CL-sync mode (#20310)

When an execution client (e.g. op-reth) is restarted, it may lose its in-memory
canonical state and return SYNCING to forkchoice updates. Without this check,
the SYNCING response gets recorded as the last-accepted forkchoice via
`e.lastForkchoice = fc`, and the subsequent `if fc == e.lastForkchoice { return nil }`
guard suppresses further FCU retries — op-node stalls until restarted.

This fix uses the existing checkForkchoiceUpdatedStatus method to validate the FCU
response before recording lastForkchoice. In CL-sync mode, SYNCING triggers a
ResetError, so FindL2Heads re-discovers the EL's actual chain state. In EL-sync
mode, SYNCING remains accepted (existing behavior preserved).

This resolves the issue where op-reth reboots require an op-node restart to recover.

test: re-sample both nodes in InSyncFn

The previous InSyncFn snapshotted the reference head once at the start
of the check and then waited up to N attempts for the base node to
incorporate that exact block. In reorg-recovery tests the reference
node can briefly hold an unsafe block that is later reorged out by the
sequencer, which left InSyncFn permanently stuck against a stale target
(see TestFollowL2_ReorgRecovery).

Re-sample both nodes on every attempt and consider them in sync when:
1. the two head numbers differ by at most maxInSyncGap blocks
2. at the lower of the two heights, both nodes agree on the canonical
   block hash

Both heads being live means a transient reorg on either side is
forgiven on the next tick, while the gap+canonical check prevents
declaring nodes in sync when one is far behind or on a different fork.
test: re-sample both nodes in InSyncFn

test: require slower node to catch up to initial high water mark in InSyncFn

The 10-block tolerance in InSyncFn could falsely pass when a reorg has
just happened: both nodes can sit a few blocks below the divergence
point, agree on shared pre-reorg history, and look in-sync even though
the slower node hasn't yet observed the reorg.

Sample both heads once before the retry loop and remember the higher of
the two as a catch-up target. The slower live head must reach that
target before the gap and canonical-hash checks decide convergence,
which forces both nodes to advance past where the faster node was when
the check started.

feat(op-reth): compute miner fee on pool tx in payload builder

Move the `effective_tip_per_gas` call in
`OpPayloadBuilderCtx::execute_best_transactions` to before
`into_consensus()`, so the miner fee is computed from the pool
transaction rather than the consensus transaction.

Semantically identical for vanilla op-reth users: for stock EIP-1559 /
legacy / deposit txs, `effective_tip_per_gas` returns the same value
on the pool or consensus form. The pool is queried with `block.basefee`,
so any tx returned from `best_txs` satisfies `max_fee_per_gas >= base_fee`.
The existing `expect` invariant still holds (I made the message more
explicit).

This unblocks a cleanup in Celo's reth implementation. On Celo,
`max_fee_per_gas` on the consensus tx can be denominated in an ERC-20
fee currency instead of native wei (CIP-64). The pool validator converts
to native equivalents and exposes the correct tip via the pool tx's
`effective_tip_per_gas` impl, but op-reth currently discards that view
via `into_consensus()` before reading the tip. Without this change, the
Celo fork needs a `SignedTx` newtype that stashes native-equivalent fees
on the consensus tx solely to thread them through this one call site
(~600 lines in celo-kona's `signed_tx.rs`, deletable once this lands).

See https://github.com/celo-org/celo-kona/issues/152

feat(alloy-op-evm): post-exec block executor and SDM warming inspector

Add the canonical post-exec block executor, along with the first
feature riding on it — SDM (Sequencer-Defined Metering) block-level
warming refunds, delivered by the SDMWarmingInspector.

- OpBlockExecutor gains three PostExecModes (Disabled / Produce /
  Verify(payload) / Invalid). Produce accumulates per-tx refund
  entries for the payload builder to append as a synthetic 0x7D tx;
  Verify validates an embedded payload against local replay;
  Disabled is the legacy path (byte-identical to pre-SDM).
- SDMWarmingInspector tracks first-warmer provenance for accounts
  and storage slots, emits exact refund attribution events for every
  re-touch past the EIP-2929 warm threshold, and suppresses claims
  from Deposit and synthetic PostExec tx kinds.
- Verify-mode validations reject duplicate payload indexes, payload
  entries targeting deposits or the 0x7D tx itself, and refunds that
  exceed the tx's raw gas. `apply_pre_execution_changes` debug_asserts
  the Produce hooks are wired so a downstream fork can't silently drop
  refunds.
- Canonical gas settlement credits the sender, debits the beneficiary
  and base-fee recipient by the refunded-gas component of their share,
  and commits the deltas when canonical gas falls below raw gas.
- beneficiary_gas_price can legitimately saturate at zero when a
  legacy tx's gas price equals basefee; inline comment documents the
  consensus-valid zero case.

fix(op-supernode): guard chain container vn against torn interface read

Supernode.Start fires the Interop activity and chain-container goroutines
in parallel. Interop's checkChainsReady immediately calls c.OptimisticAt ->
c.SyncStatus, which reads c.vn while the chain container is concurrently
assigning it in its restart loop. A torn two-word interface read can yield
(type=*simpleVirtualNode, data=nil); the `c.vn == nil` guard returns false,
the method dispatches on a nil receiver, and v.mu.Lock() panics at offset
0x58 (the mu field inside simpleVirtualNode).

Protect c.vn with a sync.RWMutex and route all reads/writes through
getVN/setVN helpers so every method takes one consistent snapshot. Also
add nil-receiver guards on the *simpleVirtualNode methods as a defense
against typed-nil interfaces slipping through in tests or future refactors.

feat(kona): execute NUT bundles at Karst fork activation (#20157)

* feat(kona): execute NUT bundles at Karst fork activation

Add build.rs that reads karst_nut_bundle.json at compile time and
generates Rust code to construct the NutBundle. The derive pipeline
now adds upgrade gas to the block gas limit at fork activation,
matching op-node's gas accounting behavior.

* test(op-e2e): add generic NUT bundle activation block action test

Verifies that every fork with an embedded NUT bundle produces an
activation block containing exactly the bundle's deposit transactions.
Discovery uses forks.All + derive.UpgradeTransactions, so future forks
with NUT bundles are covered automatically without test changes.

* fix(kona): mirror NUT bundles into kona-hardforks crate

The Docker build context for kona images is scoped to rust/, so build.rs
cannot reach op-core/nuts/bundles/ via ancestor walk and the kona-client/
host/node images fail to build. Keep a byte-identical copy inside the
crate, written and verified automatically by the existing snapshot/lock
tooling so the two sources cannot silently drift.

* Revert "fix(kona): mirror NUT bundles into kona-hardforks crate"

This reverts commit 941e15aa7ce4f7816e1a8ae5b6ae23ef4acb1cac.

* build(docker): pass NUT bundles as named context to kona images

The kona-hardforks build.rs walks ancestors of CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR to find
op-core/nuts/bundles/ during compilation. The kona-{client,host,node}
images scope their Docker context to rust/, so the ancestor walk can't
reach op-core/ and the images fail to build.

Pass op-core/nuts/bundles as an additional named BuildKit context
(nuts-bundles) and copy it into /workspace/op-core/nuts/bundles so the
ancestor walk succeeds. Keeps the primary rust/ context small and avoids
mirroring the bundle JSON into the crate tree.

* test(op-e2e): tighten NUT bundle activation test coverage

Iterate forks.From(forks.Karst) with a NoError assertion on
derive.UpgradeTransactions rather than silently skipping forks whose
bundle fails to load, so a broken bundle surfaces as a test failure.

Also assert every tx in the activation block has a successful receipt
so a reverted upgrade tx can't hide behind the byte-equality check.

* refactor(kona-hardforks): extract impl_hardfork_from_bundle macro

The Hardfork impl for each NUT-bundle-backed fork is identical boilerplate
(decode, EIP-2718 encode, sum gas). Move that pattern into a single
internal macro so adding future forks is a one-liner next to the
build-script-generated constructor.

* refactor(kona-hardforks): make build.rs testable with shared codegen

Split parsing + codegen into build_helpers.rs, included via #[path] from
both the build script and a new integration test. Use anyhow to carry
error context up to a single panic in main. The integration test runs
the generator on a fixture JSON and asserts the exact Rust source output,
so codegen changes surface as a test failure rather than a downstream
compile error.

* test(op-e2e): add karst_fork_test with pre/post impl slot assertion

Follows the per-fork test convention from ecotone/fjord/isthmus/holocene.
Asserts the EIP-1967 implementation slot of representative predeploy
proxies (L1Block, GasPriceOracle) changes across Karst activation — a
Karst-specific smoke test that the bundle's proxy upgrades took effect.

Not generalized into the NUT bundle activation test because it does not
hold for future forks that may not upgrade proxies.

* refactor(op-core/forks): add Prev() sibling to Next()

Share the initialization between the next/prev maps and replace the
manual forks.All index walk in nut_bundle_activation_test.go with
forks.Prev(fork). Keeps neighbor-navigation centralized in the forks
package rather than re-derived at call sites.

* test(op-e2e): run fault-proof program and fold karst assertions in

The generic activation test was missing the core RunFaultProofProgram
call (preceded by BatchMineAndSync to advance the safe head), so it
only exercised the sequencer, not the proof pipeline it lives under
actions/proofs/ to validate.

Fold the Karst-specific impl-slot assertions back in via a switch on
fork name, establishing the pattern for future forks to register their
own post-activation checks alongside the universal ones. Delete
karst_fork_test.go.

* test(op-e2e): tighten activation-block checks

Use RollupCfg.IsActivationBlockForFork instead of the unguarded
IsActivationBlock(time-blockTime, time) — the helper avoids a uint64
underflow when actHeader.Time < blockTime.

Assert the safe head lands exactly on the activation block rather than
just past it; BatchMineAndSync adds no new L2 blocks, so equality is
the right invariant.

* test(op-core/forks): add unit tests for Next, Prev, From

Table-driven coverage of edge cases (first, middle, last, unknown)
plus a NextPrev/PrevNext inverse check that guards against the two
maps drifting out of sync.

* perf(kona-hardforks): cache NUT bundle in OnceCell

Generated bundle constructors now wrap construction in a function-scoped
once_cell::sync::OnceCell and return &'static NutBundle. The first call
allocates and stores the bundle; subsequent calls return a cached
reference. Activation-path calls to txs() and upgrade_gas() no longer
reallocate on each invocation.

Consumers are unchanged — method calls auto-deref through the reference.

* style(kona-hardforks): apply nightly rustfmt and clippy fixes

cargo fmt -- collapses a few multi-line statements onto one line per
the use_small_heuristics = "Max" rustfmt.toml setting.

cargo clippy -- replaces a match-on-Option in the bundle codegen with
Option::map_or_else per the option_if_let_else lint.

* build(docker): mount NUT bundles into kona-cannon-prestate build

The cannon-repro.dockerfile's client-build stage runs cargo build on the
kona workspace, which triggers the kona-hardforks build script. That
script walks ancestors of CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR looking for op-core/ and
panicked because the context only contained kona/. Pull in
op-core/nuts/bundles from the existing 'monorepo' named context so the
ancestor walk succeeds — same pattern as the kona-node/host/client
image fix.

* fix: address nightly rustfmt and go-lint findings

- stateful.rs: collapse the u64::from_be_bytes call onto one line per
  nightly rustfmt's use_small_heuristics = "Max" setting. Introduced
  by the original Karst upgrade_gas change; caught by rust-fmt CI.
- nut_bundle_activation_test.go: use bigs.Uint64Strict(bigInt) instead
  of bigInt.Uint64() per the repo's bigint custom golangci-lint rule.

* fix(kona-hardforks): use OnceBox to avoid critical-section dep on no_std

sync::OnceCell with the critical-section feature requires an impl of
_critical_section_1_0_{acquire,release} to be linked in, which the
MIPS64 cannon and RISC-V asterisc fault-proof VM targets don't provide.
This broke kona-client on those targets.

Switch the generator to emit once_cell::race::OnceBox, which uses a
single AtomicPtr for the cache slot — lock-free and requires no
critical-section impl. The NutBundle is heap-allocated via Box on first
call and then cached as &'static NutBundle for all subsequent calls.
Enables the `race` feature on once_cell.

* build(kona): mount op-core/nuts/bundles in build-cannon-client recipe

The cannon-target docker run mounted only the rust/ directory at
/workdir, leaving /workdir/op-core/ absent. The kona-hardforks build
script walks ancestors of CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR looking for op-core/ and
panics when it can't find the directory.

Add a second read-only volume mount that exposes op-core/nuts/bundles
at /workdir/op-core/nuts/bundles, mirroring the named-context fix used
by the kona-node/host/client image bake and the cannon-prestate
Dockerfile. Unblocks kona-build-fpvm-cannon-client and
kona-host-client-offline-cannon.

* test(op-e2e): tombstone forks-without-NUT-bundle exception list

Interop is post-Karst chronologically but still uses the legacy
hardcoded upgrade-transactions path rather than a JSON NUT bundle, so
require.NoError on derive.UpgradeTransactions(forks.Interop) failed.

Replace the simple no-error assertion with a bidirectional check
against forksWithoutNUTBundle = {forks.Interop: true}. The exception
list cannot go stale silently:

- Fork lacks bundle and isn't on the list → test fails (forces a
  decision: implement the bundle or update the list).
- Fork has bundle and is on the list → test fails with
  "remove it from forksWithoutNUTBundle".

When Interop gets its NUT bundle in a follow-up PR, this test will
fail until forks.Interop is removed from the exception list, ensuring
the list stays in lockstep with the codebase.

* chore(kona-hardforks): propagate std feature to new dependencies

Zepter's `lint propagate-feature` check requires kona-hardforks's
`std` feature to also enable the `std` feature of every dependency
(runtime, build, and dev) that has one. Add propagation entries for
the deps introduced by the NUT bundle work: anyhow, once_cell, serde,
and serde_json.

* fix(op-e2e): wire KarstTime into rollup config builder

Why: TestActivationBlockNUTBundle is the first test to probe Karst
activation; without KarstTime in the rollup config, IsActivationBlockForFork
never fires for Karst.

* fix(kona-hardforks): probe for bundle file in build.rs ancestor walk

Why: Docker bind-mounts auto-create empty op-core/ ancestor stubs on the
host; an is_dir() check picks those up before reaching the real op-core
at the monorepo root. Probe for the karst bundle file directly.

ci: cap solc parallelism to 2 threads, retry contracts-bedrock-tests on large

Both 'large' (8GB RAM) and 'xlarge' (16GB RAM) OOM-killed solc with the
signature 'solc exited with signal: 9 (SIGKILL)' across all 12 matrix variants.

Root cause: foundry parallelizes solc compilation across logical cores by
default. On 'large' (4 vCPU), 4 solc processes run concurrently; on 'xlarge'
(8 vCPU), 8 do. With ~729 files to compile across 3 solc versions, peak
parallel memory exceeds available RAM.

This commit caps parallelism to 2 via FOUNDRY_THREADS=2 (foundry-rs/foundry
env var, equivalent to forge test --threads 2), which should halve peak
compilation memory at the cost of slightly longer wall-clock time. Sets the
resource_class back to large since the parallelism cap is the real fix.

which is V4 in upstream reth (Prague is mainnet). Production op-stack chains
issue V3 FCUs for every Ecotone+ timestamp via op-node's

0x03 and op-reth emitted ids beginning 0x04. The divergence breaks consumers
that compare ids across clients (rollup-boost in particular) and prevents
builder blocks and flashblocks from being delivered on chains using
op-rbuilder built on op-reth.

bumps its FCU version. Pre-PR-#23202 reth threaded the version through
`PayloadBuilderAttributes::try_new(parent, attrs, version)`; the refactor
removed that channel, so a runtime-aware fix would require a reth change.

fix(op-acceptance): drive Stage 2b catch-up to convergence, not single pass

The previous catch-up loop was a single forward pass against the initial
boundaryTimestamp, then re-derived max afterward. This left a gap when a
slow-block-time chain (BT=2) overshot in Stage 1+2 and a fast chain (BT=1)
needed multiple iterations to catch up: extending the BT=2 chain by one
block could push the max forward by 2 s, leaving the BT=1 chain at the
old max minus 1 s. AwaitValidatedTimestamp(boundary) then hung because
the lagging chain had no L1 block covering boundary.

Replace the single-pass catch-up with iterative convergence: each
iteration recomputes the max head time and extends every chain whose
head is strictly below it. Loop terminates when no chain advances. After
the loop every chain's head sits at exactly the same timestamp; assert
exact equality and use it as boundaryTimestamp.

Strengthen the post-Stage 2b invariant from "head covers boundary" to
"head time == boundary" — the iterative catch-up makes this exact
equality achievable, and tests 5/6 rely on it.

ahead of chain[0] by the time the batcher restarted, the boundary

test: re-sample both nodes in InSyncFn

The previous InSyncFn snapshotted the reference head once at the start
of the check and then waited up to N attempts for the base node to
incorporate that exact block. In reorg-recovery tests the reference
node can briefly hold an unsafe block that is later reorged out by the
sequencer, which left InSyncFn permanently stuck against a stale target
(see TestFollowL2_ReorgRecovery).

Re-sample both nodes on every attempt and consider them in sync when:
1. the two head numbers differ by at most maxInSyncGap blocks
2. at the lower of the two heights, both nodes agree on the canonical
   block hash

Both heads being live means a transient reorg on either side is
forgiven on the next tick, while the gap+canonical check prevents
declaring nodes in sync when one is far behind or on a different fork.
test: re-sample both nodes in InSyncFn

test: require slower node to catch up to initial high water mark in InSyncFn

The 10-block tolerance in InSyncFn could falsely pass when a reorg has
just happened: both nodes can sit a few blocks below the divergence
point, agree on shared pre-reorg history, and look in-sync even though
the slower node hasn't yet observed the reorg.

Sample both heads once before the retry loop and remember the higher of
the two as a catch-up target. The slower live head must reach that
target before the gap and canonical-hash checks decide convergence,
which forces both nodes to advance past where the faster node was when
the check started.

feat(alloy-op-evm): post-exec block executor and SDM warming inspector

Add the canonical post-exec block executor, along with the first
feature riding on it — SDM (Sequencer-Defined Metering) block-level
warming refunds, delivered by the SDMWarmingInspector.

- OpBlockExecutor gains three PostExecModes (Disabled / Produce /
  Verify(payload) / Invalid). Produce accumulates per-tx refund
  entries for the payload builder to append as a synthetic 0x7D tx;
  Verify validates an embedded payload against local replay;
  Disabled is the legacy path (byte-identical to pre-SDM).
- SDMWarmingInspector tracks first-warmer provenance for accounts
  and storage slots, emits exact refund attribution events for every
  re-touch past the EIP-2929 warm threshold, and suppresses claims
  from Deposit and synthetic PostExec tx kinds.
- Verify-mode validations reject duplicate payload indexes, payload
  entries targeting deposits or the 0x7D tx itself, and refunds that
  exceed the tx's raw gas. `apply_pre_execution_changes` debug_asserts
  the Produce hooks are wired so a downstream fork can't silently drop
  refunds.
- Canonical gas settlement credits the sender, debits the beneficiary
  and base-fee recipient by the refunded-gas component of their share,
  and commits the deltas when canonical gas falls below raw gas.
- beneficiary_gas_price can legitimately saturate at zero when a
  legacy tx's gas price equals basefee; inline comment documents the
  consensus-valid zero case.

fix(op-supernode): guard chain container vn against torn interface read

Supernode.Start fires the Interop activity and chain-container goroutines
in parallel. Interop's checkChainsReady immediately calls c.OptimisticAt ->
c.SyncStatus, which reads c.vn while the chain container is concurrently
assigning it in its restart loop. A torn two-word interface read can yield
(type=*simpleVirtualNode, data=nil); the `c.vn == nil` guard returns false,
the method dispatches on a nil receiver, and v.mu.Lock() panics at offset
0x58 (the mu field inside simpleVirtualNode).

Protect c.vn with a sync.RWMutex and route all reads/writes through
getVN/setVN helpers so every method takes one consistent snapshot. Also
add nil-receiver guards on the *simpleVirtualNode methods as a defense
against typed-nil interfaces slipping through in tests or future refactors.

ci: explicitly disable circleci_ip_ranges on 4 jobs that don't need it (#20455)

Sets circleci_ip_ranges: false (rather than relying on default behavior)
on four jobs where the flag was previously set to true but the job makes
no calls to allowlisted endpoints. Being explicit about the value avoids
any ambiguity about CircleCI's default.

The flag routes a job's outbound traffic through CircleCI's 21 published
static IPs at a cost of 450 credits per GB of network data. It only
provides value if downstream infrastructure allowlists those IPs.

In OP Labs' infrastructure, the only consumer of CircleCI's IP ranges is
the ci-ip-whitelist Traefik middleware in ethereum-optimism/k8s, which
protects 15 internal CI endpoints (proxyd-l1-ci, proxyd-l1-ci-archive,
proxyd-l2-ci, beacon-api-proxy-ci, github-event-manager, plus several
proxyd-*-rpc internal-ingress routes).

These four jobs make no calls to any of those allowlisted endpoints in
their step definitions:

- contracts-bedrock-tests: runs forge test against pre-built artifacts
- contracts-bedrock-heavy-fuzz-nightly: runs just test on pre-built artifacts
- ai-contracts-test: calls Devin/Slack public APIs only
- op-acceptance-tests: runs devstack locally with workspace binaries

The four jobs that DO need the flag are not touched here:
contracts-bedrock-coverage, contracts-bedrock-tests-upgrade, and
contracts-bedrock-tests-l2-fork all hit ci-mainnet-l1-archive.optimism.io
or op-mainnet-rpc.optimism.io. go-tests sets MAINNET_RPC_URL and
SEPOLIA_RPC_URL to ci-mainnet-l1-archive.optimism.io and
ci-sepolia-l1-archive.optimism.io in the justfile recipes invoked from CI.

Estimated impact: ~50M IP-range credits saved per 30 days (~38% of
current IP-range spend).

Refs: ethereum-optimism/core-team#2366

fix(op-supernode): guard chain container vn against torn interface read (#20211)

Supernode.Start fires the Interop activity and chain-container goroutines
in parallel. Interop's checkChainsReady immediately calls c.OptimisticAt ->
c.SyncStatus, which reads c.vn while the chain container is concurrently
assigning it in its restart loop. A torn two-word interface read can yield
(type=*simpleVirtualNode, data=nil); the `c.vn == nil` guard returns false,
the method dispatches on a nil receiver, and v.mu.Lock() panics at offset
0x58 (the mu field inside simpleVirtualNode).

Protect c.vn with a sync.RWMutex and route all reads/writes through
getVN/setVN helpers so every method takes one consistent snapshot. Also
add nil-receiver guards on the *simpleVirtualNode methods as a defense
against typed-nil interfaces slipping through in tests or future refactors.

* feat(alloy-op-evm): post-exec block executor and SDM warming inspector

Add the canonical post-exec block executor, along with the first
feature riding on it — SDM (Sequencer-Defined Metering) block-level
warming refunds, delivered by the SDMWarmingInspector.

- OpBlockExecutor gains three PostExecModes (Disabled / Produce /
  Verify(payload) / Invalid). Produce accumulates per-tx refund
  entries for the payload builder to append as a synthetic 0x7D tx;
  Verify validates an embedded payload against local replay;
  Disabled is the legacy path (byte-identical to pre-SDM).
- SDMWarmingInspector tracks first-warmer provenance for accounts
  and storage slots, emits exact refund attribution events for every
  re-touch past the EIP-2929 warm threshold, and suppresses claims
  from Deposit and synthetic PostExec tx kinds.
- Verify-mode validations reject duplicate payload indexes, payload
  entries targeting deposits or the 0x7D tx itself, and refunds that
  exceed the tx's raw gas. `apply_pre_execution_changes` debug_asserts
  the Produce hooks are wired so a downstream fork can't silently drop
  refunds.
- Canonical gas settlement credits the sender, debits the beneficiary
  and base-fee recipient by the refunded-gas component of their share,
  and commits the deltas when canonical gas falls below raw gas.
- beneficiary_gas_price can legitimately saturate at zero when a
  legacy tx's gas price equals basefee; inline comment documents the
  consensus-valid zero case.

* feat(kona-registry): embed DEPENDENCY_SETS, derived from superchain interop blocks

Introduce kona_registry::DEPENDENCY_SETS, a HashMap<u64, DependencySet> keyed by
L2 chain id, populated at compile time from etc/depsets.json. The build script
resets the file to [] on every build, derives per-cluster DependencySets from
each chain TOML's [interop.dependencies] block under KONA_BIND, and merges any
KONA_CUSTOM_CONFIGS_DIR/depsets.json on top with cross-cluster collision
detection. validate_depsets catches dangling chain id references at build
time. Disjoint clusters (e.g. mainnet, sepolia, rehearsal-0-bn) stay disjoint:
each cluster's chains map to that cluster's DependencySet, never a union.

fixture.

* fix(kona-proof-interop): load DependencySet from registry first, oracle fallback

BootInfo::load now consults kona_registry::DEPENDENCY_SETS before the preimage
oracle, matching the existing embedded-first pattern for rollup_configs and
l1_config. The on-chain PreimageOracle cannot supply DEPENDENCY_SET_KEY data,
so the previous oracle-only path could not complete a real fault proof once
interop is active.

The lookup is extracted into load_dependency_set so it is unit-testable.
When the proof's chain ids span two embedded clusters, the helper returns
BootstrapError::CrossDependencySetProof rather than silently unioning them
(which would let cross-cluster messages validate). Partial coverage and empty
embedded maps fall back to the oracle, preserving existing host/test flows.

feat(interop): make autorelay retries + backoff configurable, fix dead retry path

relayMessageWithRetry was always called with maxRetries=1 at both call sites
in interop/relayer.go (lines 121, 188), so the exponential backoff in the
retry loop was dead code and any single transient destination-chain RPC
failure dropped a cross-chain message permanently.

This patch:
- Adds --interop.autorelay.retries (default 3) and --interop.autorelay.retry.backoff.max
  (default 8s) flags, plumbed through CLIConfig.
- Threads them into NewL2ToL2MessageRelayer(logger, maxRetries, backoffMax)
  so the indexer-driven and waiting-pool relay paths both use r.maxRetries.
- Caps the time.Sleep(1<<attempt) backoff at retryBackoffMax to prevent
  unbounded sleep on long retry counts.
- Defaults are conservative (3 attempts, 8s cap) so existing users see
  improved liveness on transient RPC blips without behavioral surprise.
  Setting --interop.autorelay.retries=1 reproduces the prior no-retry behavior.

fix(op-reth): wait for proofs ExEx store before validator eth_getProof

FetchAndVerifyProofs queries the validator (op-reth) via eth_getProof,
which reads through OpStateProviderFactory backed by the proofs ExEx
store. The ExEx ingests ChainCommitted notifications asynchronously,

fix(supernode): VerifiedRequiredL1 takes MAX of per-chain L1s

Resolves ethereum-optimism/optimism#20481. Superroot.atTimestamp
tracked the MIN of per-chain VerifiedAt L1 blocks, which contradicts
the field's semantics: VerifiedRequiredL1 should be "the minimum L1
block including the required data to fully verify all blocks at this
timestamp" — that requires the MAX of per-chain required L1s.

With MIN, when only one chain's data was on L1 at a given L1 head, the
boundary super root falsely looked "fully verified" so the challenger's
trace provider returned SuperRoot(boundary) instead of cascading to
InvalidTransition, producing a real challenger / FPP disagreement at
trace idx 2*stepsPerTimestamp - 1.

Also unskips the two AfterChainHead subtests that worked around this
bug (DisputeTimestampAfterChainHeadConsolidate-challenger,
DisputeBlockAfterChainHead-FirstChain-challenger) and removes the
SkipChallenger field on transitionTest (now unused).

and RunVariedBlockTimesTest with deterministic block production via

AgreedBlockAfterChainHead*).

    freezeChains(chains)                            // stop real sequencers + batchers, WaitForStall
    endTimestamp := nextTimestampAfterSafeHeads(t, chains)
    advanceUnsafeToTimestamp(t, sys, chains, endTimestamp)

    advanceSafeToCurrentUnsafe(t, chains[0]); capture l1HeadAfterFirst

fix(op-acceptance): anchor after-chain-head tests on settled state

Fixes a flake in tests 5/6 of the AfterChainHead suite (added in #20349)
that hard-coded `endTimestamp + 3` and `+ 4` as guaranteed-no-block
timestamps. Under CI scheduling delays the freeze choreography never
actually bounded chain[1]'s unsafe head — chain[1] could be 30+ blocks
ahead of chain[0] by the time the batcher restarted, the boundary
batcher submitted everything in the unsafe queue (Reached has ">=" not
"==" semantics), and the supernode then returned real transition states
at the timestamps tests 5/6 assumed were unreachable.

This change reverts Stage 1 / Stage 2 of `RunSuperFaultProofTest` and
`RunVariedBlockTimesTest` to develop's batcher-only choreography
(no `StopSequencer`, no unsafe-head-derived endTimestamp, no
`Reached(eth.Unsafe, ...)` removal) and replaces Stage 2b with a
deterministic freeze-and-measure step:

  1. Wait for boundaryTimestamp to be on every chain's LocalSafe so
     `optimisticBlockAtTimestamp(boundary)` is well-defined for tests
     1-4 (a no-op for chains where TargetBlockNumber rounds boundary
     down to endTimestamp's block).
  2. AwaitValidatedTimestamp(boundary), capture l1HeadAdvanced.
  3. Stop both batchers, then both sequencers, then WaitForStall on
     both LocalUnsafe and LocalSafe for every chain. The wait-for-stalls
     absorb arbitrary scheduling pauses (each requires >=10s of stable
     head with a 2-min budget).
  4. Read each chain's settled UnsafeL2 timestamp and pick
     `ttest = max(settled) + margin`. Sequencers are stopped, so no
     chain can produce more blocks; ttest stays past every chain's head
     forever, regardless of any further pause.

`buildAfterChainHeadTests` now takes ttest and computes tests 5/6's
trace indices from it (consolidation at ttest, optimistic toward
ttest+1) rather than baking in `endTimestamp + 3 / + 4`. The new tests
cannot fail under any plausible scheduling delay.

The diff vs develop is pure addition (no Stage 1 / Stage 2 lines
removed): one new helper (`freezeAndMeasure`), one new helper
(`isOptimisticNotDerivable`), the `buildAfterChainHeadTests` block,
and a single Stage 2b call in each Run* function.

fix(op-acceptance): derive after-chain-head claimTimestamp from ttest

The previous patch added a `Require().Lessf(ttest+1, endTimestamp+100)`
assert as a defensive guard. That assert is the wrong fix — it converts
the original race (chain overshoots far enough to push ttest past
claimTimestamp) into a louder failure mode rather than removing it.
Option 1's principle is "measure, don't assume", which has to apply to
every timestamp the new tests depend on, including claimTimestamp.

This change derives claimTimestamp from ttest:
    claimTimestamp = ttest + claimBuffer (= 5)
so the trace window always covers consolidateAfterHeadIdx (timestamp
ttest) and optimisticAfterHeadIdx (timestamp ttest+1) regardless of
how far past endTimestamp the chains overshot before the freeze.

Trace size = (claimTimestamp - startTimestamp) * stepsPerTimestamp.
With claimTimestamp ≈ endTimestamp + 8 in the common case (and well
under endTimestamp + 130 even under extreme overshoot), the trace stays
far below 2^gameDepth (deployer default DisputeSplitDepth = 30 → 2^30
slots vs ~12k actually used), so there is no risk of running out of
trace addresses.

Also drops the `afterChainHeadClaimTimestampOffset` constant (only
existed so the assert could see the same value as the test build) and
softens the margin comment to reflect that block times are chosen by
us, not arbitrary.

The `just test` recipe used `{{args}}` (textual interpolation), which
re-tokenizes args via the shell and breaks any quoting. Passing a -run

token" because those characters were exposed to bash without the

checks) so args reach `go test` exactly as the caller passed them.

fix(supernode): VerifiedRequiredL1 takes MAX of per-chain L1s

Resolves ethereum-optimism/optimism#20481. Superroot.atTimestamp
tracked the MIN of per-chain VerifiedAt L1 blocks, which contradicts
the field's semantics: VerifiedRequiredL1 should be "the minimum L1
block including the required data to fully verify all blocks at this
timestamp" — that requires the MAX of per-chain required L1s.

With MIN, when only one chain's data was on L1 at a given L1 head, the
boundary super root falsely looked "fully verified" so the challenger's
trace provider returned SuperRoot(boundary) instead of cascading to
InvalidTransition, producing a real challenger / FPP disagreement at
trace idx 2*stepsPerTimestamp - 1.

Also unskips the two AfterChainHead subtests that worked around this
bug (DisputeTimestampAfterChainHeadConsolidate-challenger,
DisputeBlockAfterChainHead-FirstChain-challenger) and removes the
SkipChallenger field on transitionTest (now unused).

and RunVariedBlockTimesTest with deterministic block production via
TestSequencer.SequenceBlock, and adds the 6 AfterChainHead subtests
(DisputeTimestampAfterChainHead*, DisputeBlockAfterChainHead*,
AgreedBlockAfterChainHead*).

Setup:

    freezeChains(chains)                            // stop real sequencers + batchers, WaitForStall
    endTimestamp := nextTimestampAfterSafeHeads(t, chains)
    advanceUnsafeToTimestamp(t, sys, chains, endTimestamp)
    capture l1HeadBefore
    advanceSafeToCurrentUnsafe(t, chains[0]); capture l1HeadAfterFirst
    advanceSafeToCurrentUnsafe(t, chains[1]); capture l1HeadCurrent
    AwaitValidatedTimestamp(endTimestamp)
    extendChainsExpectingBoundaryBlock(t, sys, chains, endTimestamp+1)
    build*Tests + buildAfterChainHeadTests

LocalUnsafe + LocalSafe to stall on every chain. From there, only
TestSequencer.SequenceBlock advances UnsafeL2 and only explicit
Batcher.Start/Stop advances LocalSafe.

Per-config branching in buildAfterChainHeadTests is keyed off block-time
inference (blockExpectedAt) rather than runtime supernode probing.

tests: add InSync check for advancing heads

Made-with: Cursor
tests: add InSync check for advancing heads

test: re-sample both nodes in InSyncFn

The previous InSyncFn snapshotted the reference head once at the start
of the check and then waited up to N attempts for the base node to
incorporate that exact block. In reorg-recovery tests the reference
node can briefly hold an unsafe block that is later reorged out by the
sequencer, which left InSyncFn permanently stuck against a stale target
(see TestFollowL2_ReorgRecovery).

Re-sample both nodes on every attempt and consider them in sync when:
1. the two head numbers differ by at most maxInSyncGap blocks
2. at the lower of the two heights, both nodes agree on the canonical
   block hash

Both heads being live means a transient reorg on either side is
forgiven on the next tick, while the gap+canonical check prevents
declaring nodes in sync when one is far behind or on a different fork.
test: re-sample both nodes in InSyncFn

test: require slower node to catch up to initial high water mark in InSyncFn

The 10-block tolerance in InSyncFn could falsely pass when a reorg has
just happened: both nodes can sit a few blocks below the divergence
point, agree on shared pre-reorg history, and look in-sync even though
the slower node hasn't yet observed the reorg.

Sample both heads once before the retry loop and remember the higher of
the two as a catch-up target. The slower live head must reach that
target before the gap and canonical-hash checks decide convergence,
which forces both nodes to advance past where the faster node was when
the check started.

test: tighten InSyncFn gap tolerance to 5 blocks

10 blocks (~20s of L2 progression at 2s block time) was generously
permissive. 5 is enough to absorb sample-to-sample timing variance
between the two nodes while keeping the in-sync window tight.
test: tighten InSyncFn gap tolerance to 5 blocks

test: treat InSyncFn arguments as peers

The two nodes passed to InSyncFn play symmetric roles, so name them
node1/node2 and update the wrapper parameters to other. Fold the
lower/higher/gap derivation into a single if-block.

Replaces the python:3.12-slim-bookworm Dockerfile with a declarative
apko + melange build using upstream Wolfi packages and the
factory/.github/workflows/apko.yaml reusable workflow.

Project changes
- Move flat-file Python modules into a proper op_conductor_ops/
  package directory; convert sibling imports to relative.
- Wrap the typer entrypoint in a main() function so it can be
  registered as a [tool.poetry.scripts] entry.

  declare packages, and register the op-conductor-ops console script
  pointing at op_conductor_ops.cli:main.
- Drop the legacy shell launcher that ran `poetry install` at
  container startup. apko-built images install everything at build
  time.

Build changes
- Add op-conductor-ops/melange.yaml. One pipeline step:
  uses: python/build-wheel. The PEP 517 frontend reads pyproject.toml
  and invokes poetry-core to produce a wheel. The runtime closure
  is declared via Wolfi apk names mirroring [tool.poetry.dependencies].
- Add op-conductor-ops/apko/op-conductor-ops.apko.yaml. Pulls
  wolfi-baselayout, ca-certificates-bundle, tzdata, and the melange-
  produced op-conductor-ops apk. Runs as uid 65532 (non-root).
- Update .github/images.json: add op-conductor-ops as a `groups`
  entry (mode: apko, services: [op-conductor-ops]) and remove it
  from the Dockerfile-mode `images` map.
- Update branches.yaml + tags.yaml: replace the legacy
  detect-changes / parse-tag actions with factory/actions/plan and
  add a job that calls factory/.github/workflows/apko.yaml for the

refactor(op-service/sources): minimal-fetch path for L2BlockRef and SystemConfig

L2Client.L2BlockRefBy{Label,Number,Hash} and SystemConfigByL2Hash used to
fetch the entire L2 block (eth_getBlockByX with fullTx=true) only to read a
handful of header fields and decode the first transaction (the L1 info
deposit). For large blocks this can waste >99% of bandwidth and CPU.

Add a minimal-fetch path that downloads only the header (fullTx=false) and
the first transaction in a single batched JSON-RPC round trip, with
optimistic consistency checking and a small extra retry on label/number
race.

- New eth.PayloadToInfo wrapper makes *ExecutionPayload satisfy BlockInfo.
- New derive helpers BlockRefFromHeaderAndDeposit and
  SystemConfigFromHeaderAndDeposit operate on (eth.BlockInfo, *deposit-tx).
  Existing PayloadTo{BlockRef,SystemConfig} become thin wrappers.
- New EthClient.HeaderAndFirstTx batches eth_getBlockByX(false) +
  eth_getTransactionByBlockXAndIndex(0). On non-by-hash paths, verifies
  header.Transactions[0] == tx.Hash() and refetches the tx by header hash on
  mismatch; on by-hash paths the consistency check is skipped (the tx call
  is bound to a definite hash). Caches (header, deposit) by block hash for
  reuse across L2BlockRefByHash and SystemConfigByL2Hash, which routinely
  hit the same hash in the engine + attributes-builder path.
- New RPCHeaderWithTxHashes type to decode the fullTx=false response with
  transaction hashes for the consistency check.
- L2Client adapters rewritten: PayloadByX → HeaderAndFirstTx →
  derive.BlockRefFromHeaderAndDeposit / SystemConfigFromHeaderAndDeposit.
  Existing per-result caches (l2BlockRefsCache, systemConfigsCache)
  unchanged.

fix(kona-proof): decode EIP-2935 storage slot value as U256

The EIP-2935 history lookup decoded the storage slot leaf as B256,
which expects exactly 32 bytes of RLP payload. Ethereum stores storage
values as RLP-encoded U256 with leading zero bytes stripped — so any
block hash whose high byte is 0x00 (~1/256 of all hashes) encodes to
fewer than 32 bytes and fails to decode with RlpError::UnexpectedLength.

Decode as U256 and reconstruct the 32-byte hash, matching the pattern
already used by TrieDB::storage in kona-executor. Update the test mock
to mirror real-chain encoding and add a regression case for a hash
with a leading zero byte.

fix(op-challenger): route super-cannon-kona to KonaSuperExecutor in run-trace

The runner factory dispatched both CannonKonaGameType and
SuperCannonKonaGameType through vm.NewKonaExecutor(). The single-chain
KonaExecutor emits the kona host `single` subcommand, requires exactly
one entry in cfg.L2s, reads inputs.L2Head / inputs.L2OutputRoot, and
ignores inputs.AgreedPreState - none of which match the super-state
inputs createGameInputsInterop produces. The result was a kona-host
command with zero L2 head hashes that could never reach a successful
output-root verification.

fix(kona-proof): decode EIP-2935 storage slot value as U256 (#20518)

The EIP-2935 history lookup decoded the storage slot leaf as B256,
which expects exactly 32 bytes of RLP payload. Ethereum stores storage
values as RLP-encoded U256 with leading zero bytes stripped — so any
block hash whose high byte is 0x00 (~1/256 of all hashes) encodes to
fewer than 32 bytes and fails to decode with RlpError::UnexpectedLength.

Decode as U256 and reconstruct the 32-byte hash, matching the pattern
already used by TrieDB::storage in kona-executor. Update the test mock
to mirror real-chain encoding and add a regression case for a hash
with a leading zero byte.

fix(supernode): VerifiedRequiredL1 takes MAX of per-chain L1s (#20484)

Resolves ethereum-optimism/optimism#20481. Superroot.atTimestamp
tracked the MIN of per-chain VerifiedAt L1 blocks, which contradicts
the field's semantics: VerifiedRequiredL1 should be "the minimum L1
block including the required data to fully verify all blocks at this
timestamp" — that requires the MAX of per-chain required L1s.

With MIN, when only one chain's data was on L1 at a given L1 head, the
boundary super root falsely looked "fully verified" so the challenger's
trace provider returned SuperRoot(boundary) instead of cascading to
InvalidTransition, producing a real challenger / FPP disagreement at
trace idx 2*stepsPerTimestamp - 1.

Also unskips the two AfterChainHead subtests that worked around this
bug (DisputeTimestampAfterChainHeadConsolidate-challenger,
DisputeBlockAfterChainHead-FirstChain-challenger) and removes the
SkipChallenger field on transitionTest (now unused).

fix(op-node): record effective safe/finalized metrics in supernode mode

In supernode mode, SafeL2Head() and FinalizedHead() consult the
superAuthority (interop verifiers) and return values that may differ
from localSafeHead/localFinalizedHead. The metrics recorded in
SetDeprecatedSafeHead/SetFinalizedHead only capture the local values,
causing the l2_safe and l2_finalized Prometheus gauges to diverge from
what the API and logs report.

This is most visible during catchup: the superAuthority-derived
finalized head advances as verifiers make progress, but
promoteFinalized() cannot call SetFinalizedHead() because its proposed
ref is behind FinalizedHead() (which already reflects the verifier
value). The metric stays stuck at genesis while the API correctly
reports advancing blocks.

Fix: record the effective safe/finalized refs in
requestForkchoiceUpdate(), which is where these values are published
to the event system. The gauge overwrite is a no-op for standalone
op-node (where local and effective values are identical) and only
changes behavior in supernode mode during catchup.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(kona-interop): guard executing chain against interop activation block

`MessageGraph::check_single_dependency` only enforces the interop
activation invariant on the initiating chain. The interop spec forbids
executing messages in any chain's activation block, and op-supervisor's
`LinkCheckerImpl.CanExecute` and op-program's consolidation enforce both
sides. Without the executing-side guard, kona-client accepts
exec-message-in-activation-block while op-program rejects it, producing
divergent post-states from the same agreed pre-state at the dispute
boundary.

This adds the missing guard, mirroring op-supervisor's structure
(`op-supervisor/supervisor/backend/depset/links.go:43,47-48`):

if !exec_cfg.is_interop_active(t) || exec_cfg.is_first_interop_block(t)

Surfaced as a new `MessageGraphError::ExecutedTooEarly` variant,
symmetric to the existing `InitiatedTooEarly`. Three tests cover:
activation set well in the future, unaligned activation that lands the
first block on the activation timestamp, and aligned activation at the
local-safe head.

op-supernode: under-claim i.currentL1 by one L1 block on Advance

After DecisionAdvance(T_v), i.currentL1 was set to L1Inclusion(T_v) — the
max L1 source across chains at T_v. This over-claims: L1Inclusion is
monotonic, so the next unverified ts T_v+1 can have the same L1Inclusion
when no chain advanced its L1 source between T_v and T_v+1 (the common
case during the gap between batch postings, which can be hours apart).

A consumer relying on aggregate.CurrentL1 ≥ s.l1Head as proof that
everything derivable from L1[≤s.l1Head] is verified is then lied to
whenever s.l1Head == L1Inclusion(T_v): an unverified T_v+1 also lives
at that L1, per-chain reads can return Data == nil, and the gate still
passes — leading op-challenger to play InvalidTransition for a ts whose
canonical answer is a SuperRoot.

Under-claim by one L1 block: i.currentL1 = L1Inclusion(T_v) - 1 with
the parent block's hash from the L1 source. The aggregate gate then
fails for queries at the offending ts and the consumer correctly
retries. Liveness: stalls only inside a constant-L1Inclusion run; the
existing DecisionWait branch's refreshCurrentL1OnWait lifts i.currentL1
back to localL1 between Advances, so dispute-game progress is bounded
by L2 block production cadence (seconds), never by batch-posting
cadence (hours).

L1 hash is best-effort: if the l1Source lookup fails, we fall back to
a hash-less BlockID with the under-claimed Number. Current consumers
(op-challenger gate uses .Number only; op-proposer logs .Hash) tolerate
a zero hash. At L1 genesis (Number == 0) there is nothing earlier, so
the result is reported unchanged.

op-supernode: detect VN restart / RewindEngine during superroot gather

simpleChainContainer gains a generation counter (c.gen) bumped on every
state transition that could make data gathered earlier inconsistent with
state observed later: a new virtual node being installed (setVN) and entry
to RewindEngine. GatherSuperRootData captures c.gen at the start of its
work and re-reads it after all reads complete; if it changed in between,
the reads have straddled pre- and post-mutation state and ChainSuperRootData
is discarded with ErrInconsistentSnapshot — the caller can retry on the
next polling tick.

Inner-pipeline rollup.ResetEvent paths (channel decode, blob data fetch
failure, attribute mismatch, finalizer divergence, etc.) don't currently
go through either site and therefore aren't caught by this counter; that
wiring is a follow-up.

op-node,op-supernode: surface pipeline resets to the supernode's gen counter

The chain container's generation counter (introduced in the previous
commit) only bumps on setVN and RewindEngine, so a superroot_atTimestamp
gather running while the inner derivation pipeline emits rollup.ResetEvent
for any non-RewindEngine reason — channel decode error, blob fetch failure,
attribute mismatch, finalizer divergence, BlockInsertPrestateErr, batch
invariant violation, SafeHeadUpdated I/O failure — would not detect that
the engine had been forceReset and SafeDB possibly truncated.

Add an OnPipelineReset callback to InitializationOverrides, plumb it
through driver.NewDriver to status.NewStatusTracker, and invoke it from
the existing rollup.ResetEvent arm in StatusTracker.OnEvent. The chain
container installs the callback in its Start loop — alongside the existing
MetricsRegistry and SuperAuthority assignments — to bump c.gen on every

refactor(op-service/sources): minimal-fetch path for L2BlockRef and SystemConfig

L2Client.L2BlockRefBy{Label,Number,Hash} and SystemConfigByL2Hash used to
fetch the entire L2 block (eth_getBlockByX with fullTx=true) only to read a
handful of header fields and decode the first transaction (the L1 info
deposit). For large blocks this can waste >99% of bandwidth and CPU.

Add a minimal-fetch path that downloads only the header (fullTx=false) and
the first transaction in a single batched JSON-RPC round trip, with
optimistic consistency checking and a small extra retry on label/number
race.

- New eth.PayloadToInfo wrapper makes *ExecutionPayload satisfy BlockInfo.
- New derive helpers BlockRefFromHeaderAndDeposit and
  SystemConfigFromHeaderAndDeposit operate on (eth.BlockInfo, *deposit-tx).
  Existing PayloadTo{BlockRef,SystemConfig} become thin wrappers.
- New EthClient.HeaderAndFirstTx batches eth_getBlockByX(false) +
  eth_getTransactionByBlockXAndIndex(0). On non-by-hash paths, verifies
  header.Transactions[0] == tx.Hash() and refetches the tx by header hash on
  mismatch; on by-hash paths the consistency check is skipped (the tx call
  is bound to a definite hash). Caches (header, deposit) by block hash for
  reuse across L2BlockRefByHash and SystemConfigByL2Hash, which routinely
  hit the same hash in the engine + attributes-builder path.
- New RPCHeaderWithTxHashes type to decode the fullTx=false response with
  transaction hashes for the consistency check.
- L2Client adapters rewritten: PayloadByX → HeaderAndFirstTx →
  derive.BlockRefFromHeaderAndDeposit / SystemConfigFromHeaderAndDeposit.
  Existing per-result caches (l2BlockRefsCache, systemConfigsCache)
  unchanged.

eth_getBlockByNumber returns JSON null for labels like "finalized" before any
L2 block has finalized, and for unknown numbers/hashes. The previous payloadCall
path used a pointer result (*RPCBlock) so a null decoded to nil and the
caller correctly returned ethereum.NotFound, which op-node sync/start.go relies
on to fall back to the genesis block.

post-merge / hash-consistency checks with confusing errors. In the supernode,
this fired on every sync_deriver tick across multiple chains and exhausted
CircleCI's 50 MB log cap.

ethereum.NotFound when the decoder leaves it nil. Mirrors the existing
headerCall semantics.

fix(op-service/sources): retry on nil first-tx in HeaderAndFirstTx batch

The batched call (getBlockByX(false) + getTransactionByBlockXAndIndex(0))
breaks atomicity that the old fullTx=true path provided: under derivation
pressure the EL has been observed to return a header with non-empty
transaction hashes for the first call while returning null for the second
in the same batch. The error surfaced as derivation getting stuck in CI
(`memory-all-opn-op-geth` job, sync_tester_hfs test): "failed to determine
SystemConfig of hash 0x...: l2 block first tx fetch returned nil".

Treat firstTx == nil while header.Transactions[0] is set as a transient
and retry the tx fetch by hash, the same retry path the consistency-check
mismatch already uses on label/number queries. The retry is by
eth_getTransactionByBlockHashAndIndex(rpcHdr.Hash, 0) — guaranteed
deterministic since rpcHdr.Hash is now known and verified.

Adds TestEthClient_HeaderAndFirstTx_ByHash_FirstTxNilRetry as a regression
guard.

activation invariant on the initiating chain. The interop spec forbids
executing messages in any chain's activation block, and op-supervisor's
`LinkCheckerImpl.CanExecute` and op-program's consolidation enforce both
sides. Without the executing-side guard, kona-client accepts
exec-message-in-activation-block while op-program rejects it, producing
divergent post-states from the same agreed pre-state at the dispute
boundary.

(`op-supervisor/supervisor/backend/depset/links.go:43,47-48`):

if !exec_cfg.is_interop_active(t) || exec_cfg.is_first_interop_block(t)

symmetric to the existing `InitiatedTooEarly`. Three tests cover:
activation set well in the future, unaligned activation that lands the
first block on the activation timestamp, and aligned activation at the
local-safe head.

ci(op-reth): use fast-build profile in PR docker bake (#20543)

Override BUILD_PROFILE for the op-reth bake target to fast-build on
pull_request events; keep maxperf for pushes to develop, scheduled
builds, and tags.

maxperf uses lto = "fat" and codegen-units = 1, which serializes the
final link and dominates op-reth build time. The fast-build profile
(defined in rust/Cargo.toml) uses opt-level = 0, codegen-units = 256
and incremental = true, dropping the link bottleneck and parallelizing
codegen.

unaffected, since branches.yaml has no merge_group trigger today.

fix(op-acceptance-tests): make freezeChains return with safe == unsafe

freezeChains stopped sequencers and batchers in parallel and only waited
for LocalUnsafe and LocalSafe to each individually stall. WaitForStall does
not imply LocalSafe == LocalUnsafe: if the batcher stopped before draining
the most recent unsafe blocks, safe ended up behind unsafe.

nextTimestampAfterSafeHeads then computed endTimestamp from the safe head,
so startTimestamp = endTimestamp - 1 could land before the chain's current
unsafe head time, and advanceUnsafeToTimestamp would fail with
"head is already past target". The race window scales with block time and
hit the 1s chain in TestPreinteropFaultProofs_VariedBlockTimes intermittently.

Fix the contract instead of the consumer: reorder freezeChains so it stops
sequencers first, waits for LocalUnsafe to stall, lets the still-running
batchers drain remaining unsafe blocks until LocalSafe catches up to
LocalUnsafe, and only then stops the batchers. nextTimestampAfterSafeHeads
is correct as named once safe == unsafe on entry.

op-supernode: serve OptimisticAtTimestamp from durable state

Snapshot per-chain optimistic observations into the verified DB so
superroot_atTimestamp can answer OptimisticAtTimestamp without re-reading
live SafeDB or engine state. Without this, a chain rewind between the
verifier observing a chain and the RPC being served could drop derivable
optimistic blocks from the response.

VerifiedRecord now stores per-chain ChainObservation (L2 head, per-chain
L1 inclusion, OutputV0 preimage). Aggregate L1Inclusion and per-chain
output roots are derived on demand. DenyRecord and InvalidHead also gain
a per-chain L1Inclusion field captured at decision time, so OptimisticAt
for invalidated blocks can be reconstructed from durable state too.

The reader prefers stored snapshots and overlays denylist entries on top
to preserve the pre-existing semantics that OptimisticAtTimestamp
returns the originally-observed block, not the post-consolidation
replacement. Falls back to live state for pre-verification timestamps.

CurrentL1 in the response now comes from the verifier's durable
frontier (Interop.VerifierCurrentL1), advanced every Wait round so it
tracks live L1 progress within a few blocks even between L2 batches.
This is what op-challenger needs to know whether the game's L1 head has
been fully processed.

state for in-flight (post-activation, pre-commit) timestamps without a
live SafeDB read.

The verifier replaces a single (timestamp, per-chain ChainObservation)
snapshot atomically each round in checkChainsReady. Replacement —
including dropping chains that previously had a block but no longer do —
is what closes the rewind race against the RPC: a chain that rewound
between the round's CurrentL1 advance and a later RPC call cannot leak
stale observations into the response.

checkChainsReady now returns partial results plus an allReady bool.
NotFound from a chain is no longer a fatal error from the verifier's
loop; the round is treated as Wait and the partial snapshot is still
persisted so the challenger can serve per-chain partial visibility
(needed to identify which chain's optimistic step is the
InvalidTransition boundary). The startup readyFirstVerifiableTimestamp
helper still surfaces NotFound when not every chain is ready.

Live fallback in superroot.go now applies only when the verifier is not
responsible for the timestamp (no provider configured, or the timestamp
is pre-activation). Post-activation, both Data and OptimisticAtTimestamp
come exclusively from durable state, making CurrentL1 >= game.L1Head a
sufficient guarantee that the challenger only acts on durable data.

Snapshot is cleared on rewind so post-rewind queries cannot return
stale observations.

fix(kona/protocol): reject invalid is_last byte in frame decode

Per the OP Stack derivation spec, the trailing `is_last` byte of a frame
must be 0 or 1; any other value makes the frame invalid and the entire
batcher transaction's frames must be rejected. op-node enforces this in
`Frame.UnmarshalBinary`, but kona's `Frame::decode` was treating
`is_last` as `(byte == 1)`, silently coercing values like 2 to `false`.

This created a parsing divergence: op-node would reject a malformed
batcher transaction while kona would accept it, with the potential to
yield different L2 derivation outputs in a hybrid Go-node + Rust
fault-proof setup.

Add a new `FrameDecodingError::InvalidIsLast(u8)` variant and reject any
non-{0,1} byte in `Frame::decode`. Mirrors op-node's
`TestFrameUnmarshalInvalidIsLast`.

Fixes ethereum-optimism/optimism#19335

fix(op-supervisor): fsync logs DB at seal and truncate boundaries

Adds durability across crashes for the supervisor logs DB.

EntryDB.Truncate now fsyncs before returning. Truncate is a metadata
change with no semantically valid non-durable form: every existing
caller (Rewind, Clear, the rollback path inside Append, and the
cleanupFailedWrite retry) wants the file size change to survive a
crash. Folding the sync into Truncate removes a class of mistakes
where callers Truncate and forget to follow up.

EntryStore gains a Sync method for callers that need to commit a
durability boundary after Append. The logs DB threads a sync flag
through flush: SealBlock calls flush(true) to make a sealed block's
entries durable, AddLog calls flush(false) because logs in unsealed
blocks are re-derivable from chain receipts on restart.

The cost is one fsync per L2 block seal plus one fsync per Rewind or
Clear (rare). AddLog is unchanged in the hot path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(op-supervisor): acquire rwLock in logs DB Clear

Clear was the only mutator on the logs DB that did not take db.rwLock.
SealBlock, AddLog, and Rewind all hold the write lock for the duration
of their mutations; Clear's truncation of the underlying store could
race with in-flight readers and other writers. The reads.Invalidator
prevents new reads from starting but does not block in-flight readers
or concurrent mutators, so the lock is still required.

Extract the body into an unlocked clear helper so Rewind, which already
holds the write lock, can call it without re-entering rwLock.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix(op-supervisor): acquire rwLock in logs DB Clear

fix(op-supervisor): make logs DB Rewind validate before truncating

Rewind previously truncated the entry store and then called init to
rehydrate the in-memory logContext. If init returned an error, disk
was already truncated while lastEntryContext retained its pre-rewind
value, leaving the running process serving a stale head until the
next successful operation or a restart.

The iterator returned by newIteratorAt has already walked from a
search checkpoint up to and through newHead's seal, so iter.current
is the hydrated post-rewind logContext. Hydration is now done before
any disk mutation: validate via the iterator, truncate (the only
mutation), assign iter.current. If truncate fails, both disk and
memory remain consistent.

Adds TestRewind subtests covering the failure-path invariants:
hash-conflict leaves state untouched, head identity is preserved
across a checkpoint-crossing rewind, no-op rewind to the current
head, and chained rewinds with writes between them. Each runs
through both fresh-DB and close+reopen variants.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(op-interop-filter): validate earliest block on resume

findAndSetEarliestBlock previously stored first.Number+1 as the earliest
queryable block without verifying that block actually had log data. Two
states could mislabel an unqueryable block as queryable: the DB
containing only the anchor (process killed between sealParentBlock and
the first ingestBlock), or an unexpected DB state with sealed blocks
past the anchor that fail to open.

In addition, GetExecMsgsAtTimestamp conflated "uninitialized" with
"before earliest" — both returned (nil, nil), so a query for a sealed
anchor while no blocks had been ingested yet would silently report "no
executing messages" instead of surfacing that the filter wasn't ready.

Now, on resume:
- If only the anchor is sealed, leave earliestIngestedBlockSet false and
  let ingestBlock set it on the first successful ingestion (matching
  the fresh-start path).
- If blocks past the anchor are sealed, verify with OpenBlock and refuse
  to start if it fails — the DB is in an unexpected state we should not
  serve queries from.

GetExecMsgsAtTimestamp now returns ErrUninitialized when the lower
bound is unset, distinct from the (nil, nil) "before earliest" case.

Addresses RV audit finding (medium): unchecked edge cases in
findAndSetEarliestBlock.

`OracleL1ChainProvider::block_info_by_number` previously walked from

fix(op-devstack): add WithoutHonestProposer preset option for challenger tests (#20575)

* fix(op-devstack): add WithoutHonestProposer preset option for challenger tests

The DSL helper StartSuperCannonKonaGame computes the synthetic honest
root claim as keccak256(extraData), which is byte-for-byte identical to
the canonical super root the in-process op-proposer submits for the
same safe timestamp (op-service/eth/super_root.go:33-36). Because the
factory UUID is keccak256(gameType, rootClaim, extraData), the test and
the proposer can race to create games with identical UUIDs at the same
safe timestamp, causing one of them to revert with GameAlreadyExists.
The race is intermittent because it only triggers when the L2 safe head
has not advanced between the proposer's most recent proposal and the
test's safeTimestamp() query.

Tests that don't actually exercise proposer behaviour shouldn't be
running an honest proposer at all. Add WithoutHonestProposer() so such
tests can opt out cleanly. The option threads a SkipHonestProposer flag
through PresetConfig into the proofs setup paths in
op-devstack/sysgo/multichain_proofs.go (attachSuperChallengerAndProposer
and attachSupervisorSuperProofs); when set, startSuperProposer is
skipped entirely.

Apply the option to the three challenger_test.go tests in
op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/proofs that don't depend on the
proposer:

- TestChallengerRespondsToMultipleInvalidClaims (the flaky one)
- TestChallengerRespondsToMultipleInvalidClaimsEOA (same race)
- TestChallengerPlaysGame (already collision-immune via WithSuperRootFrom,

TestProposer and TestSuperRootWithdrawal continue to run with the

fix(op-acceptance-tests): make freezeChains return with safe == unsafe (#20580)

freezeChains stopped sequencers and batchers in parallel and only waited
for LocalUnsafe and LocalSafe to each individually stall. WaitForStall does
not imply LocalSafe == LocalUnsafe: if the batcher stopped before draining
the most recent unsafe blocks, safe ended up behind unsafe.

nextTimestampAfterSafeHeads then computed endTimestamp from the safe head,
so startTimestamp = endTimestamp - 1 could land before the chain's current
unsafe head time, and advanceUnsafeToTimestamp would fail with
"head is already past target". The race window scales with block time and
hit the 1s chain in TestPreinteropFaultProofs_VariedBlockTimes intermittently.

Fix the contract instead of the consumer: reorder freezeChains so it stops
sequencers first, waits for LocalUnsafe to stall, lets the still-running
batchers drain remaining unsafe blocks until LocalSafe catches up to
LocalUnsafe, and only then stops the batchers. nextTimestampAfterSafeHeads
is correct as named once safe == unsafe on entry.

Fixes ethereum-optimism/optimism#19804

transaction-data size exceeds `params.MaxBlockSize` (8 MiB). Tx data

`LatestBlockFetcher` interface (just `InfoAndTxsByLabel`). The
acceptance test passes `apis.EthClient` directly; the CLI provides a
small adapter around `*ethclient.Client` that maps `Unsafe` →

fix(kona/node-service): tolerate transient get_logs errors at L1 head

The L1 watcher's `head_stream.next()` → `get_logs(filter.select(head.hash))`
sequence is racy on chains with rapid head reorgs or load-balanced RPC
endpoints with propagation lag: the head hash can disappear from the
responding node between the two calls. The upstream returns
`-32001 block not found`, the `?` propagates it as
`L1WatcherActorError::Transport`, the actor task returns Err and gets
dropped — closing `block_signer_sender` (an `mpsc::Sender<Address>`)
which is the producer side of `NetworkActor.signer`. The network actor
then logs "Found no unsafe block signer on receive" and itself returns
`ChannelClosed`. JoinSet observes both errors; the rollup_node task
collector reports the first as `Critical error in sub-routine`.

Demote the `get_logs` failure to a `warn!` + `continue`. The
SystemConfig log scan is idempotent across head ticks (an
`UnsafeBlockSigner` update is observable on any later canonical block
whose log set still contains the event), so skipping a tick is safe and
the next head update will retry. Crucially, the actor stays alive, the
signer sender stays open, and the network actor doesn't get pulled down
as a side effect.

Reproduced on a private L1 with sub-second block times where the head
reorged between the polling stream's emit and the log fetch.

test(flashblocks): split TestFlashblocksTransfer into bounded phases (#19934)

The test conflated three distinct failure modes — tx never confirmed,
op-rbuilder emitted no flashblocks at all, op-rbuilder emitted flashblocks
for other blocks but not the inclusion block — into a single 30-minute
hang on the package timeout, all reported as the misleading
"never found the transaction in flashblock receipts for the confirmed
block" message. The May-7 instance (pipeline 124622) is an example: in
that run the underlying problem was that op-rbuilder/rollup-boost
integration was broken for the entire test (every block produced
"Missing payload" / "Unknown payload" errors, zero user txs landed,
zero flashblocks were ever delivered). The original message blamed the
flashblock observation but the actual failure was in tx submission, so
the next investigator would chase the wrong subsystem.

Restructure the test into two sequential, separately-timed phases:

1. Wait for Alice's tx to confirm on-chain, bounded by
   txConfirmTimeout (60s). Failure here clearly points at the
   sequencer / txpool, not at flashblocks.

2. Wait for op-rbuilder to publish a flashblock for the confirmed
   inclusion block, bounded by flashblockObserveTimeout (30s).
   The diagnostic message distinguishes "no flashblocks at all"
   (op-rbuilder broken) from "flashblocks for other blocks but not
   the inclusion block" (real flashblock-vs-inclusion mismatch),
   and lists the block numbers that did emit flashblocks.

Run a collector goroutine in parallel to buffer all matching
flashblocks during phase 1, so phase 2 picks up flashblocks emitted
before the on-chain inclusion is observed.

This eliminates the race where the package timeout — not the test
logic — was the only bound on failure detection, and gives engineers
actionable diagnostics for the next failure.

Refs #19934

test(flashblocks): fix collector goroutine deadlock in TestFlashblocksTransfer

The previous fix registered two defers — `defer cancelCollector()` then
`defer collectorWG.Wait()` — and on every return Go's LIFO ordering ran
`Wait()` first. The collector goroutine was parked in
`<-fbClient.Next()` (which only closes when startClient's t.Cleanup fires
*after* the test-function defers), so `Wait()` blocked until the package
test timeout, on both success and failure paths.

Collapse the two defers into one closure that cancels the collector
context first and then waits, so the collector exits via its
`<-collectorCtx.Done()` arm before `Wait()` is called.

Also replace `sort.Slice` with `slices.Sort` per the linter's hint.

Note: this fixes the deadlock the previous commit introduced. The
underlying flake — op-rbuilder/rollup-boost not emitting a flashblock for
the inclusion block — is unchanged and still requires a separate fix in
the builder pipeline. This change improves diagnostics so the next
failure points at the right subsystem; it does not reduce flake count.

fix(kona/protocol): grow output buffer on NeedsMoreInput-with-full-buffer

When `available_in` and `available_out` reach 0 in the same iteration,
`BrotliDecompressStream` returns `NeedsMoreInput` with priority over
`NeedsMoreOutput`, even though it has more output to flush given more
buffer space. The previous loop treated this as "done" and returned the
partial buffer.

Go's `brotli.NewReader` doesn't have this issue because its bufio
indirection re-reads from the source on the next call, which gives brotli
a fresh output slice. So the kona wrapper bug surfaced as a Go vs Rust
derivation divergence on truncated brotli channels: kona produced
significantly fewer output bytes than op-node from the same input.

Treat the simultaneous full-buffer + exhausted-input state identically to
`NeedsMoreOutput`: at the size cap, stop (spec truncation); otherwise
grow the buffer and call brotli again. Brotli will signal
`NeedsMoreInput` again with non-zero `available_out` only when truly out
of input.

Add `test_decompress_truncated_matches_streaming_reader` which sweeps
truncations of a compressed stream and asserts kona's output matches the
brotli crate's high-level Reader byte-for-byte (matching what Go's
brotli.NewReader produces).

Refs ethereum-optimism/optimism#19333

op-supernode: under-claim i.currentL1 by one L1 block on Advance

After DecisionAdvance(T_v), i.currentL1 was set to L1Inclusion(T_v) — the
max L1 source across chains at T_v. This over-claims: L1Inclusion is
monotonic, so the next unverified ts T_v+1 can have the same L1Inclusion
when no chain advanced its L1 source between T_v and T_v+1 (the common
case during the gap between batch postings, which can be hours apart).

A consumer relying on aggregate.CurrentL1 ≥ s.l1Head as proof that
everything derivable from L1[≤s.l1Head] is verified is then lied to
whenever s.l1Head == L1Inclusion(T_v): an unverified T_v+1 also lives
at that L1, per-chain reads can return Data == nil, and the gate still
passes — leading op-challenger to play InvalidTransition for a ts whose
canonical answer is a SuperRoot.

Under-claim by one L1 block: i.currentL1 = L1Inclusion(T_v) - 1 with
the parent block's hash from the L1 source. The aggregate gate then
fails for queries at the offending ts and the consumer correctly
retries. Liveness: stalls only inside a constant-L1Inclusion run; the
existing DecisionWait branch's refreshCurrentL1OnWait lifts i.currentL1
back to localL1 between Advances, so dispute-game progress is bounded
by L2 block production cadence (seconds), never by batch-posting
cadence (hours).

L1 hash is best-effort: if the l1Source lookup fails, we fall back to
a hash-less BlockID with the under-claimed Number. Current consumers
(op-challenger gate uses .Number only; op-proposer logs .Hash) tolerate
a zero hash. At L1 genesis (Number == 0) there is nothing earlier, so
the result is reported unchanged.

refactor(op-acceptance-tests,op-devstack): assert kona disagrees on osaka tx-gas-cap

Splits `TestEIP7825TxGasLimitCap` from a table-driven test into two
`t.Run` subtests. The pre-karst subtest is the inverse of the previous
osaka kona refactors: instead of asserting kona agrees with the live
chain, it deliberately mismatches kona's view and asserts kona
*disagrees*. The live chain runs Jovian (no cap) and accepts a tx with
gas > 2^24, but kona's rollup config is overridden so kona thinks
Karst is at genesis — kona then rejects that block on EIP-7825 grounds
and `RunKonaNative` returns false. The post-karst subtest just
verifies op-reth's RPC rejects the tx; no kona is involved.

The mismatch is wired through a new explicit `WithKonaKarstAtGenesis`
option on `presets.NewMinimalWithKona`. It hooks into the existing
`AfterBuild` mechanism, reads the on-disk `rollup.json` that kona-host
will load, unmarshals into a fresh `rollup.Config`, sets
`KarstTime = 0`, and writes it back — so kona reads the lying config
and the live chain's in-memory config is never touched.
