fix(op-devstack): progress-aware initial sync check for ELSync verifiers

The preset's initial CrossSafe match for ELSync-mode verifiers was a fixed
120-attempt poll (240s). Under CI resource contention, op-geth's beacon-driven
EL sync sometimes does not complete within that budget — the verifier's
unsafe head keeps advancing via CL gossip every 2s while the safe head stays
at 0 because the EL is still snap-syncing historical blocks. The whole
budget then burns and the test fails at setup.

Replace the fixed-attempt poll with a progress-aware wait: keep polling for
up to 8 minutes, but fail fast (within 30s) if the verifier's LocalUnsafe
head stops advancing. LocalUnsafe is driven by CL P2P gossip and is
independent of EL snap-sync, so a stall there means the test setup is
genuinely stuck and more waiting will not help. Successful runs still finish
in tens of seconds; only the worst-case CI runs use the extended window.

Refs #20649.
fix(op-devstack): progress-aware initial sync check for ELSync verifiers

fix(op-acceptance-tests): stop wedging test sequencer on transient L1 EL stalls

Fixes flake in TestUnsafeGapFillAfterSafeReorg and related reorg/follow_l2
tests (#19884). The polling closures advancing L1 via the test sequencer
used require.NoError on ts.New and ts.Next. A single transient stall of
the in-process L1 EL (CPU starvation under CI load) caused ts.Next to
exceed its 10s RPC call timeout, which both marked the test failed via
require.NoError AND left the sequencer with currentJob set. Every
subsequent ts.New(parent=zero) then returned ErrConflictingJob, so the
polling loop could never satisfy its condition and the test ended with
"Condition never satisfied" 120s later.

Drop the explicit ts.New from the polling callback (Sequencer.Next
already calls s.New(BuildOpts{}) internally and tolerates
ErrConflictingJob, so it recovers from a wedged job on its own) and
replace require.NoError(ts.Next(...)) with a log-and-retry path so a
transient stall no longer marks the test failed.

Refs #19884

fix(op-supervisor/logs): atomic operations and crash-safe recovery

Rewrites logs.DB so every mutating operation (AddLog/SealBlock/Rewind/Clear)
is all-or-nothing and durable, and so that startup recovery never lands on a
non-closing-boundary tail.

Core changes:

- logContext gains cloneForWrite(): a value-receiver returning an independent
  copy. logs.DB adopts a working-clone pattern — AddLog accumulates into a
  clone with no I/O; SealBlock does one Write + Sync + atomic swap. On any
  failure the clone is discarded and the committed lastEntryContext is
  unchanged. Reads observe only the committed state.
- entrydb gains Sync() (fsync) on EntryStore. The cleanupFailedWrite bool is
  replaced by an explicit pendingCleanup{active, truncateTo} struct: failed
  Truncates are retried on the next mutation, and reads are bounded by the
  pending target so a swap-before-truncate Rewind never exposes
  post-target bytes.
- Rewind swaps committed state first, then truncates and syncs. Clear and a
  test-only DB.forceBlock follow the same pattern. fsync runs at the end of
  every successful commit.
- trimToLastSealed walks back to a true closing-block boundary
  (CanonicalHash preceded by SearchCheckpoint with logsSince==0), skipping
  periodic search-checkpoints inserted every 256 entries.
- Startup recovery adds a drop-last-block rule: if the file ends exactly at
  the last closing boundary (nothing post-boundary), the last block is
  dropped. Post-boundary entries are the only proof that the prior
  SealBlock's Sync return value was observed; without that proof, drop the
  block. Cost: one re-fetched block per startup.
- Package doc at the top of logs/db.go records both invariants and the FS
  assumptions (ext4/xfs ftruncate atomicity, Linux fsync flushing the
  device cache, macOS *os.File.Sync NOT issuing F_FULLFSYNC).

Test changes:

- New TestLogContextCloneForWrite_Isolation walks every field via reflection
  and asserts the clone cannot share state with the original — adding a
  field to logContext without updating cloneForWrite is a deterministic
  failure.
- New crash-injection harness in crash_test.go exercises sync-failure
  rollback and the periodic-checkpoint recovery edge case. A
  BenchmarkSealBlock_SyscallCount sanity-checks that a steady-state
  SealBlock issues exactly 1 Write + 1 Sync.
- TestRecoverOnCreate subtests updated for the drop-last-block rule.
  Subtests that previously relied on AddLog flushing per-call (so
  intermediate state survived Close/reopen) moved their AddLog calls into
  the assertion phase, which both "New" and "Existing" runDBTest variants
  share. db.pendingNextIndex() replaces m.entryCount as the loop guard for
  patterns like `for ... < N { AddLog(...) }`.
- Supernode and op-interop-filter tests that asserted "latest block
  survives reopen" updated to assert "latest block - 1 survives reopen" per
  the new recovery rule.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(op-chain-ops,op-acceptance-tests): port EIP-7934 to karsttest

Add `karsttest.CheckEIP7934BlockSizeDisabled`, port the
block-size-disabled acceptance test to use it, and expose a new
`eip-7934` subcommand on `check-karst` (with a `--poll-interval` flag).

The check polls the unsafe head until it finds a block whose total
transaction-data size exceeds `params.MaxBlockSize` (8 MiB). Tx data
size is a strict lower bound on RLP-encoded block size, so observing
txData > 8 MiB proves the block exceeds the EIP-7934 limit.

Producing such a block requires sustained traffic. The acceptance test
keeps its `spamTxs` setup to drive the chain; the karsttest function
itself only does the polling. There is no internal timeout — callers
control the deadline via the context (the acceptance test framework's
deadline; Ctrl+C in the CLI). The CLI subcommand is not wired into
`CheckAll`, since on a quiet chain it would block forever.

To minimize coupling, `CheckEIP7934BlockSizeDisabled` takes a tiny
`LatestBlockFetcher` interface (just `InfoAndTxsByLabel`). The
acceptance test passes `apis.EthClient` directly; the CLI provides a
small adapter around `*ethclient.Client` that maps `Unsafe` →
`BlockByNumber(nil)`.

fix(op-interop-filter): validate earliest block on resume

findAndSetEarliestBlock previously stored first.Number+1 as the earliest
queryable block without verifying that block actually had log data. Two
states could mislabel an unqueryable block as queryable: the DB
containing only the anchor (process killed between sealParentBlock and
the first ingestBlock), or an unexpected DB state with sealed blocks
past the anchor that fail to open.

In addition, GetExecMsgsAtTimestamp conflated "uninitialized" with
"before earliest" — both returned (nil, nil), so a query for a sealed
anchor while no blocks had been ingested yet would silently report "no
executing messages" instead of surfacing that the filter wasn't ready.

Now, on resume:
- If only the anchor is sealed, leave earliestIngestedBlockSet false and
  let ingestBlock set it on the first successful ingestion (matching
  the fresh-start path).
- If blocks past the anchor are sealed, verify with OpenBlock and refuse
  to start if it fails — the DB is in an unexpected state we should not
  serve queries from.

GetExecMsgsAtTimestamp now returns ErrUninitialized when the lower
bound is unset, distinct from the (nil, nil) "before earliest" case.

Addresses RV audit finding (medium): unchecked edge cases in
findAndSetEarliestBlock.

op-supernode: clear v.inner on Stop and consolidate superroot_atTimestamp gather

Two related changes preparing for an upcoming consistency fix in
superroot_atTimestamp:

1. simpleVirtualNode.Stop now clears v.inner synchronously before
   returning, so SyncStatus / SafeHeadAtL1 / L1AtSafeHead observe
   ErrVirtualNodeNotRunning as soon as Stop has been invoked. Previously
   these methods kept serving the stopped VN's last published snapshot
   for the duration of the inner-node drain, which let the
   superroot_atTimestamp handler return a populated CurrentL1 paired
   with Data == nil while a concurrent rewind had mutated the EL.

2. ChainContainer gains GatherSuperRootData, a single per-chain method
   that returns every field the superroot_atTimestamp handler needs.
   The handler is rewritten to call GatherSuperRootData per chain and
   aggregate over the gathered results, instead of issuing five separate
   reads per chain (SyncStatus, VerifiedAt, OptimisticOutputAtTimestamp,
   OptimisticAt, OutputRootAtL2BlockNumber). Behaviour is preserved:
   the gather method composes the same underlying calls. The
   consolidation is the seam at which the consistency guarantees in a
   follow-up commit will be enforced.

A regression test (TestVirtualNode_StopClearsInnerBeforeReturn) pins the
post-Stop synchronous behaviour using the existing blockingStopMock.

op-supernode: detect VN restart / RewindEngine during superroot gather

simpleChainContainer gains a generation counter (c.gen) bumped on every
state transition that could make data gathered earlier inconsistent with
state observed later: a new virtual node being installed (setVN) and entry
to RewindEngine. GatherSuperRootData captures c.gen at the start of its
work and re-reads it after all reads complete; if it changed in between,
the reads have straddled pre- and post-mutation state and ChainSuperRootData
is discarded with ErrInconsistentSnapshot — the caller can retry on the
next polling tick.

Inner-pipeline rollup.ResetEvent paths (channel decode, blob data fetch
failure, attribute mismatch, finalizer divergence, etc.) don't currently
go through either site and therefore aren't caught by this counter; that
wiring is a follow-up.

Replace the GatherSuperRootData consolidation and the standalone
OnPipelineReset callback with a single per-chain generation counter. The
counter is bumped on every state-mutating event that could make per-chain
reads inconsistent across a single superroot_atTimestamp request — VN
restart, RewindEngine entry, inner-pipeline rollup.ResetEvent — and the
superroot activity captures it at the start and end of its work to detect
mid-call mutations.

Two structural changes go together:

1. NotifyPipelineReset moves onto the SuperAuthority interface. The chain
   container already implements SuperAuthority for payload-validation
   queries; surfacing pipeline resets through the same interface unifies
   the supernode-talks-to-op-node and op-node-talks-back-to-supernode
   contracts and removes the ad-hoc OnPipelineReset func() field that
   InitializationOverrides had been carrying. The interface conformance
   assertion now enforces "supernode handles pipeline resets" at compile
   time. NewStatusTracker takes a SuperAuthority and invokes
   NotifyPipelineReset from the rollup.ResetEvent arm of OnEvent — before
   UpdateSyncStatus republishes the zeroed snapshot, so the gen bump
   precedes any reader observing the reset.

2. GatherSuperRootData is removed from the ChainContainer interface and
   simpleChainContainer. The per-chain reads (SyncStatus,
   VerifierCurrentL1s, VerifiedAt, OutputRootAtL2BlockNumber,
   OptimisticOutputAtTimestamp, OptimisticAt) live back in the
   superroot.atTimestamp handler where they used to live, plus a single
   start/end gen comparison that returns ErrInconsistentSnapshot if any
   chain's Generation() advanced during the gather. The chain container
   exposes c.gen.Load() via a new Generation() interface method;
   ChainSuperRootData / VerifiedChainData / OptimisticChainData and the
   old chain-container-level ErrInconsistentSnapshot are gone.

op-supernode: under-claim i.currentL1 by one L1 block on Advance

After DecisionAdvance(T_v), i.currentL1 was set to L1Inclusion(T_v) — the
max L1 source across chains at T_v. This over-claims: L1Inclusion is
monotonic, so the next unverified ts T_v+1 can have the same L1Inclusion
when no chain advanced its L1 source between T_v and T_v+1 (the common
case during the gap between batch postings, which can be hours apart).

A consumer relying on aggregate.CurrentL1 ≥ s.l1Head as proof that
everything derivable from L1[≤s.l1Head] is verified is then lied to
whenever s.l1Head == L1Inclusion(T_v): an unverified T_v+1 also lives
at that L1, per-chain reads can return Data == nil, and the gate still
passes — leading op-challenger to play InvalidTransition for a ts whose
canonical answer is a SuperRoot.

Under-claim by one L1 block: i.currentL1 = L1Inclusion(T_v) - 1 with
the parent block's hash from the L1 source. The aggregate gate then
fails for queries at the offending ts and the consumer correctly
retries. Liveness: stalls only inside a constant-L1Inclusion run; the
existing DecisionWait branch's refreshCurrentL1OnWait lifts i.currentL1
back to localL1 between Advances, so dispute-game progress is bounded
by L2 block production cadence (seconds), never by batch-posting
cadence (hours).

L1 hash is best-effort: if the l1Source lookup fails, we fall back to
a hash-less BlockID with the under-claimed Number. Current consumers
(op-challenger gate uses .Number only; op-proposer logs .Hash) tolerate
a zero hash. At L1 genesis (Number == 0) there is nothing earlier, so
the result is reported unchanged.

Splits `TestEIP7825TxGasLimitCap` from a table-driven test into two
`t.Run` subtests. The pre-karst subtest is the inverse of the previous
osaka kona refactors: instead of asserting kona agrees with the live
chain, it deliberately mismatches kona's view and asserts kona
*disagrees*. The live chain runs Jovian (no cap) and accepts a tx with
gas > 2^24, but kona's rollup config is overridden so kona thinks
Karst is at genesis — kona then rejects that block on EIP-7825 grounds

verifies op-reth's RPC rejects the tx; no kona is involved.

will load, unmarshals into a fresh `rollup.Config`, sets

and the live chain's in-memory config is never touched.

test(flashblocks): split TestFlashblocksTransfer into bounded phases for clearer diagnostics (#20600)

* test(flashblocks): split TestFlashblocksTransfer into bounded phases (#19934)

The test conflated three distinct failure modes — tx never confirmed,
op-rbuilder emitted no flashblocks at all, op-rbuilder emitted flashblocks
for other blocks but not the inclusion block — into a single 30-minute
hang on the package timeout, all reported as the misleading
"never found the transaction in flashblock receipts for the confirmed
block" message. The May-7 instance (pipeline 124622) is an example: in
that run the underlying problem was that op-rbuilder/rollup-boost
integration was broken for the entire test (every block produced
"Missing payload" / "Unknown payload" errors, zero user txs landed,
zero flashblocks were ever delivered). The original message blamed the
flashblock observation but the actual failure was in tx submission, so
the next investigator would chase the wrong subsystem.

Restructure the test into two sequential, separately-timed phases:

1. Wait for Alice's tx to confirm on-chain, bounded by
   txConfirmTimeout (60s). Failure here clearly points at the
   sequencer / txpool, not at flashblocks.

2. Wait for op-rbuilder to publish a flashblock for the confirmed
   inclusion block, bounded by flashblockObserveTimeout (30s).
   The diagnostic message distinguishes "no flashblocks at all"
   (op-rbuilder broken) from "flashblocks for other blocks but not
   the inclusion block" (real flashblock-vs-inclusion mismatch),
   and lists the block numbers that did emit flashblocks.

Run a collector goroutine in parallel to buffer all matching
flashblocks during phase 1, so phase 2 picks up flashblocks emitted
before the on-chain inclusion is observed.

This eliminates the race where the package timeout — not the test
logic — was the only bound on failure detection, and gives engineers
actionable diagnostics for the next failure.

* test(flashblocks): fix collector goroutine deadlock in TestFlashblocksTransfer

The previous fix registered two defers — `defer cancelCollector()` then
`defer collectorWG.Wait()` — and on every return Go's LIFO ordering ran
`Wait()` first. The collector goroutine was parked in
`<-fbClient.Next()` (which only closes when startClient's t.Cleanup fires
*after* the test-function defers), so `Wait()` blocked until the package
test timeout, on both success and failure paths.

Collapse the two defers into one closure that cancels the collector
context first and then waits, so the collector exits via its
`<-collectorCtx.Done()` arm before `Wait()` is called.

Also replace `sort.Slice` with `slices.Sort` per the linter's hint.

Note: this fixes the deadlock the previous commit introduced. The
underlying flake — op-rbuilder/rollup-boost not emitting a flashblock for
the inclusion block — is unchanged and still requires a separate fix in
the builder pipeline. This change improves diagnostics so the next
failure points at the right subsystem; it does not reduce flake count.

fix(kona/client): bump FPVM precompile oracle gas for Glamsterdam (EIP-7904)

Split the single gas constant in each FPVM-accelerated precompile into two
named values: the L2 gas charge (unchanged) and the oracle/L1 staticcall
gas required by EIP-7904, sent in the L1Precompile preimage hint.

Without this fix, once Glamsterdam activates on L1, the
`loadPrecompilePreimagePart` staticcall would silently OOG for KZG, BLS12-381
G1Add, G2Add, and bn256 pairing because the requiredGas embedded in the
preimage key would be below the post-7904 L1 cost. Higher-than-needed
oracle gas is always safe, so this can deploy proactively.

L2 gas charging (`EthPrecompileOutput::gas_used`) and the OOG guards
continue to use the existing values, preserving state-root agreement with
op-reth pre-revm-bump.

Affected (EIP-7904 L1 cost → embedded in oracle hint):
- KZG point eval (0x0a): 89_363
- BLS12-381 G1Add (0x0b): 643
- BLS12-381 G2Add (0x0d): 765
- bn256 pairing (0x08): 45_000 + 34_103 × k

Mirrors ethereum-optimism/optimism#19381 for kona-proof.

op-supernode: redefine superroot_atTimestamp CurrentL1 as block being processed

CurrentL1 in the superroot_atTimestamp response previously meant "highest L1
block fully derived and verified by all chains". L1Inclusion is monotonic in
L2 timestamp, so the next unverified ts T_v+1 can share L1Inclusion(T_v) when
no chain's L1 source advanced — a consumer relying on aggregate.CurrentL1
≥ s.l1Head as proof that everything derivable from L1[≤s.l1Head] is verified
gets lied to whenever s.l1Head == L1Inclusion(T_v).

Match op-node's sync-status semantics instead: CurrentL1 names the L1 block
currently being processed by the slowest L1 processor in the supernode, so
L1[<CurrentL1] is fully processed. Consumers gating on "L1[≤X] fully
processed" require CurrentL1 > X.

Advance is correct under the new meaning, and collectCurrentL1's min over
op-node CurrentL1 (also "being processed") stays consistent. op-challenger's
three ErrNotInSync gates in provider_supernode.go flip from `<` to `<=`.

op-challenger/runner game-input generation and op-proposer are intentionally
left alone: the runner's downstream logic compensates for an l1Head one block
high, and the proposer never gates on the equality case.

fix(op-devstack): wait for L1 head past game createdAt before prove

OptimismPortal2.proveWithdrawalTransaction reverts with
OptimismPortal_InvalidProofTimestamp (selector 0xb4caa4e5) when
block.timestamp <= disputeGameProxy.createdAt(). Because estimateGas
evaluates the call against the current L1 head, any prove attempt before
the head advances past the game's createdAt is guaranteed to revert.

The previous code relied on a 30s / 1s `Eventually` retry to "catch" the
revert and try again as the L1 head advanced. Under loaded CI, L1 block
production stalls (this run saw a ~6s gap between L1 blocks 13 and 14),
so the retry loop burned its budget on guaranteed-revert estimateGas
calls before the head moved, then ran out of remaining budget to confirm
the actual prove transaction.

Wait deterministically for `head.timestamp > game.createdAt()` (using a
60s budget that is generous enough to absorb L1 stalls) before entering
the prove-tx retry. The 30s prove retry is now correctly scoped to
transient submission/confirmation, not to a precondition that the test
can observe directly.

Adds a `CreatedAt() -> uint64` accessor to the FaultDisputeGame binding
to support this.

Fixes #19963.

fix(op-node): record safeDB by local-safe derivation L1

The safeDB previously recorded entries on engine.SafeDerivedEvent, which
is emitted only by EngineController.PromoteSafe — the cross-safe
promotion path. In non-interop, local-safe and cross-safe coincide so
this was harmless. In interop, cross-safe promotion happens later than
local-safe, so the L1 key for each safe head was the cross-safe-
promotion L1 rather than the L1 from which the L2 block was derived.

block that includes the last piece of batch data required to derive the
L2 optimistic block). Switch SyncDeriver to write the safeDB on
engine.LocalSafeUpdateEvent and key by x.Source (the derivation L1).

Replacement blocks have no derivation L1; the prior local-safe entry is
re-keyed correctly by SafeHeadReset on engine-reset confirmation, so
the new handler explicitly ignores engine.ReplaceBlockSource.

op-supernode: under-claim i.currentL1 by one L1 block on Advance

After DecisionAdvance(T_v), i.currentL1 was set to L1Inclusion(T_v) — the
max L1 source across chains at T_v. This over-claims: L1Inclusion is
monotonic, so the next unverified ts T_v+1 can have the same L1Inclusion
when no chain advanced its L1 source between T_v and T_v+1 (the common
case during the gap between batch postings, which can be hours apart).

A consumer relying on aggregate.CurrentL1 ≥ s.l1Head as proof that
everything derivable from L1[≤s.l1Head] is verified is then lied to
whenever s.l1Head == L1Inclusion(T_v): an unverified T_v+1 also lives
at that L1, per-chain reads can return Data == nil, and the gate still
passes — leading op-challenger to play InvalidTransition for a ts whose
canonical answer is a SuperRoot.

Under-claim by one L1 block: i.currentL1 = L1Inclusion(T_v) - 1 with
the parent block's hash from the L1 source. The aggregate gate then
fails for queries at the offending ts and the consumer correctly
retries. Liveness: stalls only inside a constant-L1Inclusion run; the
existing DecisionWait branch's refreshCurrentL1OnWait lifts i.currentL1
back to localL1 between Advances, so dispute-game progress is bounded
by L2 block production cadence (seconds), never by batch-posting
cadence (hours).

L1 hash is best-effort: if the l1Source lookup fails, we fall back to
a hash-less BlockID with the under-claimed Number. Current consumers
(op-challenger gate uses .Number only; op-proposer logs .Hash) tolerate
a zero hash. At L1 genesis (Number == 0) there is nothing earlier, so
the result is reported unchanged.

Two acceptance tests in op-acceptance-tests/tests/superfaultproofs that
demonstrate op-challenger and kona disagreeing on the optimistic-branch
step values when chain A's at-T block hasn't been cross-safe-promoted at
the game's L1 head.

Both tests place an invalid exec message on chain A with the init on chain B
and pause chain B's batcher to control L1 ordering. They differ in whether
the bad block is eventually replaced via cross-validation (B's batcher is
restarted) or remains local-safe with no replacement (B's batcher stays
stopped). Same expectation in both: step 1 should produce
\`start + A_optimistic\` and step 2 should produce InvalidTransition. Kona
agrees in both runs; the supernode-driven trace provider returns
InvalidTransition for step 1 because RequiredL1 is the cross-safe-promotion
L1 (\`> game L1 head\`) rather than the local-safe L1 where the block actually
becomes derivable.

demonstrates that op-supernode records the local-safe derivation L1 in safeDB

without re-verifying it, which is why the fpp variants passed.

pattern as runFaultProofTest:

  - freezeChains() to take exclusive control of L2 block production.
  - advanceUnsafeToTimestamp + advanceSafeToCurrentUnsafe to land each
    chain's pre-T block on L1 and reach cross-safe at startTimestamp.
  - Build chain A's at-endTimestamp block with a fabricated invalid exec
    message via TestSequencer.SequenceBlockWithTxs.
  - Batch chain A's at-endTimestamp block.
  - Wait l1GapBetweenChainBatches L1 blocks so chain B's batch is strictly
    later.
  - Capture gameL1Head at the start of the gap window.
  - With-replacement: build chain B's empty at-endTimestamp block and
    batch it; op-supernode invalidates A and replaces it.
  - No-replacement: leave chain B's at-endTimestamp unbuilt; A stays
    local-safe at endTimestamp forever.

Adds a pre-condition assertion that the super root at startTimestamp has
VerifiedRequiredL1 <= gameL1Head so any future regression in the setup
itself fails fast. Adds diagnostic logging of L1 head positions and the
supernode's superroot_atTimestamp response for both timestamps.

fix(kona-host): verify preimage bytes hash to the requested key

Mirror op-program's `preimage.WithVerification` posture on the kona host
side. Previously, `OracleServer::next_preimage_request` forwarded
`PreimageFetcher` bytes straight to the client with no check that the
returned data actually hashes to the requested key — a corrupt RPC,
buggy hint handler, or tampered KV store would silently produce wrong
off-chain claims and lose bonds at the cannon step instead of erroring
at fetch time.

Adds `VerifyingPreimageFetcher<F>` in `kona-preimage` that re-hashes
returned data for `Keccak256` and `Sha256` keys (matching the [1..32]
byte comparison op-program uses) and passes through `Local`, `Blob`,
`Precompile`, and the reserved `GlobalGeneric` types, which cannot be
verified from `(key, data)` alone. Wraps every host backend
construction site:

- bin/host/src/single/cfg.rs   (offline + online)
- bin/host/src/interop/cfg.rs  (offline + online)
- bin/host/src/interop/handler.rs (online re-execution backend)

Adds `PreimageOracleError::IncorrectData` to surface the mismatch and
unit tests covering valid data, corrupt data, empty data, and
pass-through for non-self-verifying key types.

This is defence-in-depth, not a consensus fix: the on-chain
`PreimageOracle` already derives keys from supplied preimages, so an
attacker cannot register `(K, D)` with `keccak256(D) != K` on-chain.
The change closes the off-chain detection gap so kona provers fail
loudly at fetch time, matching op-program.

fix(op-supernode): stabilize superroot_atTimestamp Data field

The verified branch of superroot_atTimestamp recomputed per-chain
OutputV0 from live L2 EL state on every call via VerifiedAt's safeDB
walkback + OutputRootAtL2BlockNumber. That meant an EL reorg or
cross-chain invalidation could change SuperRoot(T) for the same T
across calls, violating the stability invariant op-challenger needs
to play interop dispute games.

Rework so:

- Post-interop: source the canonical (chainID, blockHash) tuples from
  verifiedDB (the existing cross-safe write gate at interop.go:730)
  and read per-chain OutputV0 by hash from the L2 EL via a new
  OutputRootAtL2BlockHash on ChainContainer. Add dep-set sanity and a
  rewind-race coupling check.
- Pre-interop / interop disabled: compose Data by reusing the
  per-chain entries already built for the response's
  OptimisticAtTimestamp map — pre-interop, local-safe outputs cannot
  be invalidated, so the optimistic outputs ARE the canonical
  outputs. No second per-chain fetch; the regime is selected via a
  new sentinel interop.ErrNotActive returned by
  Interop.VerifiedResultAtTimestamp (and the new
  NoopVerifiedResultReader when interop is not configured).

Optimistic-branch chain-level transport errors continue to fail the
RPC under every regime — silently emitting a partial
OptimisticAtTimestamp map at step>0 would cause op-challenger to
commit InvalidTransition permanently on chain.

Deletes ChainContainer.VerifiedAt and ChainContainer.OutputRootAtL2BlockNumber
plus their test mocks. simpleChainContainer.safeDBAtL2 is preserved
(still used by OptimisticAt).

fix(op-supernode): distinguish below-verified-db regime in superroot_atTimestamp

Split the regime signal so the four cases for superroot_atTimestamp(T) are
distinguishable:

  - T < activationTimestamp           → ErrNotActive, compose Data from
                                        per-chain optimistic outputs
                                        (pre-interop blocks cannot be
                                        invalidated, so optimistic ≡ canonical)
  - T < firstVerifiableTimestamp      → ErrBeforeVerifiedDB, fail the RPC
                                        (no entry will ever exist on this
                                        node and no deny-list data is
                                        available to reconstruct from
                                        optimistic state)
  - verifiedDB entry present          → compose from VerifiedResult + EL
                                        by-hash; answer pinned to entry
  - verifiedDB.Get → NotFound         → ethereum.NotFound, return Data=nil
                                        and let CurrentL1 communicate
                                        verifier progress

Previously [activation, firstVerifiable) was folded into ErrNotActive and
fell through to the optimistic-fallback path. That was wrong: post-activation
the chain has been through interop validation elsewhere, but this node lacks
the deny-list entries to reproduce that state, so the optimistic outputs are
not guaranteed to match canonical.

Also tightens comments across the change to drop design-doc references and
change-history phrasing.

fix(op-supernode): close verifiedDB/CurrentL1 read race in superroot_atTimestamp

Without an atomic read across both, the response could pair a stale
aggregate CurrentL1 with a fresh verifiedDB observation (or vice versa):

  - Reader: aggregate.CurrentL1 = high
  - Writer: rewind drops i.currentL1 to 0, then deletes verifiedDB row
  - Reader: verifiedDB.Get → NotFound
  → response {CurrentL1: high, Data: nil} — caller reads as "passed
    required L1 with no entry → final negative" but the entry existed
    moments ago.

The symmetric race exists in the commit direction (entry committed,
then currentL1 advanced, between the two reads), so simply reordering
doesn't help.

VerifiedResultReader.VerifiedResultAtTimestamp now returns the verifier's
CurrentL1 captured under the same RLock as the verifiedDB.Get. The
superroot handler reports min(aggregate.CurrentL1, snapshotL1) and feeds
the same value to the rewind-race coupling check. The verifier's existing
mutation ordering — commit writes the entry before advancing currentL1;
rewind zeroes currentL1 before deleting rows — combined with the atomic
read guarantees a consistent snapshot.

fix(op-supernode): drop rewind-race coupling check in superroot_atTimestamp

The previous check refused to return Data when the response's CurrentL1
was below the entry's VerifiedRequiredL1 (e.g. mid-rewind, where the
verifier has rolled CurrentL1 back but the entry has not yet been

that pair is internally consistent — it accurately says "this entry
was committed but the verifier is currently at a lower L1." Callers
gate trust on CurrentL1 themselves, so returning the data is more

Add `karsttest.CheckEIP7934BlockSizeDisabled`, port the
block-size-disabled acceptance test to use it, and expose a new
`eip-7934` subcommand on `check-karst` (with a `--poll-interval` flag).

The check polls the unsafe head until it finds a block whose total
transaction-data size exceeds `params.MaxBlockSize` (8 MiB). Tx data
size is a strict lower bound on RLP-encoded block size, so observing
txData > 8 MiB proves the block exceeds the EIP-7934 limit.

Producing such a block requires sustained traffic. The acceptance test
keeps its `spamTxs` setup to drive the chain; the karsttest function
itself only does the polling. There is no internal timeout — callers
control the deadline via the context (the acceptance test framework's
deadline; Ctrl+C in the CLI). The CLI subcommand is not wired into
`CheckAll`, since on a quiet chain it would block forever.

To minimize coupling, `CheckEIP7934BlockSizeDisabled` takes a tiny
`LatestBlockFetcher` interface (just `InfoAndTxsByLabel`). The
acceptance test passes `apis.EthClient` directly; the CLI provides a
small adapter around `*ethclient.Client` that maps `Unsafe` →
`BlockByNumber(nil)`.

fix(kona-host): verify preimage bytes hash to the requested key (#20661)

* fix(kona-host): verify preimage bytes hash to the requested key

Mirror op-program's `preimage.WithVerification` posture on the kona host
side. Previously, `OracleServer::next_preimage_request` forwarded
`PreimageFetcher` bytes straight to the client with no check that the
returned data actually hashes to the requested key — a corrupt RPC,
buggy hint handler, or tampered KV store would silently produce wrong
off-chain claims and lose bonds at the cannon step instead of erroring
at fetch time.

Adds `VerifyingPreimageFetcher<F>` in `kona-preimage` that re-hashes
returned data for `Keccak256` and `Sha256` keys (matching the [1..32]
byte comparison op-program uses) and passes through `Local`, `Blob`,
`Precompile`, and the reserved `GlobalGeneric` types, which cannot be
verified from `(key, data)` alone. Wraps every host backend
construction site:

- bin/host/src/single/cfg.rs   (offline + online)
- bin/host/src/interop/cfg.rs  (offline + online)
- bin/host/src/interop/handler.rs (online re-execution backend)

Adds `PreimageOracleError::IncorrectData` to surface the mismatch and
unit tests covering valid data, corrupt data, empty data, and
pass-through for non-self-verifying key types.

This is defence-in-depth, not a consensus fix: the on-chain
`PreimageOracle` already derives keys from supplied preimages, so an
attacker cannot register `(K, D)` with `keccak256(D) != K` on-chain.
The change closes the off-chain detection gap so kona provers fail
loudly at fetch time, matching op-program.

* fix(kona-preimage): propagate std feature to sha2

Zepter's propagate-feature check requires that if a crate's dependency
has a std feature, the parent crate's std feature must activate it.
sha2 was added as a workspace dependency (default-features = false) but
not propagated in the std feature list, causing the rust-zepter CI job
to fail.

* fix(kona-preimage): gate verifier behind opt-in `verify` feature

Make `sha2` an optional dependency and gate `VerifyingPreimageFetcher` /
`verify_preimage` behind a new `verify` feature so zkVM consumers
(Kailua, op-succinct) don't pull `sha2` into their dependency graph
where an accidental `use sha2::Sha256;` would be hazardous (stock crypto
in a zkVM costs huge numbers of constraints without an accelerator hook).

The verifier is host-only in practice, clients trust cannon, not their
own re-hashing, so `kona-host` opts in via `features = ["std", "verify"]`
and everything else stays unchanged.

* reject GlobalGeneric, include key in IncorrectData

* test(op-supernode): reproduce superroot_atTimestamp optimistic pairing bug

Two acceptance tests in op-acceptance-tests/tests/superfaultproofs that
demonstrate op-challenger and kona disagreeing on the optimistic-branch
step values when chain A's at-T block hasn't been cross-safe-promoted at
the game's L1 head.

Both tests place an invalid exec message on chain A with the init on chain B
and pause chain B's batcher to control L1 ordering. They differ in whether
the bad block is eventually replaced via cross-validation (B's batcher is
restarted) or remains local-safe with no replacement (B's batcher stays
stopped). Same expectation in both: step 1 should produce
\`start + A_optimistic\` and step 2 should produce InvalidTransition. Kona
agrees in both runs; the supernode-driven trace provider returns
InvalidTransition for step 1 because RequiredL1 is the cross-safe-promotion
L1 (\`> game L1 head\`) rather than the local-safe L1 where the block actually
becomes derivable.

Tests are gt.Skip()'d pending a fix; unskip when ethereum-optimism/optimism#20657
is resolved.

* test(op-supernode): rewrite optimistic-pairing tests with deterministic sequencing; no bug

Re-run with controlled TestSequencer + per-chain Batcher.Start/Stop driving
demonstrates that op-supernode records the local-safe derivation L1 in safeDB
correctly. The originally-suspected ethereum-optimism/optimism#20657 bug does
not exist: op-node in supernode mode runs with SupervisorEnabled=false, so
localSafeIsFullySafe() returns true and local-safe is promoted to cross-safe
at the same L1 origin (engine_controller.go:801, 822-824). The safeDB
SafeDerivedEvent write path is therefore already keyed by the local-safe
derivation L1.

The original tests reproduced challenger/kona divergence because uncontrolled
batcher timing (Stop B then aliceB.SendRandomInitMessage then Start B) made
chain B's pre-T and at-T blocks land in the same L1 batch — pushing
VerifiedAt(B, startTimestamp) to that late L1 and tripping the trace
provider's prevRoot.Data.VerifiedRequiredL1 gate. That was a test-setup
artefact, not a supernode bug. Kona accepted the invalid agreed prestate
without re-verifying it, which is why the fpp variants passed.

This commit rewrites both variants to use the same deterministic sequencing
pattern as runFaultProofTest:

  - freezeChains() to take exclusive control of L2 block production.
  - advanceUnsafeToTimestamp + advanceSafeToCurrentUnsafe to land each
    chain's pre-T block on L1 and reach cross-safe at startTimestamp.
  - Build chain A's at-endTimestamp block with a fabricated invalid exec
    message via TestSequencer.SequenceBlockWithTxs.
  - Batch chain A's at-endTimestamp block.
  - Wait l1GapBetweenChainBatches L1 blocks so chain B's batch is strictly
    later.
  - Capture gameL1Head at the start of the gap window.
  - With-replacement: build chain B's empty at-endTimestamp block and
    batch it; op-supernode invalidates A and replaces it.
  - No-replacement: leave chain B's at-endTimestamp unbuilt; A stays
    local-safe at endTimestamp forever.

Adds a pre-condition assertion that the super root at startTimestamp has
VerifiedRequiredL1 <= gameL1Head so any future regression in the setup
itself fails fast. Adds diagnostic logging of L1 head positions and the
supernode's superroot_atTimestamp response for both timestamps.

Unskips both tests in the serial interop fault-proofs suite. They pass.

Closes ethereum-optimism/optimism#20657 — no fix required.

fix(op-devstack): wait for L1 head past game createdAt before prove (#20677)

OptimismPortal2.proveWithdrawalTransaction reverts with
OptimismPortal_InvalidProofTimestamp (selector 0xb4caa4e5) when
block.timestamp <= disputeGameProxy.createdAt(). Because estimateGas
evaluates the call against the current L1 head, any prove attempt before
the head advances past the game's createdAt is guaranteed to revert.

The previous code relied on a 30s / 1s `Eventually` retry to "catch" the
revert and try again as the L1 head advanced. Under loaded CI, L1 block
production stalls (this run saw a ~6s gap between L1 blocks 13 and 14),
so the retry loop burned its budget on guaranteed-revert estimateGas
calls before the head moved, then ran out of remaining budget to confirm
the actual prove transaction.

Wait deterministically for `head.timestamp > game.createdAt()` (using a
60s budget that is generous enough to absorb L1 stalls) before entering
the prove-tx retry. The 30s prove retry is now correctly scoped to
transient submission/confirmation, not to a precondition that the test
can observe directly.

Adds a `CreatedAt() -> uint64` accessor to the FaultDisputeGame binding
to support this.

Fixes #19963.

fix(kona/protocol): reject invalid is_last byte in frame decode (#20590)

* fix(kona/protocol): reject invalid is_last byte in frame decode

Per the OP Stack derivation spec, the trailing `is_last` byte of a frame
must be 0 or 1; any other value makes the frame invalid and the entire
batcher transaction's frames must be rejected. op-node enforces this in
`Frame.UnmarshalBinary`, but kona's `Frame::decode` was treating
`is_last` as `(byte == 1)`, silently coercing values like 2 to `false`.

This created a parsing divergence: op-node would reject a malformed
batcher transaction while kona would accept it, with the potential to
yield different L2 derivation outputs in a hybrid Go-node + Rust
fault-proof setup.

Add a new `FrameDecodingError::InvalidIsLast(u8)` variant and reject any
non-{0,1} byte in `Frame::decode`. Mirrors op-node's
`TestFrameUnmarshalInvalidIsLast`.

Fixes ethereum-optimism/optimism#19335

fix(op-interop-filter): validate earliest block on resume (#20585)

findAndSetEarliestBlock previously stored first.Number+1 as the earliest
queryable block without verifying that block actually had log data. Two
states could mislabel an unqueryable block as queryable: the DB
containing only the anchor (process killed between sealParentBlock and
the first ingestBlock), or an unexpected DB state with sealed blocks
past the anchor that fail to open.

In addition, GetExecMsgsAtTimestamp conflated "uninitialized" with
"before earliest" — both returned (nil, nil), so a query for a sealed
anchor while no blocks had been ingested yet would silently report "no
executing messages" instead of surfacing that the filter wasn't ready.

Now, on resume:
- If only the anchor is sealed, leave earliestIngestedBlockSet false and
  let ingestBlock set it on the first successful ingestion (matching
  the fresh-start path).
- If blocks past the anchor are sealed, verify with OpenBlock and refuse
  to start if it fails — the DB is in an unexpected state we should not
  serve queries from.

GetExecMsgsAtTimestamp now returns ErrUninitialized when the lower
bound is unset, distinct from the (nil, nil) "before earliest" case.

Addresses RV audit finding (medium): unchecked edge cases in
findAndSetEarliestBlock.

* op-supernode: detect VN restart / RewindEngine during superroot gather

to RewindEngine. GatherSuperRootData captures c.gen at the start of its

* op-supernode: under-claim i.currentL1 by one L1 block on Advance

After DecisionAdvance(T_v), i.currentL1 was set to L1Inclusion(T_v) — the
max L1 source across chains at T_v. This over-claims: L1Inclusion is
monotonic, so the next unverified ts T_v+1 can have the same L1Inclusion
when no chain advanced its L1 source between T_v and T_v+1 (the common
case during the gap between batch postings, which can be hours apart).

A consumer relying on aggregate.CurrentL1 ≥ s.l1Head as proof that
everything derivable from L1[≤s.l1Head] is verified is then lied to
whenever s.l1Head == L1Inclusion(T_v): an unverified T_v+1 also lives
at that L1, per-chain reads can return Data == nil, and the gate still
passes — leading op-challenger to play InvalidTransition for a ts whose
canonical answer is a SuperRoot.

Under-claim by one L1 block: i.currentL1 = L1Inclusion(T_v) - 1 with
the parent block's hash from the L1 source. The aggregate gate then
fails for queries at the offending ts and the consumer correctly
retries. Liveness: stalls only inside a constant-L1Inclusion run; the
existing DecisionWait branch's refreshCurrentL1OnWait lifts i.currentL1
back to localL1 between Advances, so dispute-game progress is bounded
by L2 block production cadence (seconds), never by batch-posting
cadence (hours).

L1 hash is best-effort: if the l1Source lookup fails, we fall back to
a hash-less BlockID with the under-claimed Number. Current consumers
(op-challenger gate uses .Number only; op-proposer logs .Hash) tolerate
a zero hash. At L1 genesis (Number == 0) there is nothing earlier, so
the result is reported unchanged.

fix(op-acceptance-tests): stop wedging test sequencer on transient L1 EL stalls (#20651)

Fixes flake in TestUnsafeGapFillAfterSafeReorg and related reorg/follow_l2
tests (#19884). The polling closures advancing L1 via the test sequencer
used require.NoError on ts.New and ts.Next. A single transient stall of
the in-process L1 EL (CPU starvation under CI load) caused ts.Next to
exceed its 10s RPC call timeout, which both marked the test failed via
require.NoError AND left the sequencer with currentJob set. Every
subsequent ts.New(parent=zero) then returned ErrConflictingJob, so the
polling loop could never satisfy its condition and the test ended with
"Condition never satisfied" 120s later.

Drop the explicit ts.New from the polling callback (Sequencer.Next
already calls s.New(BuildOpts{}) internally and tolerates
ErrConflictingJob, so it recovers from a wedged job on its own) and
replace require.NoError(ts.Next(...)) with a log-and-retry path so a
transient stall no longer marks the test failed.

fix(kona-host): bound get_preimage retries

OnlineHostBackend::get_preimage ran an unbounded `while preimage.is_none()`
loop with no termination condition. Three paths hot-spun at 100% CPU:

1. last_hint is None — the inner `if let Some(hint)` block is skipped and
   the loop iterates without progress or yield.
2. fetch_hint returns Err every iteration (RPC down, malformed payload,
   etc.) — `continue` retries instantly while the error! log spams.
3. fetch_hint returns Ok(()) but the requested key was never written —
   loop body completes, preimage stays None, re-iterates immediately.

Operational impact: a prover whose L1/blob/L2 RPC fails mid-dispute
saturates a CPU, propagates no error, and never recovers. If the spin
coincides with a dispute-game bisection deadline, the prover loses by
timeout. Also a bond-griefing vector for attackers who can disrupt a
known prover's RPC during critical windows.

Fix: replace the unbounded loop with a bounded retry budget plus
exponential backoff (default: 5 attempts, 50ms -> 2s). On budget
exhaustion `get_preimage` returns Err(PreimageOracleError::Other(...))
rather than hanging; the no-hint case returns Err(KeyNotFound)
immediately, matching op-program's `for ... && p.lastHint != ""` guard
(prefetcher.go:115-138).

Caller-visible behavior change: get_preimage can now return Err where
on baseline it would hang. The error propagates via VerifyingPreimageFetcher
and PreimageOracleServer to start_oracle_server, which exits the host
process with PreimageRequestFailed — matching op-program's
"exit on prefetch error" behavior. Operators get an exit code and error
logs to alert on instead of a silent 100%-CPU hang.

No trait signature changes. No new error variants. No new dependencies.
No public API surface added — `RetryPolicy`, `with_retry_policy`, and
the new `retry_policy` field are all private to the `online` module.

feat(kona/derive): pure sync deriver with full span-batch overlap check

Phase 3 of the pure-derivation migration. Builds a pure (sync, IO-free,
no_std) `Deriver` on top of phase 2's `core/*` primitives, and closes
the post-Holocene span-batch overlap content-check spec gap that both
op-node and kona's async pipeline skip today.

Public API in `kona_derive::pure`:
- `Deriver::new(rollup_cfg, l1_cfg, sys_config, safe_head, dep_set)`
- `Deriver::derive(safe_head) -> (Derivation, DeriveTrace)` — never errors
- `Deriver::add_l1_input(L1Input) -> Result<(), CriticalError>`
- `Deriver::add_span_batch_overlap(SpanBatchOverlap) -> Result<(), CriticalError>`
- `Deriver::reset(safe_head, sys_config) -> DeriveTrace`
- `extract_l1_input(header, txs, receipts, rollup_cfg) -> L1Input` — filter-only,
  sysconfig-blind

Contract invariants encoded in types:
- `derive` never returns `Err`; malformed inputs surface as
  `TraceEntry::*Dropped` / `*Failed` entries.
- `add_*` only error on contract violations (non-contiguous L1, overlap
  range mismatch, unsolicited overlap, etc.).
- No `tracing::*` calls inside `pure/` — callers translate trace events.
- `extract_l1_input` does no fallible parsing; `L1Input` carries raw
  `Vec<Log>` and raw `(Address, Bytes)` calldata.
- `SpanBatchOverlapBlock.txs: Vec<Bytes>` — raw RLP throughout, no
  encode/decode round-trip in the overlap content check.
- `pure/` is `no_std`; verified by the workspace's
  `riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf` target.
- Every `match` on `Derivation` and `TraceEntry` inside `pure/` is
  exhaustive; strict typed reason enums everywhere, no `String` fields.

fix(op-supernode): anchor backfill end to verifiedDB on restart

After a wipe-logs restart the L2 op-node's StatusTracker briefly reports
SafeL2 at block 0 (the post-ResetEvent state, before the next
OnCrossSafeUpdate). runLogBackfill called resolveFirstVerifiableTimestamp
which read this live SafeL2 and computed endTime = activationTimestamp,
producing a degenerate one-block range covering only block 0. The
acceptance test TestSupernodeLogBackfill_HappyPath then failed with
"0 is not greater than 0" because first == latest == block 0.

The verifiedDB persists across the wipe because it lives in the supernode
data dir, not in the per-chain logs directories the wipe deletes. It is
the durable source of truth for the next timestamp the main loop will
verify — observeRound already picks NextTimestamp = LastTimestamp+1
whenever the verifiedDB is initialized. Anchor backfill's end to that
same value so a stale live SafeL2 cannot truncate the backfill range.

Refs: ethereum-optimism/optimism#20690

fix(kona/client): bump FPVM precompile oracle gas for Glamsterdam (EIP-7904)

Split the single gas constant in each FPVM-accelerated precompile into two
named values: the L2 gas charge (unchanged) and the oracle/L1 staticcall
gas required by EIP-7904, sent in the L1Precompile preimage hint.

Without this fix, once Glamsterdam activates on L1, the
`loadPrecompilePreimagePart` staticcall would silently OOG for KZG, BLS12-381
G1Add, G2Add, and bn256 pairing because the requiredGas embedded in the
preimage key would be below the post-7904 L1 cost. Higher-than-needed
oracle gas is always safe, so this can deploy proactively.

L2 gas charging (`EthPrecompileOutput::gas_used`) and the OOG guards
continue to use the existing values, preserving state-root agreement with
op-reth pre-revm-bump.

Affected (EIP-7904 L1 cost → embedded in oracle hint):
- KZG point eval (0x0a): 89_363
- BLS12-381 G1Add (0x0b): 643
- BLS12-381 G2Add (0x0d): 765
- bn256 pairing (0x08): 45_000 + 34_103 × k

Mirrors ethereum-optimism/optimism#19381 for kona-proof.

fix(op-devstack): progress-aware initial sync check for ELSync verifiers

The preset's initial CrossSafe match for ELSync-mode verifiers was a fixed
120-attempt poll (240s). Under CI resource contention, op-geth's beacon-driven
EL sync sometimes does not complete within that budget — the verifier's
unsafe head keeps advancing via CL gossip every 2s while the safe head stays
at 0 because the EL is still snap-syncing historical blocks. The whole
budget then burns and the test fails at setup.

Replace the fixed-attempt poll with a progress-aware wait: keep polling for
up to 8 minutes, but fail fast (within 30s) if the verifier's LocalUnsafe
head stops advancing. LocalUnsafe is driven by CL P2P gossip and is
independent of EL snap-sync, so a stall there means the test setup is
genuinely stuck and more waiting will not help. Successful runs still finish
in tens of seconds; only the worst-case CI runs use the extended window.

Refs #20649.

fix(op-node,op-batcher): fix maxSafeLag stall, resume, and channel timeout

The `--sequencer.max-safe-lag` feature was effectively non-functional due to
a state-management bug in the sequencer, compounded by a missing timeout
re-check in the batcher.

## Root Cause (op-node)

In `onForkchoiceUpdate`, the maxSafeLag check ran **before** the head-advancement
block. When a new block was confirmed (`UnsafeL2Head > latestHead`), the
head-advancement block unconditionally set `nextActionOK = true`, immediately
overriding the `nextActionOK = false` set by the maxSafeLag check. The sequencer
continued producing blocks regardless of the safe-head lag.

## Fix (op-node)

Move the maxSafeLag check to **after** the head-advancement block so it can
properly override `nextActionOK = true`. Additionally:

- **Stall/resume tracking**: Introduce a `stalledByMaxSafeLag` flag so the
  recovery branch only resumes sequencing when the stall was caused by
  maxSafeLag specifically. Without this, the resume logic would interfere with
  other `nextActionOK = false` states (pipeline reset, L1-derivation backoff,
  mid-seal wait).

- **Safe head catch-up recovery**: When the safe head catches up (gap drops
  below maxSafeLag), the sequencer automatically resumes via the
  `else if d.stalledByMaxSafeLag` branch. Uses `d.active.Load()` to match the
  resume pattern used throughout the file.

- **Runtime disable**: If an operator sets `maxSafeLag = 0` while the sequencer
  is stalled, the outer `else if d.stalledByMaxSafeLag` branch detects this and
  resumes immediately, preventing a permanent stall.

- **Lifecycle cleanup**: `stalledByMaxSafeLag` is cleared in `forceStart`,
  `onReset`, and `Stop` to prevent stale state across lifecycle transitions.

## Root Cause (op-batcher)

When the sequencer stalls and stops producing blocks, the batcher quickly
consumes all pending blocks into a channel (`pendingBlocks = 0`). In
`getReadyChannel`, the `pendingBlocks() == 0` early-return path skips
`registerL1Block()` — the only call site that checks channel duration timeout.
The channel never times out, never closes, and the data is never submitted to
L1, leaving the safe head permanently stuck.

## Fix (op-batcher)

When `pendingBlocks == 0` but a non-full channel exists, still call
`registerL1Block()` to re-evaluate the channel duration timeout. If the channel
times out, flush it immediately. Respects the `ignoreMaxChannelDuration` flag
for consistency with the normal path.

## Scenarios Covered

| Scenario | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| Gap exceeds maxSafeLag | Sequencer stalls, stops producing blocks |
| Safe head catches up | Sequencer auto-resumes |
| Batcher running, sequencer stalled | Channel times out via batcher fix, data submitted, safe head advances |
| Batcher restarted during stall | New channel created, data submitted quickly |
| maxSafeLag disabled at runtime | Sequencer resumes immediately |
| Pipeline reset during stall | Flag cleared, reset proceeds normally |
| Conductor failover | forceStart clears flag, new leader starts clean |

Fixes ethereum-optimism/optimism#17936

fix(kona/client): bump FPVM precompile oracle gas for Glamsterdam (EIP-7904) (#20689)

Split the single gas constant in each FPVM-accelerated precompile into two
named values: the L2 gas charge (unchanged) and the oracle/L1 staticcall
gas required by EIP-7904, sent in the L1Precompile preimage hint.

Without this fix, once Glamsterdam activates on L1, the
`loadPrecompilePreimagePart` staticcall would silently OOG for KZG, BLS12-381
G1Add, G2Add, and bn256 pairing because the requiredGas embedded in the
preimage key would be below the post-7904 L1 cost. Higher-than-needed
oracle gas is always safe, so this can deploy proactively.

L2 gas charging (`EthPrecompileOutput::gas_used`) and the OOG guards
continue to use the existing values, preserving state-root agreement with
op-reth pre-revm-bump.

Affected (EIP-7904 L1 cost → embedded in oracle hint):
- KZG point eval (0x0a): 89_363
- BLS12-381 G1Add (0x0b): 643
- BLS12-381 G2Add (0x0d): 765
- bn256 pairing (0x08): 45_000 + 34_103 × k

Mirrors ethereum-optimism/optimism#19381 for kona-proof.

fix(kona/protocol): grow output buffer on NeedsMoreInput-with-full-buffer (#20598)

When `available_in` and `available_out` reach 0 in the same iteration,
`BrotliDecompressStream` returns `NeedsMoreInput` with priority over
`NeedsMoreOutput`, even though it has more output to flush given more
buffer space. The previous loop treated this as "done" and returned the
partial buffer.

Go's `brotli.NewReader` doesn't have this issue because its bufio
indirection re-reads from the source on the next call, which gives brotli
a fresh output slice. So the kona wrapper bug surfaced as a Go vs Rust
derivation divergence on truncated brotli channels: kona produced
significantly fewer output bytes than op-node from the same input.

Treat the simultaneous full-buffer + exhausted-input state identically to
`NeedsMoreOutput`: at the size cap, stop (spec truncation); otherwise
grow the buffer and call brotli again. Brotli will signal
`NeedsMoreInput` again with non-zero `available_out` only when truly out
of input.

Add `test_decompress_truncated_matches_streaming_reader` which sweeps
truncations of a compressed stream and asserts kona's output matches the
brotli crate's high-level Reader byte-for-byte (matching what Go's
brotli.NewReader produces).

Refs ethereum-optimism/optimism#19333

op-supernode: redefine superroot_atTimestamp CurrentL1 as block being processed (#20687)

* op-supernode: redefine superroot_atTimestamp CurrentL1 as block being processed

CurrentL1 in the superroot_atTimestamp response previously meant "highest L1
block fully derived and verified by all chains". L1Inclusion is monotonic in
L2 timestamp, so the next unverified ts T_v+1 can share L1Inclusion(T_v) when
no chain's L1 source advanced — a consumer relying on aggregate.CurrentL1
≥ s.l1Head as proof that everything derivable from L1[≤s.l1Head] is verified
gets lied to whenever s.l1Head == L1Inclusion(T_v).

Match op-node's sync-status semantics instead: CurrentL1 names the L1 block
currently being processed by the slowest L1 processor in the supernode, so
L1[<CurrentL1] is fully processed. Consumers gating on "L1[≤X] fully
processed" require CurrentL1 > X.

No supernode logic change is needed — i.currentL1 = L1Inclusion(T_v) after
Advance is correct under the new meaning, and collectCurrentL1's min over
op-node CurrentL1 (also "being processed") stays consistent. op-challenger's
three ErrNotInSync gates in provider_supernode.go flip from `<` to `<=`.

op-challenger/runner game-input generation and op-proposer are intentionally
left alone: the runner's downstream logic compensates for an l1Head one block
high, and the proposer never gates on the equality case.

fix(op-supernode): stabilize superroot_atTimestamp Data field (#20658)

* fix(op-supernode): stabilize superroot_atTimestamp Data field

The verified branch of superroot_atTimestamp recomputed per-chain
OutputV0 from live L2 EL state on every call via VerifiedAt's safeDB
walkback + OutputRootAtL2BlockNumber. That meant an EL reorg or
cross-chain invalidation could change SuperRoot(T) for the same T
across calls, violating the stability invariant op-challenger needs
to play interop dispute games.

Rework so:

- Post-interop: source the canonical (chainID, blockHash) tuples from
  verifiedDB (the existing cross-safe write gate at interop.go:730)
  and read per-chain OutputV0 by hash from the L2 EL via a new
  OutputRootAtL2BlockHash on ChainContainer. Add dep-set sanity and a
  rewind-race coupling check.
- Pre-interop / interop disabled: compose Data by reusing the
  per-chain entries already built for the response's
  OptimisticAtTimestamp map — pre-interop, local-safe outputs cannot
  be invalidated, so the optimistic outputs ARE the canonical
  outputs. No second per-chain fetch; the regime is selected via a
  new sentinel interop.ErrNotActive returned by
  Interop.VerifiedResultAtTimestamp (and the new
  NoopVerifiedResultReader when interop is not configured).

Optimistic-branch chain-level transport errors continue to fail the
RPC under every regime — silently emitting a partial
OptimisticAtTimestamp map at step>0 would cause op-challenger to
commit InvalidTransition permanently on chain.

Deletes ChainContainer.VerifiedAt and ChainContainer.OutputRootAtL2BlockNumber
plus their test mocks. simpleChainContainer.safeDBAtL2 is preserved
(still used by OptimisticAt).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(op-supernode): distinguish below-verified-db regime in superroot_atTimestamp

Split the regime signal so the four cases for superroot_atTimestamp(T) are
distinguishable:

  - T < activationTimestamp           → ErrNotActive, compose Data from
                                        per-chain optimistic outputs
                                        (pre-interop blocks cannot be
                                        invalidated, so optimistic ≡ canonical)
  - T < firstVerifiableTimestamp      → ErrBeforeVerifiedDB, fail the RPC
                                        (no entry will ever exist on this
                                        node and no deny-list data is
                                        available to reconstruct from
                                        optimistic state)
  - verifiedDB entry present          → compose from VerifiedResult + EL
                                        by-hash; answer pinned to entry
  - verifiedDB.Get → NotFound         → ethereum.NotFound, return Data=nil
                                        and let CurrentL1 communicate
                                        verifier progress

Previously [activation, firstVerifiable) was folded into ErrNotActive and
fell through to the optimistic-fallback path. That was wrong: post-activation
the chain has been through interop validation elsewhere, but this node lacks
the deny-list entries to reproduce that state, so the optimistic outputs are
not guaranteed to match canonical.

Also tightens comments across the change to drop design-doc references and
change-history phrasing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(op-supernode): close verifiedDB/CurrentL1 read race in superroot_atTimestamp

Without an atomic read across both, the response could pair a stale
aggregate CurrentL1 with a fresh verifiedDB observation (or vice versa):

  - Reader: aggregate.CurrentL1 = high
  - Writer: rewind drops i.currentL1 to 0, then deletes verifiedDB row
  - Reader: verifiedDB.Get → NotFound
  → response {CurrentL1: high, Data: nil} — caller reads as "passed
    required L1 with no entry → final negative" but the entry existed
    moments ago.

The symmetric race exists in the commit direction (entry committed,
then currentL1 advanced, between the two reads), so simply reordering
doesn't help.

VerifiedResultReader.VerifiedResultAtTimestamp now returns the verifier's
CurrentL1 captured under the same RLock as the verifiedDB.Get. The
superroot handler reports min(aggregate.CurrentL1, snapshotL1) and feeds
the same value to the rewind-race coupling check. The verifier's existing
mutation ordering — commit writes the entry before advancing currentL1;
rewind zeroes currentL1 before deleting rows — combined with the atomic
read guarantees a consistent snapshot.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(op-supernode): drop rewind-race coupling check in superroot_atTimestamp

The previous check refused to return Data when the response's CurrentL1
was below the entry's VerifiedRequiredL1 (e.g. mid-rewind, where the
verifier has rolled CurrentL1 back but the entry has not yet been
deleted). With the atomic (verifiedDB, currentL1) snapshot in place,
that pair is internally consistent — it accurately says "this entry
was committed but the verifier is currently at a lower L1." Callers
gate trust on CurrentL1 themselves, so returning the data is more
useful than erroring.

The safe-head startup handoff covers timestamps below firstVerifiable, so
treat them like the pre-activation regime: build Data from per-chain
optimistic outputs instead of returning a hard RPC error. This restores
the contract that the chain container's VerifiedAt previously upheld
(returning verified=true trivially below firstVerifiable) and fixes
TestSuperRootScript in op-e2e/actions/interop.

Also clears two lint failures left over from removed tests: a goimports
nit in superroot_test.go and the now-unused mockVerificationActivity in
chain_container_test.go.

* fix(op-supernode): guard VerifiedResultAtTimestamp against pre-Start nil ctx

Supernode registers each activity's RPC API before scheduling its Start
goroutine, so a superroot_atTimestamp call can reach the interop reader
in the microseconds-wide window before i.ctx is populated, panicking on
a nil-context dereference inside firstVerifiableTimestamp.

Add an ErrNotStarted sentinel and route it through the same optimistic
composition fallback used for ErrNotActive / ErrBeforeVerifiedDB, so the

fix(op-supernode): resume from verifiedDB unconditionally on warm restart

Gating warm-restart resume on EL finalized rejects the normal case where
cross-safe (and therefore verifiedDB.LastTimestamp) is ahead of finalized,
and it also blocks sequencer-side liveness — the sequencer must produce
blocks before L1 finality can advance.

When verifiedDB is initialized, resume at LastTimestamp + 1 unconditionally.
If EL finalized happens to be ahead (e.g. EL restored from snapshot while
supernode was offline), the main loop rolls forward through it; finalized
blocks cannot contain invalid exec messages.

On cold start, anchor on min EL finalized head + 1 (clamped to activation).
A finalized head at genesis (Number == 0) with a real hash is a valid
anchor — only reject the zero-value response that signals an EL that
isn't ready yet. The previous "Number == 0" guard rejected genesis and
caused op-e2e action tests to hang forever during supernode startup.

The "verifiedDB ahead of canonical L2" failure mode (e.g. a local L2 reorg
invalidating a prior commit) cannot be detected via finalized — that needs
a tip-hash check against the EL block-by-number lookup, out of scope here.

fix(op-acceptance-tests): stabilize TestFollowSource_HeadsDivergeThenConverge

Cross-safety only commits at L2 timestamps where every chain in the
interop set has a local-safe block. With a 2s block time, stopping two
sequencers via sequential RPCs lets the leader sneak in one extra
block while the laggard is still being told to stop (the gap was ~80ms
in the original CI failure, well over the inter-block window in the
race). The laggard then never produces a block at that timestamp, so
the supernode verifier stalls at the laggard's last timestamp. The
follower for the leader chain ends up with local-safe at the extra
block but cross-safe stuck a block behind, and the convergence wait in
the test times out.

Replace the two sequential StopSequencer calls with a new
dsl.StopSequencersSynced helper that issues all stops concurrently and
then aligns the chains: any sequencer below the maximum unsafe head is
restarted just long enough to produce the missing block(s) and stopped
again. The alignment loop is bounded so a real bug fails fast instead
of hanging. Chains in the same interop set share a genesis time and
block time, so equal unsafe numbers imply equal timestamps and the
verifier can advance.

Refs ethereum-optimism/optimism#19821

refactor(dsl): align StopSequencersSynced by timestamp, not block number

The previous implementation aligned chains by unsafe-head block number, which
only equals timestamp alignment when chains share genesis time AND block time.
That assumption holds for the current acceptance-test presets but is not
generally true for Superchain interop sets, where member chains can have
different rollup configs.

Cross-safety only cares about timestamps: the verifier walks one L2 timestamp
at a time and requires every chain to have a local-safe block at that
timestamp. Aligning by timestamp is therefore both correct and strictly more
general.

Drop the docstring claim about shared genesis/block time, and switch the
leader/level-up comparison plus log fields to timestamps. No behaviour change
for chains with identical configs (the only current call site).
refactor(dsl): align StopSequencersSynced by timestamp, not block number

refactor: align chains via TestSequencer instead of a new DSL helper

The start/poll/stop level-up approach in StopSequencersSynced is fundamentally
racy: a restarted sequencer produces a burst of catch-up blocks faster than any
sane poll interval, so stopping at exactly the target block is unreliable.

Use TestSequencer.SequenceBlock instead, which builds exactly one block at
parent.Time + blockTime deterministically. The test now stops both sequencers
and then drives the trailing chain up to the leader's timestamp with
single-block SequenceBlock calls — no restart, no overshoot risk.

Drop dsl.StopSequencersSynced entirely; it has no remaining callers and the
TestSequencer path is strictly better for presets that expose one.

fix(kona-proof-interop/boot): reject future-timestamped prestate (#20727)

Add an `assert!` in `BootInfo::load` rejecting any agreed pre-state whose
timestamp exceeds `claimed_l2_timestamp`. The honest actor never agrees to
such a pre-state; op-program panics on the same condition (see
`op-program/client/interop/interop.go:87-97`). Without this guard, a
malicious proposer could register a future-timestamped SuperRoot or
TransitionState preimage (the oracle only verifies
`key == keccak256(preimage)`, not the timestamp inside) and commit the
same hash as both starting and disputed claim at trace-extended bisection
positions, where kona's `claim == prestate => Ok(())` arm would resolve
as `vmStatus = VALID`.

With the guard, both arms of `interop::run` only need to handle the
legitimate `==` boundary; tighten `>=` to `==` accordingly to make intent
explicit.

Tests:
- Flip
`trace_extension_transition_state_past_game_timestamp_accepts_matching_claim`
  to `#[should_panic]`; its previous assertion pinned the buggy lenient
  behavior. The flipped version is now the regression guard for the
  TransitionState arm.
- Add `rejects_super_root_with_timestamp_after_game_timestamp` as the
  symmetric guard for the SuperRoot arm.
- Refactor `setup_interop_preimages` to take a `PreState` so both arms
  reuse the fixture.

Resolves the "narrow both kona arms to `==`" follow-up flagged in #20717.

feat(op-supernode): add raft-wal-backed LogsDB implementation

Adds a new raftwallogdb sub-package implementing the LogsDB interface on top
of hashicorp/raft-wal. Each sealed block is stored as a single raft-wal entry
whose payload is a fixed-width binary header followed by a logHash array and
an execMsg array, so Contains is an O(1) memcpy regardless of how many logs
the block carries. StoreLog fsyncs the entry to disk before returning, so
SealBlock is durable on return and atomic with any pending logs buffered by
AddLog.

fix(raftwallogdb): align error contract with op-supervisor logs DB

Audit of error-type divergences between the original op-supervisor logs DB
and the new raft-wal-backed implementation surfaced several behaviour
differences that downstream consumers (op-supernode, op-interop-filter)
implicitly depend on. Reconciled to match the old contract:

- Pass-through transient read errors from GetLog/readBlockAt instead of
  wrapping them as ErrDataCorruption. Real structural corruption (short
  buffer in decodeBlockRecord, length checks on entry data) keeps the
  ErrDataCorruption tag.
- OpenBlock returns ErrSkipped at blockNum == firstBlock when firstBlock
  is non-zero, matching the old DB so op-supernode's algo.go fallback
  remains a no-op replica of the success path. Tracked for cleanup in
  ethereum-optimism/optimism#20726.
- AddLog rejects parentBlock == eth.BlockID{} with ErrOutOfOrder. Genesis
  blocks cannot carry receipts; structurally enforces the invariant at
  the write boundary so Contains does not need a read-path guard.
- AddLog parent-identity mismatches return ErrOutOfOrder (was
  ErrConflict). Matches old DB. Prevents op-interop-filter's
  ErrorConflict failsafe from tripping on transient state-disagreement.
- SealBlock block-number gap and backwards-timestamp now return
  ErrConflict (were ErrOutOfOrder). Matches old DB. Restores
  op-interop-filter's failsafe trip on structural desync.
- Removed the dead raft.ErrLogNotFound tolerance in clearLocked.
  raft-wal's DeleteRange does not produce that sentinel — it returns nil
  for ranges outside the stored log.

Test fixtures using blockID(0, 0x00) collided with eth.BlockID{} (real
chains never have a zero genesis hash); switched to blockID(0, 0xA0).

fix(op-devstack): progress-aware initial sync check for ELSync verifiers (#20652)

The preset's initial CrossSafe match for ELSync-mode verifiers was a fixed
120-attempt poll (240s). Under CI resource contention, op-geth's beacon-driven
EL sync sometimes does not complete within that budget — the verifier's
unsafe head keeps advancing via CL gossip every 2s while the safe head stays
at 0 because the EL is still snap-syncing historical blocks. The whole
budget then burns and the test fails at setup.

Replace the fixed-attempt poll with a progress-aware wait: keep polling for
up to 8 minutes, but fail fast (within 30s) if the verifier's LocalUnsafe
head stops advancing. LocalUnsafe is driven by CL P2P gossip and is
independent of EL snap-sync, so a stall there means the test setup is
genuinely stuck and more waiting will not help. Successful runs still finish
in tens of seconds; only the worst-case CI runs use the extended window.

Refs #20649.

fix(op-node,op-batcher): fix maxSafeLag stall, resume, and channel ti… (#19758)

* fix(op-node,op-batcher): fix maxSafeLag stall, resume, and channel timeout

The `--sequencer.max-safe-lag` feature was effectively non-functional due to
a state-management bug in the sequencer, compounded by a missing timeout
re-check in the batcher.

## Root Cause (op-node)

In `onForkchoiceUpdate`, the maxSafeLag check ran **before** the head-advancement
block. When a new block was confirmed (`UnsafeL2Head > latestHead`), the
head-advancement block unconditionally set `nextActionOK = true`, immediately
overriding the `nextActionOK = false` set by the maxSafeLag check. The sequencer
continued producing blocks regardless of the safe-head lag.

## Fix (op-node)

Move the maxSafeLag check to **after** the head-advancement block so it can
properly override `nextActionOK = true`. Additionally:

- **Stall/resume tracking**: Introduce a `stalledByMaxSafeLag` flag so the
  recovery branch only resumes sequencing when the stall was caused by
  maxSafeLag specifically. Without this, the resume logic would interfere with
  other `nextActionOK = false` states (pipeline reset, L1-derivation backoff,
  mid-seal wait).

- **Safe head catch-up recovery**: When the safe head catches up (gap drops
  below maxSafeLag), the sequencer automatically resumes via the
  `else if d.stalledByMaxSafeLag` branch. Uses `d.active.Load()` to match the
  resume pattern used throughout the file.

- **Runtime disable**: If an operator sets `maxSafeLag = 0` while the sequencer
  is stalled, the outer `else if d.stalledByMaxSafeLag` branch detects this and
  resumes immediately, preventing a permanent stall.

- **Lifecycle cleanup**: `stalledByMaxSafeLag` is cleared in `forceStart`,
  `onReset`, and `Stop` to prevent stale state across lifecycle transitions.

## Root Cause (op-batcher)

When the sequencer stalls and stops producing blocks, the batcher quickly
consumes all pending blocks into a channel (`pendingBlocks = 0`). In
`getReadyChannel`, the `pendingBlocks() == 0` early-return path skips
`registerL1Block()` — the only call site that checks channel duration timeout.
The channel never times out, never closes, and the data is never submitted to
L1, leaving the safe head permanently stuck.

## Fix (op-batcher)

When `pendingBlocks == 0` but a non-full channel exists, still call
`registerL1Block()` to re-evaluate the channel duration timeout. If the channel
times out, flush it immediately. Respects the `ignoreMaxChannelDuration` flag
for consistency with the normal path.

## Scenarios Covered

| Scenario | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| Gap exceeds maxSafeLag | Sequencer stalls, stops producing blocks |
| Safe head catches up | Sequencer auto-resumes |
| Batcher running, sequencer stalled | Channel times out via batcher fix, data submitted, safe head advances |
| Batcher restarted during stall | New channel created, data submitted quickly |
| maxSafeLag disabled at runtime | Sequencer resumes immediately |
| Pipeline reset during stall | Flag cleared, reset proceeds normally |
| Conductor failover | forceStart clears flag, new leader starts clean |

Fixes ethereum-optimism/optimism#17936

fix(op-node): tolerate NotFound on Finalized lookup during ELSync

In ELSync mode the verifier op-node's execution engine has no finalized
(and often no safe) L2 block until its initial snap-sync completes and
the CL emits a finalized FCU. Today, initializeUnknowns returns an error
for the NotFound case on eth.Finalized — which the engine queue surfaces
as "Engine temporary error: cannot update engine until engine forkchoice
is initialized: failed to load finalized head: not found" once per
derivation tick. On a typical recurrence of #20649 this is hundreds of
warnings in a single test run, crowding out the real signal in CI logs.

Mirror the existing eth.Safe NotFound fallback: in ELSync mode treat the
NotFound on eth.Finalized as "no finalized block yet", leaving the
FinalizedHead at zero and continuing. The next initializeUnknowns call
retries the lookup; once snap-sync completes and the CL drives the
engine through its first finalized FCU, the lookup succeeds and the
head is populated.

Also harden the safe-fallback path: if both finalized and safe come
back NotFound, skip the misleading "Loaded initial local-safe block
from finalized local_safe=0x0...:0" log and let the next retry populate
both refs.

CLSync mode preserves the prior error behavior — after the initial
reset the engine is expected to have a valid finalized block, and
NotFound there indicates an unexpected state worth surfacing.

Refs: #20649

fix(sync-tester): clear WindowSyncPolicy cache on session reset

TestMultiELSync flakes because session.ResetSession was leaving the
ELSyncPolicy.cache untouched. When L2CL2's verifier op-node manages to
push a NewPayload + FCU to the SyncTester before sys.L2CL2.Stop() returns,
the WindowSyncPolicy cache ends up holding the payload number from that
in-flight call (commonly 2). ResetSession clears Validated, CurrentState,
and Payloads, but the policy's private cache survives — so the test's
first FCU(targetNum-2 = 3) immediately forms the consecutive sequence
[2,3] required by cnt=2, the policy returns Valid, and session.Validated
jumps to 3. The follow-up NewPayload(targetNum-1 = 4) then returns VALID
instead of SYNCING, hitting the assertion at sync_test.go:60. The race is
intermittent because it depends on how far L2CL2's engine driver has
progressed when Stop() is invoked.

Acceptance tests on memory-all-opn-op-reth (and the op-geth/kona variants)
write devnet state to /tmp on the runner's real disk. When many in-process
tests run in parallel, op-reth's mdbx commit waits on fsync and stalls — we

cascades that failed ~36 unrelated tests in one merge-queue run.
