feat(op-supernode): re-insert canonical payload during engine rewind

When rewinding the engine for DecisionRewind/DecisionInvalidate, the existing
flow inserted a synthetic block and FCU'd to it, then FCU'd back to the
original target block. The target block was no longer canonical between those
two FCUs, which lets op-reth's pruner discard it and breaks the second FCU.

Re-insert the canonical target payload via engine_newPayload immediately
before the second FCU so the EL is guaranteed to still have the block.

Also short-circuit RewindToTimestamp when the chain is not actually ahead of
the target, and treat ethereum.NotFound from L2BlockRefByNumber in
InvalidateBlock as "already rewound — nothing to do".

If the EL has not yet produced a block at the requested rewind target,
L2BlockRefByNumber returns ethereum.NotFound — there is nothing to rewind.
errors.Is(err, ethereum.NotFound) survives the RPC jump via
eth.MaybeAsNotFoundErr, which the L2 client wraps every block-fetch
response with.

feat(op-supernode): WAL canonical payloads for rewind / invalidate operations

The previous design left a window where the engine could not safely complete
a rewind across a crash: after the synthetic FCU made the target block
non-canonical, the EL (op-reth in particular) was free to prune it. On
recovery, fetching the canonical block at the rewind height by number would
return the synthetic block instead of the original target, and fetching by
hash could return NotFound.

This change makes the supernode WAL the authoritative source for the rewind
target:

- RewindPlan gains TargetPayloads (canonical envelope per chain at the rewind
  target). PendingTransition gains InvalidationParentPayloads (parent
  envelope per invalidated chain).
- Build paths fetch each chain's canonical payload by hash at decision time —
  while the block is still canonical — and persist it in the WAL. Any fetch
  failure aborts the build; the decision is re-evaluated next round.
- Apply paths use the WAL'd payloads exclusively. The engine controller no
  longer consults the live EL to discover the target.
- engine.Rewind(ctx, target) replaces RewindToTimestamp. The synthetic block
  is derived from the supplied target, and the same target is re-inserted via
  engine_newPayload between the synthetic and target FCUs to guarantee EL
  durability across pruning.

InvalidateBlock and RewindEngine now take the target envelope explicitly so
the WAL contract reaches all the way down to the engine controller. Tests
have been updated to register canonical payloads through a harness helper
that mirrors verifiedDB commits onto the chain mocks.

feat(op-supernode): drive invalidation reorg via safe-head cap on reset

Replaces the synchronous op-reth rewind (debug-grade FCU + synthetic
ExtraData payload + retry loop) with a deny-list-only invalidation path.
On DecisionInvalidate, op-supernode persists the deny entry; when the VN
restarts, op-node's reset path consults
SuperAuthority.CanonicalDeniedHeight and caps the safe (and finalized)
head to (height - 1) before any FCU is issued. Derivation re-derives the
denied block, payload_process.go's IsDenied check fires, deposits-only
attributes replace the block, and the unsafe chain is reorged by op-reth
on the resulting FCU.

- Adds DenyList.CanonicalDeniedHeight (top-down walk, returns lowest
  still-canonical denied height) and SuperAuthority.CanonicalDeniedHeight.
- Adds sync.ApplyDenyCap wired into currentHeads, initializeUnknowns,
  and L2HeadsForELSyncWithOffset. Unsafe is intentionally not capped;
  the mismatch against the still-canonical denied block is what drives
  consolidation to issue BuildStartEvent and reorg op-reth.
- Renames InvalidateBlock → RecordInvalidation; drops the rewind branch
  and the L2BlockRefByNumber canonicality probe. Refuses zero StateRoot /
  MessagePasserStorageRoot at the boundary (preimages are captured during
  verify in newInvalidHead).
- applyPendingTransition now resumes invalidated chains first (so their
  VNs restart and the cap fires) before non-invalidated chains.
- onPayloadSuccess's replacement-block path emits CriticalErrorEvent if
  the replacement is itself on the deny list — preventing a reorg loop.

Finalized is capped defensively even though invariants of the interop
verifier (VerifiedDB only records DecisionAdvance) preclude a denied
block being finalized; capping locally keeps `finalized <= safe`
obvious to callers.

fix(op-node): check IsDenied in consolidateNextSafeAttributes

The safe-head cap alone wasn't enough to reorg the unsafe chain when a
denied block was already canonical. After the cap, derivation re-built
the bad block's attributes deterministically from its L1 batch and
AttributesMatchBlock matched them against the still-canonical unsafe
block — silently promoting the denied block back to safe via
TryUpdatePendingSafe. IsDenied never fired on this path because
PayloadProcessEvent isn't emitted for the consolidation-match case.

Inject the deny check into consolidateNextSafeAttributes before
AttributesMatchBlock: when the existing unsafe block at the consolidation
height is on the deny list AND the derived attributes are not already
deposits-only, emit DepositsOnlyPayloadAttributesRequestEvent. Derivation
then produces deposits-only attributes whose transactions differ from the
bad block, AttributesMatchBlock returns mismatch, and BuildStartEvent
issues the FCU + newPayload that reorgs op-reth.

The `!IsDepositsOnly()` guard prevents an infinite loop: once derivation
has produced the deposits-only attributes for this height, the second
pass through consolidation must fall through to the match check (which
fails on tx-count mismatch) rather than re-requesting another rebuild.

Also update the docstring on initializeUnknowns to reflect the new
deny-list cap behaviour and drop the stale op-supervisor reference.

fix(op-node): fail closed on deny-list check error in consolidation

Previously logged the error and proceeded with AttributesMatchBlock —
which can silently promote a denied block to safe if the existing unsafe
block happens to match the derived attributes. Surface an
EngineTemporaryErrorEvent instead so the caller retries on the next
pipeline step. The deny-list entry itself is already durable (bbolt
fsync); the error only signals a transient inability to read it.

Adds a unit test asserting no AttributesMatchBlock call, no
TryUpdatePendingSafe, and an EngineTemporaryErrorEvent emission when
SuperAuthority.IsDenied errors during consolidation.
fix(op-node): fail closed on deny-list check error in consolidation

fix(op-node): only apply deny-cap during initial head load

initializeUnknowns runs on every tryUpdateEngineInternal iteration. The
previous version applied the deny-list cap unconditionally whenever
localSafeHead was non-zero, which caused an oscillation loop:

1. consolidateNextSafeAttributes detects denied unsafe block → emits
   DepositsOnlyPayloadAttributesRequestEvent → pipeline produces
   deposits-only attrs → BuildStartEvent → op-reth builds and inserts
   the replacement block on its fork chain.
2. PayloadSuccess path advances engine controller's localSafeHead to
   the new deposits-only block.
3. Before op-reth commits the canonical-chain swap (a few ms later),
   tryUpdateEngineInternal fires initializeUnknowns again.
4. Cap calls L2BlockRefByNumber on the denied height: op-reth's
   canonical chain still briefly reports the bad block, so the cap
   considers it canonical and rolls localSafeHead back over the
   just-built replacement.
5. Derivation re-runs from the rolled-back safe, re-derives the bad
   block from the original L1 batch, AttributesMatchBlock fails
   against the deposits-only unsafe, BuildStartEvent rebuilds the bad
   block as canonical, and we're back at step 1.

Gate the cap on safeJustLoaded || finalizedJustLoaded so it only fires
when this exact call loaded a head from EL labels — the explicit
fresh-state case. Subsequent iterations (the common case) skip the cap
entirely. The onResetEngineRequest → FindL2Heads path still runs the
cap on its own freshly-read EL labels.

fix(op-node): stall consolidate on NotFound during EL sync

When op-node receives a future unsafe payload via gossip during EL sync,
the EL accepts it as a sync target and returns SYNCING. Derivation then
tries to consolidate the next safe block against the unsafe chain, but
the EL doesn't have pending_safe+1 yet, so PayloadByNumber returns
NotFound.

Previously this triggered a derivation pipeline reset. The reset's
forkchoiceUpdated re-targets the EL away from its in-flight sync target,
and the next gossiped payload moves it back — producing a thrash loop
where EL sync never finishes and local safe never advances.

When the engine reports IsEngineInitialELSyncing, treat NotFound at
pending_safe+1 as a transient condition and emit
EngineTemporaryErrorEvent instead of ResetEvent. The attributes stay
queued and consolidation retries on the next pending-safe poke, by
which point EL sync should have filled in the block. Outside EL sync,
NotFound still triggers the existing reset.

feat(op-node): serve superroot_atTimestamp for non-interop chains

Add a new `superroot` JSON-RPC namespace on op-node with method
`AtTimestamp(timestamp)`, mirroring op-supernode's wire contract
exactly so existing clients (op-challenger, op-dispute-mon) can
point `--supernode-rpc` at op-node URL on non-interop chains.

The handler reuses op-node primitives only — driver SyncStatus +
BlockRefWithStatus, l2EthClient OutputV0AtBlock, and the shared
safedb.L1AtSafeHead walkback — to construct a single-chain
SuperRootAtTimestampResponse byte-compatible with op-supernode's
output for the same chain.

Field semantics are documented in code:

  - CurrentSafeTimestamp / CurrentLocalSafeTimestamp / CurrentFinalizedTimestamp
    pulled directly from SyncStatus, matching op-supernode's per-field
    aggregation collapsed to one chain.
  - VerifiedRequiredL1 (and OptimisticAtTimestamp[chainID].RequiredL1
    on the verified branch) come from safedb.L1AtSafeHead — this is
    the value op-challenger compares against l1Head to gate
    InvalidTransition, so it is correctness-critical, not perf.
  - Optimistic-only branch (block beyond LocalSafeL2 but within UnsafeL2)
    uses the L2 block's L1Origin as RequiredL1, mirroring op-supernode.
  - Pre-genesis / beyond-UnsafeL2 / safeDB-not-found all degrade to
    populated sync fields with Data nil — never zero-out the response
    on transport errors (consumers check CurrentL1.Number first).

Per the issue's resolution by @ajsutton, no activation gate: the API
behaves the same pre- and post-Interop, since a single-chain super
root is well-defined at any timestamp.

Unit tests cover: pre-genesis, beyond-unsafe, optimistic-only,
verified happy path, safeDB-not-found fallback, driver/output
errors, and a runtime SuperRootProvider conformance check (mirror
of op-challenger's and op-dispute-mon's consumer interface).

The compatibility check uses a test-only adapter rather than adding
a SuperRootAtTimestamp method to the live struct — go-ethereum
auto-registers exported methods on RPC services, so a method on the
live struct would leak `superroot_superRootAtTimestamp` as a wire
method. The test-only adapter keeps the wire surface to exactly
`superroot_atTimestamp`.

Refs: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20552

eth: implement EIP-7975 (eth/70 - partial block receipt lists) (#33153)

In this PR, we add support for protocol version eth/70, defined by EIP-7975.

Overall changes:

- Each response is buffered in the peer’s receipt buffer when the
`lastBlockIncomplete` field is true.
- Continued request uses the same request id of its original
  request(`RequestPartialReceipts`).
- Partial responses are verified in `validateLastBlockReceipt`.
- Even if all receipts for partial blocks of the request are collected,
  those partial results are not sinked to the downloader, to avoid
  complexity. This assumes that partial response and buffering occur only
  in exceptional cases.

beacon/light: keep retrying checkpoint init if failed (#33966)

This PR changes the blsync checkpoint init logic so that even if the
initialization fails with a certain server and an error log message is
printed, the server goes back to its initial state and is allowed to
retry initialization after the failure delay period. The previous logic
had an `ssDone` server state that did put the server in a permanently
unusable state once the checkpoint init failed for an apparently
permanent reason. This was not the correct behavior because different
servers behave differently in case of overload and sometimes the
response to a permanently missing item is not clearly distinguishable
from an overload response. A safer logic is to never assume anything to
be permanent and always give a chance to retry.
The failure delay formula is also fixed; now it is properly capped at
`maxFailureDelay`. The previous formula did allow the delay to grow
unlimited if a retry was attempted immediately after each delay period.

triedb/pathdb: implement history index pruner (#33999)

This PR implements the missing functionality for archive nodes by 
pruning stale index data.

The current mechanism is relatively simple but sufficient for now: 
it periodically iterates over index entries and deletes outdated data 
on a per-block basis. 

The pruning process is triggered every 90,000 new blocks (approximately 
every 12 days), and the iteration typically takes ~30 minutes on a 
mainnet node.

This mechanism is only applied with `gcmode=archive` enabled, having
no impact on normal full node.

core/state: introduce state iterator interface (#33102)

In this PR, the Database interface in `core/state` has been extended
with one more function:

```go
	// Iteratee returns a state iteratee associated with the specified state root,
	// through which the account iterator and storage iterator can be created.
	Iteratee(root common.Hash) (Iteratee, error)
```

With this additional abstraction layer, the implementation details can be hidden
behind the interface. For example, state traversal can now operate directly on 
the flat state for Verkle or binary trees, which do not natively support traversal.

Moreover, state dumping will now prefer using the flat state iterator as
the primary option, offering better efficiency.


Edit: this PR also fixes a tiny issue in the state dump, marshalling the
next field in the correct way.

triedb/pathdb: skip duplicate-root layer insertion (#34642)

PathDB keys diff layers by state root, not by block hash. That means a
side-chain block can legitimately collide with an existing canonical diff layer
when both blocks produce the same post-state (for example same parent, 
same coinbase, no txs).

Today `layerTree.add` blindly inserts that second layer. If the root
already exists, this overwrites `tree.layers[root]` and appends the same 
root to the mutation lookup again. Later account/storage lookups resolve 
that root to the wrong diff layer, which can corrupt reads for descendant 
canonical states.

At runtime, the corruption is silent: no error is logged and no invariant check
fires. State reads against affected descendants simply return stale data
from the wrong diff layer (for example, an account balance that reflects one
fewer block reward), which can propagate into RPC responses and block 
validation.

This change makes duplicate-root inserts idempotent. A second layer with
the same state root does not add any new retrievable state to a tree that is
already keyed by root; keeping the original layer preserves the existing parent 
chain and avoids polluting the lookup history with duplicate roots.

The regression test imports a canonical chain of two layers followed by
a fork layer at height 1 with the same state root but a different block hash. 
Before the fix, account and storage lookups at the head resolve the fork 
layer instead of the canonical one. After the fix, the duplicate insert is 
skipped and lookups remain correct.

feat(op-node): default syncmode.offset-el-safe to 12h

Set --syncmode.offset-el-safe to a nonzero default so safe and finalized
heads no longer collapse onto the unsafe tip when EL sync completes (the
correctness bug from #17631).

12h matches the OP Mainnet sequencing window: past the seq window,
derivation can deterministically validate the retracted range, giving
the minimum offset that restores safe/finalized correctness without
demanding the multi-day derivation backlog a 168h default would impose.

warning and zero the offset instead of erroring, so the new default is
non-breaking for CL-sync deployments.

test(op-supernode/interop): reproduce FinalizedL2 regression across activation

Adds a failing acceptance test for ethereum-optimism/optimism#20365.

During interop activation, optimism_syncStatus.finalized_l2 can briefly
snap back to genesis once LocalSafeL2 crosses activation but the verifier
has no L1-finalized post-activation entry yet. The layer above interprets
the verifier's empty answer as "no information" and resolves FinalizedL2
to genesis instead of the perfectly valid pre-activation local-finalized
head.

The test traps documented in the issue are all closed:

- 240s activation delay (exceeds the FakePoS 20-block / ~120s L1 finality
  lag) so the pre-activation FinalizedL2 baseline is non-zero
- explicit wait for FinalizedL2 > 0 before snapshotting
- helper refuses to run with a zero baseline or a baseline already past
  the target time, so a future preset change can't quietly re-vacuum the
  assertion (0 >= 0)

Currently fails on develop after #21002 with:
  finalized head regressed: was 5 (..., t=...396), observed 0 (..., t=...386)

test(op-supernode/interop): derive observation window from target time

ReachedTimeWithoutRegressionFn no longer takes an attempts parameter — the
poll runs until either the head reaches targetTime, the surrounding test
context cancels, or a wall-clock deadline elapses. The deadline is
computed from targetTime plus a 5-minute buffer that covers the L1
finality lag (relevant for safety.Finalized) and ordinary test-runner
slowness, so callers can't accidentally pick an attempts count too small
for the boundary they're observing.
test(op-supernode/interop): derive observation window from target time

test(op-supernode/interop): simplify deadline calculation

Express the wait deadline as targetTime + buffer directly, instead of
deriving (targetTime - now) and re-adding it to now.

test(op-supernode/interop): use require.Eventuallyf for the poll loop

Replaces the hand-rolled sleep+poll loop with require.Eventuallyf. The
100ms tick still ensures a brief FinalizedL2 regression cannot slip
between observations, and a captured error makes the regression case
return early through the CheckFunc contract rather than waiting out the
full window.
test(op-supernode/interop): use require.Eventuallyf for the poll loop

fix(op-supernode/interop): gate finalized fallback on FinalizedL2.Time

FinalizedL2Head fell back to local-finalized only while LocalSafeL2 was
pre-activation. Once LocalSafeL2 crossed activation but the verifier had
no L1-finalized post-activation entry yet, FinalizedL2 regressed to
genesis until the verifier caught up (#20365).

Gating on the currently-published FinalizedL2 timestamp instead keeps
the fallback active until the verifier has authoritative finalized data.
Self-correcting: a spurious genesis observation is itself pre-activation
and re-fires the fallback on the next forkchoice update.

Also tightens the doc comments added earlier on this branch.

The pre-activation fallback now gates on FinalizedL2.Time instead of

fix(op-supernode): retry RewindEngine on DeadlineExceeded

The synthetic FCU in the rewind path can take minutes against a slow
execution layer (op-reth in particular). When the engine's per-call RPC
deadline fires, engine.Rewind returns context.DeadlineExceeded even
though the caller's interop-transition ctx still has budget.

Previously the retry loop in RewindEngine bailed immediately on
DeadlineExceeded. Treat it as a transient error instead and rely on the
existing ctx.Done() select to stop the loop when the caller's ctx is
actually done.

refactor(kona/service): move cancellation out of actors; replace start with step; split engine actor

Selectively port the cancellation-token ownership changes from
ethereum-optimism/optimism#19141 without adopting that PR's Builder /
InboundData / init() trait pattern.

NodeActor trait:
- Replace `start(self, ctx) -> Result<(), Error>` with
  `step(&mut self) -> Result<(), Error>`.
- Drop the StartData associated type and the CancellableContext trait.
- The orchestrator macro (`spawn_and_wait!`) now owns the umbrella
  CancellationToken, the loop, and the select! against `cancelled()`;
  no actor sees a cancellation primitive.

Actor migrations:
- Derivation, DelegateDerivation, L1Watcher, Sequencer: drop the
  cancellation_token field + CancellableContext impl; move loop-local
  state onto self (tickers, payload-to-seal, last seal duration, etc).
- Network: take a live NetworkHandler at construction; build/start the
  libp2p swarm in RollupNode::start so the constructor stays sync. The
  NetworkInboundData bundle is deleted in favor of injecting senders
  individually.
- Rpc: become non-generic. Module assembly and the initial server
  launch move upstream; the actor holds config + modules + handle and
  relaunches up to RpcBuilder::restart_count on stop. A Drop impl calls
  ServerHandle::stop() so graceful cancellation shuts the jsonrpsee
  server cleanly.

Engine actor restructure:
- The fan-out EngineActor (which only routed EngineActorRequest
  variants into one of two sub-tasks) is deleted.
- EngineProcessor is promoted to EngineActor; EngineRpcProcessor is
  promoted to EngineRpcActor. Both run as first-class peers under
  spawn_and_wait!.
- EngineProcessingRequest takes over the freed name EngineActorRequest;
  the old fan-out EngineActorRequest enum and its RpcRequest variant
  are deleted (the rpc client sends EngineRpcRequest directly).
- EngineRequestReceiver and EngineRpcRequestReceiver placeholder traits
  (testing-only scaffolding per their own doc comments) are deleted.
- No more JoinHandle polling, is_finished() checks, or PhantomData
  generics in the engine actors.

RollupNode::start:
- Single CancellationToken owned by the macro; no actor receives it.
- All cross-actor channels (mpsc + watch) created at the top of start()
  in one visually-grouped block.
- Actor construction broken out into five build_* helpers
  (build_engine_actors, build_derivation_actor, build_l1_watcher,
  build_sequencer, build_rpc_actor) plus three private type aliases.
- create_engine_actor helper deleted (inlined into build_engine_actors).

External callers:
- bin/node and examples/gossip: build the swarm handler upstream and
  spawn a step loop on a tokio task. Fixes a pre-existing bug in
  bin/node's net subcommand where the prior `network.start(()).await?`
  blocked forever, making subsequent interval-poll code unreachable.
- Network/sequencer integration tests: TestNetworkBuilder::build is now
  async; TestNetwork holds the four inbound senders individually.
- SequencerActor::new tests pass `block_time: 2` to avoid
  tokio::time::interval(0) panicking.

Phase 4 of the pure-derivation refactor (stacked on top of Phase 3 in
seb/feat/kona-pure-deriver). Replaces the kona-node `OnlinePipeline` +

  wrapping the pure `Deriver`. Owns `AlloyChainProvider`,
  `AlloyL2ChainProvider`, and `OnlineBlobProvider`; pulls L1 inputs on
  demand based on the L1 watcher's head height; fulfills

  is needed.

  modules. `decode_blob` lifted from `kona_derive::sources::blob_data`
  (Phase 5's blob/calldata helper, landed early because kona-node also
  needs it). `fetch_l1_block_data` is the per-L1-block IO glue that
  produces the `Vec<L1TxView>` shape `kona_derive::extract_l1_input`
  expects.

  method so `bin/node/src/flags/p2p.rs` can drop its
  `kona_derive::ChainProvider` trait import.
- New tests in `deriver.rs`: trace-translation gate test asserting
  structured `tracing` events fire for representative `TraceEntry`
  variants (info / warn / error / debug levels covered); a synthetic

fix(op-supernode): retry RewindEngine on DeadlineExceeded (#21023)

* fix(op-supernode): retry RewindEngine on DeadlineExceeded

The synthetic FCU in the rewind path can take minutes against a slow
execution layer (op-reth in particular). When the engine's per-call RPC
deadline fires, engine.Rewind returns context.DeadlineExceeded even
though the caller's interop-transition ctx still has budget.

Previously the retry loop in RewindEngine bailed immediately on
DeadlineExceeded. Treat it as a transient error instead and rely on the
existing ctx.Done() select to stop the loop when the caller's ctx is
actually done.

* fixup: clarify ctx framing — service ctx has no deadline

feat(op-supernode): WAL canonical payloads for rewind / invalidate operations (#21015)

* feat(op-supernode): re-insert canonical payload during engine rewind

When rewinding the engine for DecisionRewind/DecisionInvalidate, the existing
flow inserted a synthetic block and FCU'd to it, then FCU'd back to the
original target block. The target block was no longer canonical between those
two FCUs, which lets op-reth's pruner discard it and breaks the second FCU.

Re-insert the canonical target payload via engine_newPayload immediately
before the second FCU so the EL is guaranteed to still have the block.

Also short-circuit RewindToTimestamp when the chain is not actually ahead of
the target, and treat ethereum.NotFound from L2BlockRefByNumber in
InvalidateBlock as "already rewound — nothing to do".

* fixup: treat ethereum.NotFound from blockAtTimestamp as no-op rewind

If the EL has not yet produced a block at the requested rewind target,
L2BlockRefByNumber returns ethereum.NotFound — there is nothing to rewind.
errors.Is(err, ethereum.NotFound) survives the RPC jump via
eth.MaybeAsNotFoundErr, which the L2 client wraps every block-fetch
response with.

Simplifies the redundant `unsafe.Number < target.Number` branch since
that case is now handled at step 0.

* feat(op-supernode): WAL canonical payloads for rewind / invalidate operations

The previous design left a window where the engine could not safely complete
a rewind across a crash: after the synthetic FCU made the target block
non-canonical, the EL (op-reth in particular) was free to prune it. On
recovery, fetching the canonical block at the rewind height by number would
return the synthetic block instead of the original target, and fetching by
hash could return NotFound.

This change makes the supernode WAL the authoritative source for the rewind
target:

- RewindPlan gains TargetPayloads (canonical envelope per chain at the rewind
  target). PendingTransition gains InvalidationParentPayloads (parent
  envelope per invalidated chain).
- Build paths fetch each chain's canonical payload by hash at decision time —
  while the block is still canonical — and persist it in the WAL. Any fetch
  failure aborts the build; the decision is re-evaluated next round.
- Apply paths use the WAL'd payloads exclusively. The engine controller no
  longer consults the live EL to discover the target.
- engine.Rewind(ctx, target) replaces RewindToTimestamp. The synthetic block
  is derived from the supplied target, and the same target is re-inserted via
  engine_newPayload between the synthetic and target FCUs to guarantee EL
  durability across pruning.

InvalidateBlock and RewindEngine now take the target envelope explicitly so
the WAL contract reaches all the way down to the engine controller. Tests
have been updated to register canonical payloads through a harness helper
that mirrors verifiedDB commits onto the chain mocks.

* fixup: tighten review feedback on rewind/invalidate

- Rewind no-ops when unsafe is at or behind target (chain state may have moved

- InvalidateBlock no longer treats NotFound as a no-op: a prior crashed attempt
  may have left a synthetic block at this height with no canonical entry visible
  by number, so we still drive the rewind. Only skip when the canonical block at
  the height exists and is not the invalidated hash. Drop the cross-check
  against parentPayload.ExecutionPayload.BlockHash — the WAL target is the
  authoritative destination.
- Remove redundant nil-payload checks after PayloadByHash (the L2 client
  promotes nil-result to ethereum.NotFound) and trim verbose comments.

* fix(op-supernode): wal reset rewind payloads

* fix(op-supernode): satisfy bigint lint

* fixup: drop redundant rewind payload validation

EthClient's payloadCall already verifies the returned envelope matches
the requested ID and is non-nil on success.

* refactor(kona/service): make RpcActor generic over server launcher

Introduces RpcServerLauncher + RpcServerHandle traits so the actor's
relaunch and shutdown logic can be unit-tested with a controllable mock
instead of a real jsonrpsee server. The production path is unchanged: a
new JsonrpseeServerLauncher wraps RpcBuilder and produces a real
ServerHandle. Adds six unit tests covering the restart budget, failed
relaunches, and the Drop-stops-handle path. Also documents that RollupNode
shutdown is unordered, and that L1WatcherActor's builder intentionally
returns impl NodeActor because its block-stream type is unnameable.

The accessor's name shadowed the field of the same name, making
self.engine_config() and &self.engine_config visually ambiguous at
the only call site. Since the accessor only cloned the field, callers
can clone inline.

Constructing the actor with an unstarted handler causes step() to hang
or fail on the first gossip poll. The constructor stays sync to keep

document that explicitly.

The doc comment referenced crate::service::node::RollupNode, but service
is a pub(crate) module so the path is not part of the documented graph.
RollupNode is re-exported from the crate root; link there instead.

* refactor(kona/service): inject delegate-derivation deps via traits

DelegateDerivationActor used to take its two external dependencies —
the sync-status fetch client and the L1 chain provider — by concrete
type, so the actor's validation logic (sync-status fetch, L1
consistency check, conditional forwarding) could not be exercised
without standing up real HTTP and RPC clients. That is why the actor
has no unit tests today.

Introduces a one-method DerivationDelegateProvider trait, generalizes
the L1 provider to any kona_derive::ChainProvider, and threads the two
generics through the actor and its enum wrapper in RollupNode. The
production path is unchanged: DerivationDelegateClient implements the
new trait and AlloyChainProvider already implements ChainProvider.

to the full Engine API surface — including mutation methods like
forkchoiceUpdated, newPayload, and getPayload that an RPC query actor
must never call. Constrain the actor to a new EngineRpcClient trait
exposing only the two methods EngineQueries::handle actually needs:
l2_block_by_label and get_storage_hash (a narrowed projection of
get_proof that returns just the storage hash field used to compute the
L2-to-L1 message-passer storage root pre-Isthmus).

A blanket impl of EngineRpcClient for every T: EngineClient keeps
production wiring (OpEngineClient) unchanged; only the actor's static
type bound has tightened. Tests can now implement the two-method trait
directly instead of the entire EngineClient/OpEngineApi surface.

Also rename the field engine_client -> engine_rpc_client to match the
new narrowed responsibility.

All receiver fields now share the _rx suffix:
- signer        -> unsafe_block_signer_rx
- p2p_rpc       -> p2p_rpc_rx
- admin_rpc     -> admin_query_rx

Call sites are positional so no caller updates required.

the specific NetworkBuilder method chain. The trade-off rationale —
sync constructor over an init() trait method — is retained.

test_launch_no_modules, test_launch_with_modules, and
test_real_launcher_smoke all bound real localhost sockets via

RpcActor tests still cover the restart/stop logic, and the production

fix(op-node): stall consolidate on NotFound during EL sync (#21004)

* fix(op-node): stall consolidate on NotFound during EL sync

When op-node receives a future unsafe payload via gossip during EL sync,
the EL accepts it as a sync target and returns SYNCING. Derivation then
tries to consolidate the next safe block against the unsafe chain, but
the EL doesn't have pending_safe+1 yet, so PayloadByNumber returns
NotFound.

Previously this triggered a derivation pipeline reset. The reset's
forkchoiceUpdated re-targets the EL away from its in-flight sync target,
and the next gossiped payload moves it back — producing a thrash loop
where EL sync never finishes and local safe never advances.

When the engine reports IsEngineInitialELSyncing, treat NotFound at
pending_safe+1 as a transient condition and emit
EngineTemporaryErrorEvent instead of ResetEvent. The attributes stay
queued and consolidation retries on the next pending-safe poke, by
which point EL sync should have filled in the block. Outside EL sync,
NotFound still triggers the existing reset.

ci(kona/registry): assert snapshots match superchain-registry submodule (#20838)

* ci(kona/registry): assert snapshots match superchain-registry submodule

Adds `kona-registry-snapshot-check` to the Rust CI workflows. The job
initializes the `superchain-registry` submodule, runs
`KONA_BIND=true cargo build -p kona-registry`, and asserts
`git diff --exit-code rust/kona/crates/protocol/registry/etc/`. Fails with
a helpful "run X and commit the changes" message on drift.

Wired into both the full `rust-ci` workflow and the lightweight
`rust-ci-gate-short` (the path taken when no rust file changes are
detected — important because a `superchain-registry` submodule bump is
not a rust file change and would otherwise fall into the skip path).
Listed in both `required-rust-ci` requires-lists so it's a merge gate.

Catches the class of bug that left `etc/configs.json` silently drifted
from the submodule for as long as rehearsal-0-bn has been in the
registry: a submodule bump without a snapshot refresh, a hand-edit, or
a refresh of only some of the three coupled files.

consolidate superchain-registry on a single committed zip

Single Rust producer + readers, one committed binary, no Go script.
Replaces the three independent registry-sync pipelines (op-core bash
script, kona-registry KONA_BIND walker, op-reth fetch_superchain_config
bash script) with one zip generated from the
`packages/contracts-bedrock/lib/superchain-registry` submodule.

## Producer

New crate `rust/op-superchain/`:
- `data/superchain-configs.zip` (committed, ~3.8 MB binary): chains.json,
  chainList.json, depsets.json, superchains.json, dictionary, per-chain
  TOML configs, per-chain zstd-with-dictionary genesis, COMMIT entry.
- `bin/regenerate.rs`: walks the submodule, builds the zip
  deterministically (1980-01-01 mtimes, sorted entries, deflate level 9),
  writes the same bytes to both `rust/op-superchain/data/` and
  `op-core/superchain/`.
- `lib.rs`: reader helpers (`read_chain_list_json`, `read_superchains_json`,
  `read_depsets_json`, `read_chain_config_toml`, `read_chain_genesis_*`,
  `supported_chains`) used by downstream build.rss to populate OUT_DIR.

## Consumers

- **op-core/superchain (Go)**: `chain.go` unchanged — same archive/zip
  reader. `init.go` simplified to one COMMIT-vs-op-geth check (drops the
  .sha256 and .txt embeds and their pin files). The Go sync script is
  gone; sync now happens via `just sync-superchain` which runs the Rust
  binary.
- **op-chain-ops/cmd/check-prestate**: `fetchSuperchainRegistryCommit`
  switched from reading `op-core/superchain/superchain-registry-commit.txt`
  at a tag to `git ls-tree <ref> packages/contracts-bedrock/lib/superchain-registry`.
- **kona-registry**: build.rs extracts the three aggregate JSON files
  from op-superchain to $OUT_DIR; lib.rs/superchain.rs include_str! from
  $OUT_DIR. KONA_BIND gate gone; KONA_CUSTOM_CONFIGS overlay path
  preserved (same merge logic, paths repointed to OUT_DIR). Drops
  `etc/{chainList,configs,depsets}.json`.
- **reth-optimism-chainspec**: new build.rs extracts per-chain TOML→JSON
  configs + raw zstd genesis bytes to $OUT_DIR; generates `chain_specs.rs`
  + `lookups.rs` with the `Superchain` enum and match-based lookups.
  Runtime decompresses genesis via the `zstd` crate with the embedded
  dictionary (replaces miniz_oxide + tar-no-std). Drops
  `res/{superchain-configs.tar, fetch_superchain_config.sh,
  superchain_registry_commit}` and the committed
  `src/superchain/chain_specs.rs`.

## CI

- `prep-superchain` is now a thin sanity check (the zip is committed, so
  it's already on every job's checkout). Drops the .sha256 diff step.
- `kona-registry-snapshot-check` repointed at the two committed zips:
  init the submodule, `cargo run -p op-superchain --bin regenerate`, then
  `git diff --exit-code` to assert the producer is deterministic and
  caught up with the submodule pointer.
- Cannon Docker (`cannon-repro.dockerfile`) gets a `COPY rust/op-superchain/`
  so the workspace resolves inside the build container.

## Net effect

- Repo diff per submodule bump: one binary file (~3.8 MB), not 8K LOC.
- No publish-time stale-artifact risk: cargo publish ships what's in git.
- No Docker submodule init needed: the zip is in the COPY'd directories.
- Fresh `git clone` builds without `just source`.
- `+1081 / -7279` overall (5239-line `etc/configs.json` + tar + Go script
  + fetch script all removed).

fix(op-node,op-supernode): redesign SuperAuthority safe/finalized head contract as tri-state

Replace `(eth.BlockID, useLocalSafe bool)` from `rollup.SuperAuthority`
with a typed tri-state result:

    type VerifierHeadSource = PreActivation | Anchor | Verified
    type VerifierHeadStatus = Ok | HoldPrevious
    type VerifierHead struct { Block eth.BlockID; Source VerifierHeadSource }

The old boolean conflated three orthogonal states — verifier healthy with
a verified tip, verifier healthy but no entries for this chain yet, and
verifier read failure — and caused three live bugs that the new contract
structurally eliminates:

- Bug A: verifier read errors returned (BlockID{}, true) which advanced
  cross-safe to localSafeHead despite no verification. Now: HoldPrevious
  floors at FinalizedHead — never local-safe.
- Bug B: post-activation empty verifier returned (BlockID{}, false) which
  resolved to L2 genesis via L2BlockRefByNumber(0), publishing genesis as
  cross-safe and writing a synthetic L1=0/L2=genesis safeDB entry on
  restart (ethereum-optimism/optimism#20944). Now: each active verifier
  contributes its activation anchor — the L2 block at
  `verifier.ActivationTimestamp() - 1` — and the engine controller bounds
  by local-safe.
- Bug D: EL-unknown / non-canonical verifier results could fall below
  FinalizedHead. Now: degrade to FinalizedHead as reorg signal, never
  below.

Additional changes:
- `activity.VerificationActivity` exposes `ActivationTimestamp() uint64`;
  the existing accessor moves from `interop_test_access.go` to
  `interop.go` since it is now part of the production interface.
- Mixed-active-verifier safety: not-yet-active verifiers are skipped
  (their anchor block doesn't exist on this chain yet); they no longer
  surface as HoldPrevious.
- Existing `superAuthorityFinalizedHead` cache is retained — finalized
  cannot reorg, so caching is safe, and the cache holds across
  HoldPrevious and EL-hash-lookup transients.
- Cross-safe is not cached (it can reorg). Reorg signals (EL-unknown,
  non-canonical) floor at finalized.

Repro tests in op-node/rollup/engine/super_authority_safe_head_test.go
cover bugs A and B and the cold-start HoldPrevious safety property.

fix(op-node): cache cross-safe head with canonicality re-validation

Per design follow-up: cross-safe CAN reorg, so we can't blindly trust a
cached value the way we do for finalized. But we can still cache it and
re-validate against the EL on each use — preserving cross-safe progress
across transient verifier outages without compromising safety.

`useSuperAuthoritySafeCache` calls `L2BlockRefByNumber(cached.Number)` and
compares hashes; on mismatch (reorg) or RPC failure, the cache is cleared
and the caller floors at FinalizedHead as before. The cache is also bounded
by the current local-safe head to defend against derivation resets.

`floorCrossSafe` unifies the four fallback paths in SafeL2Head
(HoldPrevious, zero-block, EL-unknown, non-canonical) so they all consult
the cache first and fall through to FinalizedHead only when the cache is
unusable.

refactor(op-node,op-supernode): move anchor block resolution to engine controller

Previously simpleChainContainer resolved Anchor contributions to concrete L2
blocks by calling engine.L2BlockRefByNumber, which required the activation
timestamp via VerificationActivity.ActivationTimestamp() and a rollup config
field for the timestamp→number conversion.

This change leaves the chain_container in the lane of gathering verifier
results and picking the oldest, and pushes block resolution into the engine
controller which already owns the EL handle and the canonicality logic for
the Verified branch:

- VerifierHead gains a Timestamp field. For Anchor source the Block is zero
  and Timestamp carries the pre-activation cap; the engine controller
  resolves the canonical L2 block at that timestamp via TargetBlockNumber +
  L2BlockRefByNumber. The block is canonical by construction so no second
  check is needed.
- VerificationActivity.ActivationTimestamp() is dropped from the interface.
  *Interop keeps the method for op-devstack consumers but the head-reporting
  contract is now timestamp-driven via the existing return slot on
  LatestVerifiedL2Block / VerifiedBlockAtL1: an empty BlockID paired with
  a non-zero timestamp is a cap.
- simpleChainContainer no longer touches engine/rollup config for head
  reporting. verifierContribution collapses to a one-liner that classifies
  the verifier's return; pickOldest factors the cross-verifier comparison
  out of both head methods.
- The zero-block defensive branches in resolveVerifiedAs{Safe,Finalized}
  were unreachable under the new contract (Verified is only emitted with a
  non-zero block) and are removed. The zero-timestamp guards in the Anchor
  paths are also unnecessary — TargetBlockNumber rejects timestamps below
  genesis, which feeds the existing error fallback.

fix(op-node,op-supernode): redesign SuperAuthority safe/finalized head as tri-state

Replaces SuperAuthority.FullyVerifiedL2Head / FinalizedL2Head returning
(eth.BlockID, useLocalSafe bool) with (VerifierHead, ok bool), where
VerifierHead.Source is the tri-state PreActivation | Anchor | Verified and
ok=false signals a transient verifier read failure. VerifierHead carries a
Block (Verified) or a Timestamp (Anchor) — the engine controller resolves
Anchor timestamps to canonical L2 blocks itself. The old boolean conflated
three orthogonal states and caused three live bugs that the new contract
structurally eliminates:

- Bug A — verifier read error returned (BlockID{}, true) which advanced
  cross-safe to localSafeHead despite no verification. Now: ok=false consults
  the canonicality-checked cross-safe cache; on miss, floors at FinalizedHead
  — never local-safe.
- Bug B — post-activation empty verifier returned (BlockID{}, false) which
  resolved to L2 genesis via L2BlockRefByNumber(0), publishing genesis as
  cross-safe and writing a synthetic L1=0 / L2=genesis safeDB entry on restart
  (#20944). Now: an active verifier contributes its activation anchor as a
  cap timestamp (activationTimestamp - 1); the engine controller resolves the
  canonical L2 block at that timestamp and bounds by local-safe.
- Bug D — EL-unknown / non-canonical verifier results could fall below
  FinalizedHead. Now: degrade to the canonicality-checked cache, then to
  FinalizedHead as reorg signal — never below.

FinalizedHead is bounded by localFinalizedHead (not localSafeHead): the super
authority can delay finalization but cannot finalize a block the node hasn't
itself finalized locally.

EngineController.SafeL2Head / FinalizedHead own all block resolution and
canonicality validation (the Verified path looks up by hash and re-validates;
the Anchor path looks up by number, canonical by construction).

Caches:
- superAuthorityFinalizedHead: retained as-is. Finalized cannot reorg, so the
  cache is trusted without re-validation.
- superAuthoritySafeHead (new): cross-safe CAN reorg, so the cache is
  re-validated against the EL via L2BlockRefByNumber on every use. A
  non-canonical cache is cleared and the caller floors at FinalizedHead. The
  cross-safe fallback paths (HoldPrevious, EL-unknown, non-canonical,
  anchor-lookup-failed) unify through floorCrossSafe. The lookup-and-compare
  logic is extracted into isCanonical.

Interface housekeeping:
- SuperAuthority methods take an explicit ctx context.Context instead of
  using context.Background(). Threaded from EngineController.ctx.
- VerificationActivity is unchanged in shape: the cap timestamp rides on the
  existing return slot of LatestVerifiedL2Block / VerifiedBlockAtL1 (an empty
  BlockID paired with a non-zero ts is a cap; non-empty BlockID is a verified
  tip). *Interop keeps ActivationTimestamp() as a public accessor for
  op-devstack, but it is not part of the interface contract.

Port of #21049 onto the single-verifier base (#21077). Mixed-active-verifier
plumbing and pickOldest aggregation collapse to direct single-verifier calls.

Tests:
- op-node/rollup/engine/super_authority_safe_head_test.go adds red/green
  repro tests for bugs A, B, D plus cache happy-path and cache reorg
  invalidation. Documented in #21049 as failing on the pre-fix boolean
  contract baseline (develop 8bb872e4).
- TestEngineController_SafeL2Head / TestEngineController_FinalizedHead table
  cases updated to the new contract.
- Supernode super_authority_test.go rewritten for the new contract under the
  single-verifier base.
- interop_test.go updated: empty results return the pre-activation cap.
- op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/upgrade/finalized_activation_test.go
  brought over (TestFinalizedL2DoesNotRegressAcrossActivation). DSL helper
  ReachedTimeWithoutRegressionFn added to op-devstack/dsl/l2_cl.go.

feat(op-service/clock): make AdvancingClock continuous (#20995)

* feat(op-service/clock): make AdvancingClock continuous

The previous AdvancingClock embedded a DeterministicClock and pumped it
via a fixed 100ms wall-clock ticker. Now() therefore only changed on
tick boundaries, and pending timers fired at tick granularity. Callers
that observed Now() between ticks saw stale values; tests that jumped
time and expected timers to fire immediately had to wait for the next
tick.

Rewrite the clock with no fixed tick:

- Now() reads the wall clock on every call and adds an atomic offset
  accumulated by AdvanceTime. There is no quantisation: continuous
  wall progression and instant manual jumps.
- Pending actions live in a single sorted list owned by a scheduler
  goroutine that sleeps exactly until the next due item (via the
  injected wall Clock) and re-evaluates on wakeup/quit signals.
- AdvanceTime, addAction, Stop, Reset all signal the scheduler via a
  buffered wakeup channel so manual jumps fire overdue actions
  immediately rather than waiting for an arbitrary tick.

NewAdvancingClock retains the advanceEvery argument for source-level
compatibility; the value is now ignored. Existing callers continue
to compile unchanged.

* refactor(op-service/clock): use a single mutex for AdvancingClock

Consolidate the scheduler lock and per-action lock into AdvancingClock.mu.
Drops the embedded mutex on pendingAction; all mutable fields are now
guarded by the clock mutex.

Also fixes the race where reset() updated a.due under the per-action lock
while insertLocked read other actions' due fields under the clock lock.
With a single mutex covering both insert/remove and action mutation, that
race is gone by construction.

warning and zero the offset instead of erroring, so the new default is

When the L2 ProxyAdmin on a target chain is not owned by the aliased L1
rootSafe, the `upgradeAndCall` deposits this template generates land on
L2 but silently revert with `onlyOwner`. The L1 task tx still reports
success, so the failure is only visible by reading post-execution L2

(one URL or foundry.toml rpc alias per chain), the template forks each
L2, verifies chainId, and asserts the L2 ProxyAdmin is owned by
`AddressAliasHelper.applyL1ToL2Alias(rootSafe)`. Mismatches revert
during simulation with a message pointing at TransferL2PAOFromL1 as
the fix.

check, so existing configs (including the 034 arena-z regression

* FeeVaultUpgradeTemplate: add optional L2 ProxyAdmin owner pre-flight check

When the L2 ProxyAdmin on a target chain is not owned by the aliased L1
rootSafe, the `upgradeAndCall` deposits this template generates land on
L2 but silently revert with `onlyOwner`. The L1 task tx still reports
success, so the failure is only visible by reading post-execution L2
state — an extremely confusing failure mode for operators.

Adds an opt-in check: when `l2RpcUrls = [...]` is set in config.toml
(one URL or foundry.toml rpc alias per chain), the template forks each
L2, verifies chainId, and asserts the L2 ProxyAdmin is owned by
`AddressAliasHelper.applyL1ToL2Alias(rootSafe)`. Mismatches revert
during simulation with a message pointing at TransferL2PAOFromL1 as
the fix.

When `l2RpcUrls` is absent the template prints a warning and skips the
check, so existing configs (including the 034 arena-z regression
fixture) keep working unchanged.

feat(supernode): gate chain RPC through VN lifecycle

Gate per-chain supernode RPC dispatch on chain and VN lifecycle readiness.
During interop reorg recovery, callers could hit a newly swapped handler
before op-node registered APIs, or a handler whose shutdown had begun.

Chain containers now register a stable readiness predicate with the router.
The router waits for that predicate before dispatching, preserves it across
handler swaps, and removes the route on permanent shutdown.

Readiness comes from pause/stop state and the VN state machine.
The VN state is atomic because HTTP handlers read it without taking v.mu,
while Start and Stop update it on the lifecycle path.

Stop stores Stopped before canceling the run context, so teardown closes
the gate immediately instead of waiting for inner node shutdown to drain.

Coverage includes router wait, deadline, removal, and handler-swap cases;
chain-container readiness wiring; VN lifecycle transitions; and the interop
reorg recovery acceptance path.

op-node: resolve SuperAuthority safe + finalized together

Introduce a single resolver (rollup/engine/superauthority_forkchoice.go) that
resolves the published cross-safe AND cross-finalized heads TOGETHER, instead of
the two independent code paths that previously each reinterpreted the
SuperAuthority state. Because the EL invariant finalized <= safe couples the two
heads, the split paths produced a class of bugs (finalized pinned at genesis,
finalized ahead of safe).

Design:
  - GATHER: turn each VerifierHead+ok (PreActivation/Anchor/Verified, ok=false =
    HoldPrevious) into a concrete candidate block using the EL for canonicality /
    anchor-ts->block resolution, bounded by the corresponding local head. Any
    lookup/canonicality failure or HoldPrevious => hold previous (use cache),
    never fall back to local-safe or floor finalized.
  - resolveCrossHeads: a PURE function that takes the two candidates + cached
    cross heads and returns {safe, finalized} together, enforcing every invariant
    in one place (hold-previous on zero candidate, never rewind below cache,
    anchor/pre-activation are weak, finalized clamped down to safe). Returns an
    error on genuinely inconsistent state instead of panicking; the caller holds
    the previous cached heads. Exhaustively table-tested, with each of the 4 bug
    scenarios as a row.

EngineController.SafeL2Head/FinalizedHead now gather both authority signals,
call the resolver, persist the cache, and return safe/finalized. The scattered
resolveVerifiedAs*/resolveAnchorAs*/apply*CacheChecks/crossSafeFallback helpers
are removed. promoteFinalized under a SuperAuthority advances localFinalizedHead
unconditionally from the L1-derived finalizer and publishes only the resolver's
output. Standalone (no SuperAuthority) and FollowSource paths are unchanged.

Renamed the critical cross-state fields deprecatedSafeHead -> crossSafeHead and
deprecatedFinalizedHead -> crossFinalizedHead (and SetDeprecatedSafeHead ->
SetCrossSafeHead) throughout; supervisor-only usages keep working.

Supernode: the cold-start fix stays in the supernode layer (interop.go returns
ErrNotStarted/unavailable when the verified DB is empty during backfill, never an
anchor); the finalized<=safe clamp is NOT added to super_authority.go — the
resolver now owns that invariant.

Dual-model review of 013ff0cf7e found correctness gaps in the coupled
SuperAuthority safe+finalized resolver. Fix all of them:

1. Decouple resolver cache from deprecated/FollowSource fields. Revert the
   crossSafeHead/crossFinalizedHead rename back to deprecatedSafeHead/
   deprecatedFinalizedHead (FollowSource + supervisor only) and add a
   dedicated superAuthoritySafeHead cache mirroring superAuthorityFinalizedHead.
   The SuperAuthority resolution path now touches only superAuthority* fields.

2. Resolve the pair ONCE per FCU and reuse. New
   refreshSuperAuthorityPublished() resolves the coupled pair a single time at
   the top of each FCU cycle (tryUpdateEngineInternal, insertUnsafePayload,
   promoteLocalFinalizedWithSuperAuthority) and stores it in
   superAuthorityPublished{Safe,Finalized}Head. SafeL2Head/FinalizedHead now
   return that published snapshot with no side-effecting resolve, eliminating
   the dual-snapshot hazard and the per-call EL RPC amplification.

3. FCU-level monotonicity + finalized<=safe. reconcilePublished enforces that
   published finalized never rewinds below the last published finalized and
   <= published safe. If the clamp would force finalized below the last
   published finalized (safe legitimately lowered below it), hold the last
   published pair and emit an error + conflict metric instead of a rewind.

4. Error/hold fallback never publishes finalized>safe. The resolver error path
   now returns the last PUBLISHED consistent pair re-clamped via
   crossHeads.clampFinalizedToSafe(), never the raw per-head caches.

5. crossUseLocal cache gap. resolveOne now records the published local head in
   the cache on use-local so a following hold-previous cannot rewind to a
   stale/zero value.

   counter) on the resolver-conflict / finalized-rewind-hold paths.

7. Tests for the wiring. New superauthority_publish_test.go covers, through the

   safe lowers, a single-snapshot consistent FCU pair, the error fallback
   never publishing finalized>safe, use-local -> hold-previous not rewinding

feat(kona/node): migrate to NodeDeriver wrapping pure::Deriver (phase 4/6)

Phase 4 of the pure-derivation refactor (stacked on top of Phase 3 in
seb/feat/kona-pure-deriver). Replaces the kona-node `OnlinePipeline` +
`DerivationActor::step` loop with `NodeDeriver`, an async driver around
`kona_derive::Deriver` that owns the L1 / L2 IO substrate and translates
`DeriveTrace` entries into structured `tracing` events.

What landed:

- New `NodeDeriver` (`crates/node/service/src/actors/derivation/deriver.rs`)
  wrapping the pure `Deriver`. Owns `AlloyChainProvider`,
  `AlloyL2ChainProvider`, and `OnlineBlobProvider`; pulls L1 inputs on
  demand based on the L1 watcher's head height; fulfills
  `NeedSpanBatchOverlap` by fetching the L2 range and re-encoding txs
  to raw RLP; translates every `TraceEntry` variant to a structured
  `tracing::*` event.
- `DerivationActor` now takes a concrete `NodeDeriver` and no longer is
  generic over `Pipeline + SignalReceiver`. The `Signal::Activation`
  site collapses to a no-op (Holocene+ strict ordering subsumes it,
  per Phase 3's reset semantics).
- `DerivationStateMachine` collapsed: the `AwaitingSignal`,
  `AwaitingUpdateAfterSignal`, `SignalNeeded`, and `SignalProcessed`
  arms are gone; reset / flush flow through direct method calls on
  `NodeDeriver` so no separate "waiting for signal processing" state
  is needed.
- `OnlinePipeline` deleted (no in-tree caller remains).
- New `kona_providers_alloy::blob_decode` and `kona_providers_alloy::l1_data`
  modules. `decode_blob` lifted from `kona_derive::sources::blob_data`
  (Phase 5's blob/calldata helper, landed early because kona-node also
  needs it). `fetch_l1_block_data` is the per-L1-block IO glue that
  produces the `Vec<L1TxView>` shape `kona_derive::extract_l1_input`
  expects.
- `AlloyChainProvider::block_info_by_number` exposed as an inherent
  method so `bin/node/src/flags/p2p.rs` can drop its
  `kona_derive::ChainProvider` trait import.
- New tests in `deriver.rs`: trace-translation gate test asserting
  structured `tracing` events fire for representative `TraceEntry`
  variants (info / warn / error / debug levels covered); a synthetic
  no-overlap-without-span-batch test exercising the request/response

feat(kona/derive): pure sync deriver with full span-batch overlap check

Phase 3 of the pure-derivation migration. Builds a pure (sync, IO-free,
no_std) `Deriver` on top of phase 2's `core/*` primitives, and closes
the post-Holocene span-batch overlap content-check spec gap that both
op-node and kona's async pipeline skip today.

Public API in `kona_derive::pure`:
- `Deriver::new(rollup_cfg, l1_cfg, sys_config, safe_head, dep_set)`
- `Deriver::derive(safe_head) -> (Derivation, DeriveTrace)` — never errors
- `Deriver::add_l1_input(L1Input) -> Result<(), CriticalError>`
- `Deriver::add_span_batch_overlap(SpanBatchOverlap) -> Result<(), CriticalError>`
- `Deriver::reset(safe_head, sys_config) -> DeriveTrace`
- `extract_l1_input(header, txs, receipts, rollup_cfg) -> L1Input` — filter-only,
  sysconfig-blind

Contract invariants encoded in types:
- `derive` never returns `Err`; malformed inputs surface as
  `TraceEntry::*Dropped` / `*Failed` entries.
- `add_*` only error on contract violations (non-contiguous L1, overlap
  range mismatch, unsolicited overlap, etc.).
- No `tracing::*` calls inside `pure/` — callers translate trace events.
- `extract_l1_input` does no fallible parsing; `L1Input` carries raw
  `Vec<Log>` and raw `(Address, Bytes)` calldata.
- `SpanBatchOverlapBlock.txs: Vec<Bytes>` — raw RLP throughout, no
  encode/decode round-trip in the overlap content check.
- `pure/` is `no_std`; verified by the workspace's
  `riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf` target.
- Every `match` on `Derivation` and `TraceEntry` inside `pure/` is
  exhaustive; strict typed reason enums everywhere, no `String` fields.

requires L1 RPC + beacon + L2 snapshot access not available in this

feat(op-node): cache cross-safe head with canonicality re-validation (#21079)

* feat(op-node): cache cross-safe head with canonicality re-validation

Wraps the cached cross-safe head and its validation in a self-contained
crossSafeCache (Store / Get against an ExecEngine + local-safe bound).
crossSafeFallback consults the cache before flooring at FinalizedHead so
a transient verifier outage doesn't drop cross-safe to finalized.

Cross-safe can reorg, so Get re-validates the cached block against the EL
via L2BlockRefByNumber on every read; non-canonical or unavailable entries
are cleared. Bounded by current local-safe to defend against derivation
resets.

* fix(op-node): floor crossSafeFallback at finalized; seed cache on reset

crossSafeFallback now returns finalized whenever the cached cross-safe is
below it, preserving the engine invariant that safe >= finalized. forceReset
seeds the cross-safe cache with the reset value so a subsequent HoldPrevious
returns the reset crossSafe rather than dropping to finalized.

op-supernode: add interop cold start progress logging (#20961)

* op-supernode: add interop cold start progress logging

The interop cold start loop retries every second while waiting for
SafeDB entries on all chains, but the only log was at debug level.
At the default info level, operators see zero output — making it look
like interop never started.

Add an info-level progress log every ~30 seconds that shows:
- Attempt count and activation timestamp
- Per-chain SafeDB readiness
- Per-chain sync status (unsafe, pending_safe, safe block numbers)

Example output:
  interop cold start: waiting for SafeDB entries on all chains
    attempts=30 activationTimestamp=1777409304
    chain_420120084="safedb_ready=true unsafe=989919 pending_safe=989606 safe=0"
    chain_420120085="safedb_ready=false unsafe=1979806 pending_safe=1979403 safe=0"

This makes it immediately clear which chain is the blocker and whether
derivation is making progress.

* op-supernode: add interop verification loop progress log

After cold start completes, the verification loop runs silently — no
info-level logs for normal operation. Operators can't tell if
verification is progressing or stuck without checking metrics.

Add a periodic info-level log every ~30 rounds showing the last
verified timestamp, so operators can see verification catching up to
the chain tip and know when safe head will start advancing.

* op-supernode: set interop verification lag metric

* Revert "op-supernode: set interop verification lag metric"

This reverts commit 16bbc73d3bb1e2de8051add96100d139a7d6198c.

* op-supernode: improve interop cold start and verification observability

- Log per-chain progress on the error path too, not just the
  no-advance path. When advanceColdStartInit returns an error (e.g.
  engine client not initialized), operators previously only saw the
  raw error with no chain-level breakdown.

- Add current_l1 and finalized_l1 to the cold start progress log so
  operators can immediately tell whether a deriver is catching up or
  is at the L1 tip waiting for new batches to finalize.

- Add per-chain safe/pending_safe/unsafe to the verification progress
  log so operators can see which chain is lagging during catch-up.

* op-supernode: add interop activity state gauge

Add supernode_interop_activity_state gauge that tracks the interop
activity lifecycle:
  0 = not_started
  1 = cold_start_waiting
  2 = running
  3 = halted

Set at each lifecycle transition: cold start entry, resume from
verifiedDB, cold start complete, and permanent halt on
ErrHistoryUnavailable. Lets operators alert on state=3 (halted) or
detect stuck cold starts without parsing logs.

* op-supernode: use already-collected data for cold start progress logging

Address review feedback: instead of re-querying FirstSafeHeadTimestamp
and SyncStatus in a separate logColdStartProgress function (which is
expensive and introduces a race condition), log the per-chain readiness
info already collected by collectFirstSafeHeadTimestamps. Emits at
info level every 30 attempts, debug otherwise.

fix(op-node,op-supernode): redesign SuperAuthority safe/finalized head as tri-state (#21049)

* fix(op-node,op-supernode): redesign SuperAuthority safe/finalized head as tri-state

Replaces SuperAuthority.FullyVerifiedL2Head / FinalizedL2Head returning
(eth.BlockID, useLocalSafe bool) with (VerifierHead, ok bool), where
VerifierHead.Source is the tri-state PreActivation | Anchor | Verified and
ok=false signals a transient verifier read failure. VerifierHead carries a
Block (Verified) or a Timestamp (Anchor) — the engine controller resolves
Anchor timestamps to canonical L2 blocks itself. The old boolean conflated
three orthogonal states and caused three live bugs that the new contract
structurally eliminates:

- Bug A — verifier read error returned (BlockID{}, true) which advanced
  cross-safe to localSafeHead despite no verification. Now: ok=false consults
  the canonicality-checked cross-safe cache; on miss, floors at FinalizedHead
  — never local-safe.
- Bug B — post-activation empty verifier returned (BlockID{}, false) which
  resolved to L2 genesis via L2BlockRefByNumber(0), publishing genesis as
  cross-safe and writing a synthetic L1=0 / L2=genesis safeDB entry on restart
  (#20944). Now: an active verifier contributes its activation anchor as a
  cap timestamp (activationTimestamp - 1); the engine controller resolves the
  canonical L2 block at that timestamp and bounds by local-safe.
- Bug D — EL-unknown / non-canonical verifier results could fall below
  FinalizedHead. Now: degrade to the canonicality-checked cache, then to
  FinalizedHead as reorg signal — never below.

FinalizedHead is bounded by localFinalizedHead (not localSafeHead): the super
authority can delay finalization but cannot finalize a block the node hasn't
itself finalized locally.

EngineController.SafeL2Head / FinalizedHead own all block resolution and
canonicality validation (the Verified path looks up by hash and re-validates;
the Anchor path looks up by number, canonical by construction).

Caches:
- superAuthorityFinalizedHead: retained as-is. Finalized cannot reorg, so the
  cache is trusted without re-validation.

ci: fetch full history for forkdiff instead of fixed --depth

The build-and-deploy "Build forkdiff" step failed with "failed to compute
patch between base and fork: error: object not found".

forkdiff walks every op-geth-specific commit down to the go-ethereum base
pinned in fork.yaml. Those ~980 commits are interleaved with go-ethereum's
history in the commit graph, so the deepest sits well past depth 1000. With
the previous `git fetch --depth 1000` in CircleCI's shallow checkout, those
objects were never fetched and go-git hit the shallow boundary.

Replace the fixed-depth fetch with `git fetch --unshallow || git fetch` so
the job always has the full history it needs, regardless of how the fork
history grows.

fix(OPCMUpgradeV700): support standard chains in U19 upgrade template

Three fixes discovered while simulating U19 upgrades on standard superchain-registry
chains for the first time (all prior V700 use was betanet-only):

1. SuperchainAddressRegistry._fetchAndSaveInitialContracts: register EthLockboxProxy
   per-chain from the registry JSON when present. Standard chain discovery (via
   _processAddresses) didn't include EthLockboxProxy, so it was missing from the
   allowed storage accesses allowlist, causing the state-diff validator to reject
   valid OPCM upgrade state changes.

2. OPCMUpgradeV700._setAllowedStorageAccesses: use try/catch when fetching
   ProtocolVersions per-chain. Standard chains store ProtocolVersions on the sentinel
   chain (via addresses.toml), not per L2 chainId, so getAddress("ProtocolVersions",
   chainId) reverted for any non-betanet chain.

3. OPCMUpgradeV700._getCodeExceptions: only include true EOAs (no code). Some chains
   (e.g. Ink) use a multisig Safe as SystemConfig.owner(). Adding a contract address
   to the EOA exceptions list caused "unexpected code" validation failures when the
   OPCM re-initializes SystemConfig and writes the owner to storage slot 0x33.

4. OPCMUpgradeV700._build: skip upgradeSuperchain() if SuperchainConfig is already
   at the v7.1.17 implementation. Chains with non-standard L1PAOs (e.g. Unichain)
   cannot authorize ProxyAdmin.upgrade() on the shared SuperchainConfig. In the
   stacked execution model a prior shared-L1PAO task runs upgradeSuperchain first,
   so subsequent Unichain tasks can skip it via the idempotency check.

fix(interop): drain cross-safe verification backlog with adaptive backoff

The interop verification loop sleeps a fixed backoffPeriod (1s) after every
no-op round. On a live 2-chain network ~half of all rounds are no-ops (e.g.
timestamp gaps between chains with different block times), so the verifier
spends ~1s sleeping per no-op while advance rounds take ~34ms. This pins
cross-safe throughput to ~1 round/sec (~real-time) even with a large,
fully-local backlog and idle CPU, so after any multi-hour stall the cross-safe
head tracks the tip but never drains the backlog (observed: ~21.6k blocks /
~12h behind, recovering at ~1.0x real-time).

Use a short catch-up backoff while behind: consecutive no-op rounds back off
only briefly (advances reset the streak), so a backlog drains at IO/CPU speed;
once sustained no-ops indicate we are caught up to the tip, fall back to the
full backoff to avoid busy-polling. No verification semantics change.

flag, not the effective FailsafeEnabled() state, so a node in failsafe could
report failsafe_enabled=0.

Wire an onFailsafeChange callback into the ingester (SetError/ClearError) and
cross-validator (setError). The backend registers a callback that records the
recomputed FailsafeEnabled() so the gauge stays correct when multiple chains or
the cross-validator can independently hold failsafe on (e.g. clearing one chain
while another still errors keeps the gauge at 1).

The cross-validator invokes the callback after releasing errMu to avoid
re-acquiring the RWMutex via Error().

fix(op-acceptance-tests): stabilize TestReorgUnsafeHead reorg race

TestReorgUnsafeHead flaked (~8 CI occurrences, mostly op-reth) with
"no reorg happened on chain A". Root cause: after the test-sequencer
commits the conflicting block, the test read the EL's mutable eth.Unsafe
("latest") label to pick the parent for the next block. That read can lag
op-reth's post-forkchoice canonical-tag swap and return the *original*
head; building the next block on that stale parent issues a
forkchoiceUpdated that reorgs the EL back onto the original chain,
silently undoing the reorg. CI logs show the exact signature: a forward
reorg X->Y immediately followed by Y->X.

Replace the racy label read with the ReorgExact DSL poll (the same helper
the sibling reorg tests use): wait until the divergence height reports a
different hash with a matching parent, then read that confirmed
conflicting block back by number and use it as the explicit parent. The
final assertion uses the same helper instead of a one-shot read. Both
polls use a generous attempt budget (30 x 2s) so an oversubscribed CI box,
where op-reth can be slow to surface the reorged block, does not trip a
tight timeout.

Reproduced the flake under load (1/48 at -parallel=24) and verified the
fix (128/128 at -parallel=32, 0 failures of either mode).

Refs #20198

fix(op-node): preserve safedb across EL-sync restarts

op-node wiped the entire safedb whenever EL sync started. For op-reth/erigon
(SupportsPostFinalizationELSync) with --syncmode=execution-layer this happens
on every restart, even when the node is already synced, so the safedb was lost
each time.

Move the safedb handling from EL-sync start to completion: preserve the db when
its tip is on the synced chain; otherwise (a recent reorg dropped the tip, or a
foreign restore) trim to the recorded safe head near the offset head when that
block is canonical, else clear. Safe/finalized resume from the safedb-derived
head, with finalized never advancing past the genuinely-finalized head (it may
move backward and is re-advanced by derivation). With no safedb, fall back to
the offset-derived head as before.

feat(op-reth): seed slot-preimage DB during state-dump import

reth's V2 storage layout (`--storage.v2`, default-on) stores state in
hashed tables and, for pre-Cancun blocks, relies on an auxiliary MDBX DB
at `<datadir>/db/preimage` mapping `keccak256(slot) -> slot` so the
Execution stage can resolve plain storage keys when a SELFDESTRUCT wipes
a contract. That DB is populated only while executing blocks.

The OP Mainnet bedrock bootstrap (`init-state --without-ovm`) imports a
state dump straight into hashed storage and never populates the preimage
DB. A later pre-Ecotone selfdestruct of an imported contract then crashes
the Execution stage with "missing slot preimage for 0x... (addr=0x...)",
aborting backfill sync.

Close the gap on the op-reth side: after `init_from_state_dump`, when
storage is v2, re-read the dump (which carries plain slot keys) and seed
`keccak256(slot) -> slot` into the same env reth's execution stage reads.
Streaming parse with batched, sorted inserts keeps memory bounded; skip-
if-present makes it idempotent and crash-safe. No-op on v1, and reth
deletes the preimage DB once Ecotone activates.

The MDBX env open/insert is replicated from reth's private
`SlotPreimages::open`/`insert_preimages` at rev 81c0261 and must stay
byte-compatible; documented in-code. The durable fix belongs upstream
(a seeding helper in `reth-db-common` so importers can't bypass it).

After disconnecting CLP2P, L2CLC's unsafe head is frozen at the value last
gossiped by the sequencer, while local-safe must catch up via the follow source

perf(sdm): materialize canonical PostExec efficiently across flashblocks

Make the op-rbuilder canonical PostExec (0x7D) flashblock path both
O(1)-per-flashblock and consensus-identical to op-reth's single
whole-block pass.

Materialization without prior-tx replay:
- The per-flashblock canonical replay re-executed every prior tx from the
  parent state on each flashblock, making per-block cost O(N^2) in tx
  count. Replace it with materialize_post_exec, which seeds a throwaway
  State via with_bundle_prestate(real_bundle) and executes only the
  single PostExec system tx on top, then assembles the block from the
  already-accumulated execution info (the same prestate pattern op-reth's
  flashblocks worker uses). PostExec stays isolated in the throwaway
  state, so the main builder cache is never polluted. build_block is

  carried provenance indices feed attribution events only. Adds inspector

fix(op-acceptance-tests): stabilize TestReorgUnsafeHead reorg race (#21112)

TestReorgUnsafeHead flaked (~8 CI occurrences, mostly op-reth) with
"no reorg happened on chain A". Root cause: after the test-sequencer
commits the conflicting block, the test read the EL's mutable eth.Unsafe
("latest") label to pick the parent for the next block. That read can lag
op-reth's post-forkchoice canonical-tag swap and return the *original*
head; building the next block on that stale parent issues a
forkchoiceUpdated that reorgs the EL back onto the original chain,
silently undoing the reorg. CI logs show the exact signature: a forward
reorg X->Y immediately followed by Y->X.

Replace the racy label read with the ReorgExact DSL poll (the same helper
the sibling reorg tests use): wait until the divergence height reports a
different hash with a matching parent, then read that confirmed
conflicting block back by number and use it as the explicit parent. The
final assertion uses the same helper instead of a one-shot read. Both
polls use a generous attempt budget (30 x 2s) so an oversubscribed CI box,
where op-reth can be slow to surface the reorged block, does not trip a
tight timeout.

Reproduced the flake under load (1/48 at -parallel=24) and verified the
fix (128/128 at -parallel=32, 0 failures of either mode).

Refs #20198

feat(supernode): gate per-chain RPC during VN lifecycle transitions (#21103)

* feat(supernode): gate chain RPC through VN lifecycle

Gate per-chain supernode RPC dispatch on chain and VN lifecycle readiness.
During interop reorg recovery, callers could hit a newly swapped handler
before op-node registered APIs, or a handler whose shutdown had begun.

Chain containers now register a stable readiness predicate with the router.
The router waits for that predicate before dispatching, preserves it across
handler swaps, and removes the route on permanent shutdown.

Readiness comes from pause/stop state and the VN state machine.
The VN state is atomic because HTTP handlers read it without taking v.mu,
while Start and Stop update it on the lifecycle path.

Stop stores Stopped before canceling the run context, so teardown closes
the gate immediately instead of waiting for inner node shutdown to drain.

Coverage includes router wait, deadline, removal, and handler-swap cases;
chain-container readiness wiring; VN lifecycle transitions; and the interop
reorg recovery acceptance path.

* fix(supernode): initialize VN atomic state

Explicitly store VNStateNotStarted when constructing a virtual node so the atomic lifecycle state starts from the named state instead of relying on the atomic zero value.

* fix(supernode): remove chain RPC route on stop return

Defer RPC router removal at the start of chain-container Stop so permanent shutdown removes the route on both successful stops and stop timeout returns.

* refactor(op-supernode): address PR review feedback

- rpc_router: drop dead r.routes nil-check (always initialized by NewRouter)
- virtual_node: document the setState-before-cancel ordering invariant in Stop()

fix(op-node): reorg follow-mode sequencer onto upstream chain on divergence

A follow-mode sequencer (light op-node CL that produces unsafe blocks while
following a supernode's safe head) failed to adopt the supernode's deposits-only
invalid-message replacement: the invalid executing message persisted
(ethereum-optimism/optimism#21119).

Root cause: in EngineController.FollowSource, the divergence branch did a soft
followExternalRefs(true). That soft unsafe-head update was designed for pure
light-CL verifiers (#18571), which have no local block production. A follow-mode
sequencer keeps extending its own fork, so the soft update was clobbered by the
next sequencer block before the FCU landed, leaving head on the fork and safe on
the upstream chain. op-reth then rejected the FCU as inconsistent, the reset
re-selected the fork via the deny-list-unaware FindL2Heads, and the follower
oscillated indefinitely.

Fix: when the follower is also a sequencer (origin-selector resetter wired, i.e.
SequencerEnabled), reorg decisively onto the upstream refs with forceReset. This
cancels the in-flight fork build (ResetOrigins), aborts the sequencer, and FCUs
the engine onto the upstream chain in one shot (head==safe), after which the
sequencer rebuilds on the new head. Pure verifiers keep the proven soft path.

Adds unit guards TestFollowSource_SequencerDivergenceForcesReset and
TestFollowSource_VerifierDivergenceStaysSoft, plus cross-node convergence and
forward-progress assertions to the shared invalid-message replacement scenario.
