feat(op-conductor): reorg-recovery wedge hardening (demotion grace + reconnect-reconcile)

Closes the deep-reorg wedge demonstrated by the tight-health stress test
(~2% of reorg-reaching runs). All changes gated by --reorg-recovery.enabled;
with the flag off the grace is 0 and behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged.

Fix 1 — non-cancellable demotion-grace latch (leadership-race vector). A stale
leader (ErrSequencerNotHealthy) now keeps reporting healthy for a fixed 5s grace
so it can receive and commit the op-reth reorg notification before staleness
transfers leadership away. At grace expiry it is demoted UNCONDITIONALLY: a
healthy poll during the grace cannot cancel a pending demotion (a fresh
timestamp does not prove a correct chain), so a node oscillating onto a
fresh-but-wrong fork cannot evade failover. ErrSequencerConnectionDown and any
other error demote immediately. The latch is a pure state machine
(demotion_latch.go); the control loop owns the grace timer and applies the
unconditional demotion at expiry. The health check itself is untouched.

Fix 2 — reconnect-reconcile (WS-gap vector). reth_subscribeChainNotifications
has no replay, so a reorg during a WS disconnect is lost. Each successful
(re)subscribe now emits a synthetic ReorgEvent{Resync:true} so the leader
re-reads and commits its EL's current unsafe head, catching up any missed
reorg. Idempotent (no-op when EL head == FSM head), counted separately
(reorg_resyncs_count).

Fix 3 — subscriber reconnection test. Fake WS server exercises subscribe →
deliver → drop → reconnect → re-subscribe → resume, and asserts Commit frames
are read and ignored (kept alive, no spurious reconnect).

docs(op-conductor): document reorg-recovery demotion grace

Document the Phase 7 non-cancellable 5s demotion grace (and the reconnect
reconcile) added by --reorg-recovery.enabled: a stale leader is held healthy
long enough to commit a deep-reorg head before failing over, then demoted
unconditionally. Notes the operational trade-offs (≤5s added failover latency on
a stuck-but-connected sequencer; one guaranteed leadership handoff per deep
reorg; connection loss still fails over immediately; shallow reorgs unaffected;
grace is 0 when the flag is off) across README, RUNBOOK, and the public mdx.

ci(rust): share the Rust dependency cache across all jobs

The crate-download cache (.cargo/registry, .cargo/git, .cargo/bin,
.rustup) was keyed on the per-job prefix, so each of the ~18 Rust CI
jobs maintained its own copy even though the downloaded crate set is
identical for a given Cargo.lock — independent of job, profile, and
features. On any cold cache every job downloaded the full dependency
set from crates.io in parallel and CircleCI stored a separate multi-GB
copy per job.

Key this cache on a single shared 'rust-deps' prefix (still per-workspace
via the Cargo.lock checksum) so the dependencies are fetched and stored
once and reused by every job. The per-job target/ cache is unchanged.

No fallback key is used on purpose: a Cargo.lock change fully refreshes
the dependency cache rather than accreting old crate versions on top of
the existing set, bounding cache size. Lock changes are infrequent.

ci(rust): cache the Rust toolchain separately from dependencies

.rustup and the cargo-installed binaries (.cargo/bin) were stored in the
dependency cache keyed on Cargo.lock, so every dependency bump threw away
and re-downloaded the entire Rust toolchain — even though the toolchain
is pinned by mise.toml and rust/rust-toolchain.toml, not Cargo.lock.

Split them into a dedicated 'rust-toolchain' cache keyed on those pin
files. The toolchain is now refreshed only when the pins change, while
the dependency cache holds just the downloaded crate sources (registry +
git). Both remain shared across all jobs.

feat(op-node): serve superroot_atTimestamp for non-interop chains (#20581)

* feat(op-node): serve superroot_atTimestamp for non-interop chains

Add a new `superroot` JSON-RPC namespace on op-node with method
`AtTimestamp(timestamp)`, mirroring op-supernode's wire contract
exactly so existing clients (op-challenger, op-dispute-mon) can
point `--supernode-rpc` at op-node URL on non-interop chains.

The handler reuses op-node primitives only — driver SyncStatus +
BlockRefWithStatus, l2EthClient OutputV0AtBlock, and the shared
safedb.L1AtSafeHead walkback — to construct a single-chain
SuperRootAtTimestampResponse byte-compatible with op-supernode's
output for the same chain.

Field semantics are documented in code:

  - CurrentSafeTimestamp / CurrentLocalSafeTimestamp / CurrentFinalizedTimestamp
    pulled directly from SyncStatus, matching op-supernode's per-field
    aggregation collapsed to one chain.
  - VerifiedRequiredL1 (and OptimisticAtTimestamp[chainID].RequiredL1
    on the verified branch) come from safedb.L1AtSafeHead — this is
    the value op-challenger compares against l1Head to gate
    InvalidTransition, so it is correctness-critical, not perf.
  - Optimistic-only branch (block beyond LocalSafeL2 but within UnsafeL2)
    uses the L2 block's L1Origin as RequiredL1, mirroring op-supernode.
  - Pre-genesis / beyond-UnsafeL2 / safeDB-not-found all degrade to
    populated sync fields with Data nil — never zero-out the response
    on transport errors (consumers check CurrentL1.Number first).

Per the issue's resolution by @ajsutton, no activation gate: the API
behaves the same pre- and post-Interop, since a single-chain super
root is well-defined at any timestamp.

Unit tests cover: pre-genesis, beyond-unsafe, optimistic-only,
verified happy path, safeDB-not-found fallback, driver/output
errors, and a runtime SuperRootProvider conformance check (mirror
of op-challenger's and op-dispute-mon's consumer interface).

The compatibility check uses a test-only adapter rather than adding
a SuperRootAtTimestamp method to the live struct — go-ethereum
auto-registers exported methods on RPC services, so a method on the
live struct would leak `superroot_superRootAtTimestamp` as a wire
method. The test-only adapter keeps the wire surface to exactly
`superroot_atTimestamp`.

Refs: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20552

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fixup(op-node): match op-supernode fallback semantics exactly

Address security review on PR #20581. Three fallback branches now
mirror op-supernode chain_container behavior precisely so the new
op-node handler is byte-for-byte equivalent for the single-chain
case across all paths op-challenger and op-dispute-mon exercise:

1. blockNum > LocalSafeL2.Number — was returning an optimistic
   entry with RequiredL1 = ref.L1Origin. op-supernode's
   LocalSafeBlockAtTimestamp returns ethereum.NotFound here, so
   both VerifiedAt and OptimisticAt fail and the chain is OMITTED
   from OptimisticAtTimestamp. Now omits.

2. safeDB returns ErrL1AtSafeHeadNotFound (transient) — was
   returning an optimistic entry with L1Origin. op-supernode's
   safeDBAtL2 maps this to ethereum.NotFound, OptimisticAt fails,
   chain is OMITTED. Now omits.

3. safeDB returns ErrL1AtSafeHeadUnavailable (permanent gap) — was
   silently degrading to optimistic-only. op-supernode's safeDBAtL2
   maps this to ErrHistoryUnavailable which bubbles up as an RPC
   error (operator must intervene). Now returns the wrapped error.

The previous behavior could cause op-challenger's
SuperNodeTraceProvider at step > 0 to include a chain in
expectedState.PendingProgress that op-supernode would have
rejected via InvalidTransition (the consumer reads
OptimisticAtTimestamp[chainID] without checking Data == nil at
non-zero steps).

Tests rewritten to assert the new semantics:
  - TestSuperrootAPI_BeyondLocalSafe_OmitsChain
  - TestSuperrootAPI_SafeDBNotFound_OmitsChain
  - TestSuperrootAPI_SafeDBUnavailable_ReturnsError

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fixup(op-node): reject superroot_atTimestamp when SafeDB disabled

Optional-interface assertion at the top of superrootAPI.atTimestamp:
if the configured SafeDBReader is *safedb.DisabledDB (Enabled()==false),
return a clear error before doing any work. Without this gate, requests
within LocalSafeL2 surface ErrNotEnabled from the helper while requests
beyond LocalSafeL2 short-circuit successfully with Data=nil — an
operator who forgot --safedb.path on a non-interop chain serving
dispute infra would see inconsistent responses and op-challenger would
loop on empty data.

op-supernode does not need an equivalent check: chain_container hard-
codes vncfg.SafeDBPath at virtual-node construction, so SafeDB is
always enabled there. On op-node --safedb.path is optional, so this is
a new failure mode unique to the non-interop path.

Test uses the real safedb.Disabled singleton and sets no driver
expectations — if the handler ever calls SyncStatus before rejecting,
the testify mock fails the test, asserting both the error and the
"before any work" semantics.

ci(rust): speed up Rust CI jobs with a shared sccache compile cache (#21227)

* ci(rust): branch-scoped sccache GCS compile cache for Rust builds

Back the Rust CI compile cache with the op-rust-sccache GCS bucket, with
write access restricted to the develop branch.

- use sccache preinstalled in ci-base-clang (bump the effective rust_base_image
  pin in config.yml + the continuation defaults)
- GCP Workload Identity coords, reader service account, and bucket come from
  the project-restricted sccache-gcs-optimism CircleCI context attached to the
  rust-ci jobs
- read-only reader identity is the default for every ref; develop overrides to
  the read/write writer identity via a native when/equal on pipeline.git.branch
- the write/read split is enforced by GCP Workload Identity on the signed
  CircleCI OIDC vcs-ref claim, so a non-develop ref cannot gain write by editing
  this config; the condition only selects the service account
- sccache error log + idle timeout for observability/robustness
- prints sccache --show-stats at job end

* ci(rust): make sccache setup fail-open and drop the gcloud dependency

The sccache setup ran gcp-cli/install + gcp-oidc-authenticate as unguarded
steps, so a gcloud install break or a job missing the sccache-gcs-optimism
context hard-failed the whole rust job. sccache is an accelerator, not a gate.

- build the Workload Identity ADC config directly (no gcloud) and let sccache
  consume it via GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
- skip with a warning (never fail) when the context/coords are absent, sccache
  is missing, or the server won't start

* ci(rust): attach sccache-gcs-optimism to all Rust workspace builds

The context was only on the rust-ci anchor jobs; the heavy workspace
compiles in the main + rust-e2e workflows (rust-workspace-binaries,
rust-workspace-release, op-rbuilder, rollup-boost) ran without it and so
fell through to the cache-less fail-open path. Attach the context to those
invocations too so every Rust build on ci-base-clang uses the shared cache.

* ci(rust): use sccache in the vendored builds (op-rbuilder, rollup-boost)

Review caught that rust-build-vendored ran a bare cargo build without
RUSTC_WRAPPER, so op-rbuilder and rollup-boost carried the sccache context
but never used the cache. Invoke rust-sccache-setup in the job and set
CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 in the command (this job does not run rust-setup-env),
so a vendored rebuild on a binary-cache miss is sccache-accelerated.

* ci(rust): slim down the sccache start step

Drop the redundant guards (sccache is baked into ci-base-clang; bad/absent
coords just make --start-server fail). Keep the one invariant that matters:
set RUSTC_WRAPPER only when the server actually starts, so a cache/auth/GCS
hiccup yields an uncached build rather than failing every rustc call.

* ci(rust): fail loud if sccache cannot start; cover all routing jobs

Drop the fail-open fallback: set RUSTC_WRAPPER and let the job fail if
sccache --start-server fails, so a broken cache surfaces immediately instead
of silently building uncached. Because rust-sccache-setup now fails loud,
every job that routes through it must carry the sccache-gcs-optimism context
— add it to the kona-publish-prestate-artifacts invocations (the only routing
jobs that lacked it).

* ci(rust): skip sccache where it is not installed (machine-executor jobs)

The cannon jobs (kona-build-fpvm/host-offline/lint) run on a VM machine
executor, not the ci-base-clang image, so sccache is absent and the fail-loud
start hit 'command not found'. Skip when the binary is missing; still fail
loud when sccache is installed but the server won't start.

* ci(rust): dedupe rust-prepare/rust-setup-env into helpers.yml; drop vendored dup

Address review: rust-prepare and rust-setup-env were defined in both main.yml
and rust-ci.yml, with the sccache wiring living only in the rust-ci.yml copy
that happens to win the deep-merge — a footgun (consolidating toward the
main.yml copy would silently disable sccache). Move the single canonical copy
into helpers.yml (merged first), so there is exactly one of each and the
sccache step can't be shadowed. Also remove the byte-identical duplicate
rust-build-vendored definition.

* ci(rust): dedupe Rust cache command definitions

rust-ci.yml redefined rust-build, rust-prepare-and-restore-cache,
rust-restore-build-cache and rust-save-build-cache, duplicating the
canonical definitions in main.yml. Because merge-configs.sh merges
rust-ci.yml after main.yml (later wins), the rust-ci.yml copies silently
shadowed main.yml's, dropping two behaviours that only existed in the
main.yml version:

  - the rust_files_changed fast path that skips cargo build on feature
    branches when rust/ is unchanged (parameter was still passed but
    ignored), and
  - the --bin <binary> filter (BINARY was set but never appended to the
    cargo invocation).

Remove the duplicates so the main.yml definitions are the single source
of truth. No behaviour change beyond restoring the two dropped paths;
merged config validates with circleci config validate.

* ci(rust): share the Rust dependency cache across all jobs

The crate-download cache (.cargo/registry, .cargo/git, .cargo/bin,
.rustup) was keyed on the per-job prefix, so each of the ~18 Rust CI
jobs maintained its own copy even though the downloaded crate set is
identical for a given Cargo.lock — independent of job, profile, and
features. On any cold cache every job downloaded the full dependency
set from crates.io in parallel and CircleCI stored a separate multi-GB
copy per job.

Key this cache on a single shared 'rust-deps' prefix (still per-workspace
via the Cargo.lock checksum) so the dependencies are fetched and stored
once and reused by every job. The per-job target/ cache is unchanged.

No fallback key is used on purpose: a Cargo.lock change fully refreshes
the dependency cache rather than accreting old crate versions on top of
the existing set, bounding cache size. Lock changes are infrequent.

* ci(rust): cache the Rust toolchain separately from dependencies

.rustup and the cargo-installed binaries (.cargo/bin) were stored in the
dependency cache keyed on Cargo.lock, so every dependency bump threw away
and re-downloaded the entire Rust toolchain — even though the toolchain
is pinned by mise.toml and rust/rust-toolchain.toml, not Cargo.lock.

Split them into a dedicated 'rust-toolchain' cache keyed on those pin
files. The toolchain is now refreshed only when the pins change, while
the dependency cache holds just the downloaded crate sources (registry +
git). Both remain shared across all jobs.

* ci(rust): re-attach sccache stats to the consolidated rust-save-build-cache

The sccache --show-stats step lived in the rust-ci.yml copy of
rust-save-build-cache, which was removed by the dedup. Re-add it to the
single canonical rust-save-build-cache in main.yml.

test(devstack): un-skip #21164 light-sequencer interop tests via VN-handoff bootstrap (#21220)

* test(devstack): un-skip #21164 light-sequencer interop tests via VN-handoff bootstrap

A follow-mode ELSync light sequencer cannot bootstrap a chain from genesis: as
the sole block producer it has no peer payload to initial-EL-sync from, so it
deadlocks in willStartEL (#21164). This left two interop tests skipped. Bootstrap
them instead by sequencing on the supernode VN first, then handing off to the
light sequencers, and un-skip:
- TestLightSequencerSupernodeDerivesSafeChain
- TestSupernodeLightSequencerInteropInvalidMessageReplacement (op-reth only)

Preset / runtime
- WithSupernodeVNSequencerForBootstrap: the supernode VN sequences and the light
  follow-mode ELSync sequencers start stopped (l2CLNodeStartConfig.SequencerStopped
  -> driver.Config.SequencerStopped). The VN produces + gossips so the light seqs
  leave willStartEL via initial EL-sync.
- BootstrapLightSequencersViaVNHandoff helper: peers light<->VN, waits for the
  light seqs to EL-sync out of willStartEL, then stops sequencing on the VN and
  starts it on the light CLs.
- Batcher follows the VN during bootstrap, not the (stopped, EL-syncing) light
  seqs. Batching the light seqs leaves a gap at the handoff boundary that wedges
  L1 derivation ("dropping future span batch" forever) so the safe head never
  advances and interop verification stalls. The VN produces during bootstrap and
  tracks the light seqs via gossip after handoff, keeping a gap-free batch stream.
- Expose the supernode VN's EL per chain as L2ASupernodeEL / L2BSupernodeEL (a
  distinct node from L2ELA/L2ELB in light-sequencer mode; aliases them in
  virtual-sequencer mode).

invalid-message scenario
- Settle on cross-safe BEFORE asserting the invalid tx is gone. The unsafe head
  oscillates during recovery (#21119) and can reorg back onto an invalid-containing
  fork after the replacement validates; reading the block by number off the unsafe
  tip caught that transient. Once cross-safe advances past the block it is
  irreversible, so the read is stable.
- Anchor the post-recovery new-tx check on the supernode VN's L1-derived safe
  chain (the canonical source of truth): follow the tx by hash until it lands at or
  below the supernode's safe head, then assert it is present on BOTH the light

fix(op-e2e): lazily generate genesis allocs per alloc type (#21238)

The op-e2e/config init() unconditionally ran a full op-deployer genesis
pipeline for all 4 alloc types across 9 hardfork modes (36 pipelines) at
test-binary startup, costing minutes of CPU before any test ran. The
op-e2e-fuzz job runs three concurrent `go test -fuzz ./opgeth` processes;
each paid this full cost, oversubscribing CPU on the CI box. Under load the
combined startup exceeded the 15m no-output timeout, killing the job with
zero output from all three targets (including the pure-Go FuzzFastLzCgo,
which shares the binary and was blocked behind the same init).

Generate each alloc type lazily and once, so a binary only pays for the
alloc types its tests request. The opgeth fuzz binary uses only
DefaultAllocType, cutting its work from 4 alloc types to 1, and the two
FastLz targets need none, so they now start and stream output in seconds.

Refs ethereum-optimism/optimism#21191

fix(ci): correct BASE_REVISION typo (devlop -> develop) (#21244)

prepare-continuation-config set BASE_REVISION: devlop. collect-params.sh
computes the changed-file set with git diff --name-only "origin/${BASE_REVISION}...HEAD"
and, on failure, silently falls back to git diff HEAD~1 HEAD. Because
origin/devlop does not exist, the diff against the merge base never ran and
change detection only saw the *last commit* of a multi-commit PR — so a PR
that changed rust/ or contracts in an earlier commit but ended on a docs-only
commit could be misclassified and skip its required tests.

Reproduced: origin/devlop does not resolve (triggering the HEAD~1 fallback);
origin/develop resolves. No unit test added: collect-params.sh is not
unit-tested and test-decision-tree.sh stubs the parameter JSON rather than
exercising the diff, so there is no natural harness for this one-line config
value; the fix is verified by ref resolution above.

fix(kona-host): retry witness fetches via the get_preimage loop, not debug_dbGet

debug_executePayload (the L2PayloadWitness hint) and the L2BlockData
optimistic-block re-execution are "high-level" hints that bulk-populate the
preimage store. They were fetched once when received and discarded, so any
error was terminal: the client fell back to per-node debug_dbGet, which
op-reth does not implement, turning a transient failure into a permanent one.

Instead of fetching high-level hints eagerly, retain the latest one and let
the existing get_preimage retry loop service it: each attempt tries the
high-level hint first (bulk-populating the store), then the fine-grained
hints. A high-level hint is cleared once it succeeds (its response is
deterministic) and kept while it fails, so a transient error is retried
indefinitely without re-running an already-satisfied hint. debug_dbGet
remains the fallback only when the node genuinely lacks debug_executePayload
(JSON-RPC method-not-found).

is_rpc_method_not_found and the debug_executePayload call are consolidated
into backend::util, removing the duplication between the single-chain and
interop handlers.

fix(op-challenger): tear down VM process group on timeout

The VM (cannon) spawns the oracle/preimage server as its own child, which
inherits the VM's stdout/stderr pipes. exec.CommandContext only SIGKILLs the
direct child on timeout, so the oracle server is orphaned and keeps the pipe
write ends open. cmd.Wait then blocks forever and the VM timeout never actually
terminates a wedged run.

Run the VM in its own process group, kill the whole group on cancellation, and
set a bounded WaitDelay as a backstop so RunCmd always returns once the context
is cancelled.

feat(kona-executor): make StatelessL2Builder/KonaExecutor generic over receipt builder

Parameterizes `StatelessL2Builder`, `KonaExecutor`, `BlockBuildingOutcome`,
and `Executor::Receipt` over a receipt builder `R: OpReceiptBuilder`.
In-tree call sites pass `OpAlloyReceiptBuilder::default()` so the OP path
is byte-for-byte identical.

## Motivation

Celo (a downstream OP-Stack fork) needs to produce blocks whose receipts
include a CIP-64 variant. The stateless executor currently pipes
`OpReceiptEnvelope` through everywhere, so the only way to ship Celo's
receipt envelope is to fork the entire builder + executor. This change
swaps the concrete type for a single generic parameter.

## Trait extensions

`OpReceiptBuilder` gains:

* `strip_deposit_nonce(&self, receipt: &mut Self::Receipt)` — required
  (no default). Drives the Regolith receipts-root fixup that was
  previously inlined in `compute_receipts_root`. Required so any
  downstream implementor whose receipt envelope carries a deposit nonce
  is forced to confront the fixup at compile time rather than silently
  inherit a no-op.
* `type Receipt: TxReceipt<Log = Log> + Clone` — moves a bound bundle off
  every kona-executor impl site. `Encodable2718` stays as a call-site
  bound because not every impl's `Receipt` implements it.

## Compatibility

* No generic default on `R` — every caller is updated explicitly.
* Out-of-tree `OpReceiptBuilder` implementors need to add a
  `strip_deposit_nonce` impl.
* Out-of-tree `Executor` implementors need to add
  `type Receipt = ...;`.
* Wire formats are unchanged.

## Follow-up

The transaction side is still concrete (`Transaction = OpTxEnvelope`);
parameterizing it is a separate change.

feat(sdm): enforce MAX_GAS_LIMIT on pre-refund EVM gas

SDM (post-exec) refunds let canonical, post-refund gas fall arbitrarily
below the real work performed, so the operational block-gas-limit rate
limit no longer bounds real compute once refunds appear. Cap the
pre-refund sum of evm_gas_used per block at MAX_GAS_LIMIT (500M, mirroring
SystemConfig.MAX_GAS_LIMIT) so a sequencer can never make a block prove
more computation than the system is designed to prove, even at 100%
refund.

Layer 1 (consensus, alloy-op-evm OpBlockExecutor): accumulate pre-refund
evm_gas_used and reject a tx whose declared gas limit would push the sum
past the ceiling, mirroring the existing block-gas-limit admission check.
This single change covers op-reth verifier replicas and the kona fault
proof, both of which verify through OpBlockExecutor.

Layer 2 (producers): op-rbuilder and the op-reth standard builder
self-limit before feeding txs to the executor, so honest blocks always
verify. The binding cumulative persists across flashblocks (each
flashblock gets a fresh executor whose internal accumulator resets).

re-added here with a real consumer. Producers read it through the new
PreRefundGasUsed trait since the generic BlockExecutor::Result associated
type is otherwise opaque.

Tracking: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20709

Fix 1 — non-cancellable demotion-grace latch (leadership-race vector). A stale
leader (ErrSequencerNotHealthy) now keeps reporting healthy for a fixed 5s grace
so it can receive and commit the op-reth reorg notification before staleness
transfers leadership away. At grace expiry it is demoted UNCONDITIONALLY: a
healthy poll during the grace cannot cancel a pending demotion (a fresh
timestamp does not prove a correct chain), so a node oscillating onto a
fresh-but-wrong fork cannot evade failover. ErrSequencerConnectionDown and any
other error demote immediately. The latch is a pure state machine
(demotion_latch.go); the control loop owns the grace timer and applies the
unconditional demotion at expiry. The health check itself is untouched.

Fix 2 — reconnect-reconcile (WS-gap vector). reth_subscribeChainNotifications
has no replay, so a reorg during a WS disconnect is lost. Each successful
(re)subscribe now emits a synthetic ReorgEvent{Resync:true} so the leader
re-reads and commits its EL's current unsafe head, catching up any missed
reorg. Idempotent (no-op when EL head == FSM head), counted separately
(reorg_resyncs_count).

Fix 3 — subscriber reconnection test. Fake WS server exercises subscribe →
deliver → drop → reconnect → re-subscribe → resume, and asserts Commit frames
are read and ignored (kept alive, no spurious reconnect).

docs(op-conductor): document reorg-recovery demotion grace

Document the Phase 7 non-cancellable 5s demotion grace (and the reconnect
reconcile) added by --reorg-recovery.enabled: a stale leader is held healthy
long enough to commit a deep-reorg head before failing over, then demoted
unconditionally. Notes the operational trade-offs (≤5s added failover latency on
a stuck-but-connected sequencer; one guaranteed leadership handoff per deep
reorg; connection loss still fails over immediately; shallow reorgs unaffected;
grace is 0 when the flag is off) across README, RUNBOOK, and the public mdx.

test(conductor-reorg): wire VN-hub star EL P2P topology for bootstrap

The conductor reorg-recovery harness bootstraps its follow-mode ELSync
sequencers via a supernode VN that produces genesis blocks, then hands off
(#21164 — a follow-mode sequencer cannot bootstrap from genesis as sole
producer). Each candidate EL had a single P2P link to the primary sequencer
EL; if that lone link lost its connection race, the candidate sat at genesis
(connected_peers=0, stuck in the reth Headers stage) for the whole bootstrap
window and the gate timed out (~1/100).

Replace the ad-hoc links with a star topology: every conductor sequencer EL
(primary + candidates) peers only with the supernode VN EL as the hub, and
trusts it so reth auto-reconnects if the link drops. Sequencer ELs are
deliberately not meshed — the cluster is a leaderless raft with no
source-of-truth sequencer, so candidate<->candidate peering let a node sync a
divergent pre-reorg chain from a sibling and broke convergence after deep
reorgs. Routing all block-body sync through the VN hub keeps every node
tracking the single canonical head.

Validated: 100/100 passes of TestConductorDeepReorgRecoveryTightHealth (was
~99/100 with the single-link race; a transitional full-mesh variant instead
introduced ~5% leadership thrash, which the VN-only star eliminates).

feat(op-reth): multi-endpoint quorum validation for interop filter (#21195)

* feat(op-reth): multi-endpoint quorum validation for interop filter

Fan out interop_checkAccessList to multiple interop-filter endpoints
concurrently inside InteropFilterClient and combine by quorum agreement:
a definitive verdict (valid, or a known SuperchainDAError rejection) counts
toward quorum; transport errors and timeouts do not. The aggregator decides
once min_responses verdicts arrive and does not await slower endpoints.
Accept iff all collected verdicts are valid; all-invalid surfaces the real
reason; a mix logs and rejects (Disagreement); too few definitive verdicts
fail closed (QuorumNotReached). A failsafe reported by any endpoint is a hard
short-circuit rejection regardless of quorum.

query_failsafe ORs admin_getFailsafeEnabled across endpoints, short-circuiting
on the first true so a slow endpoint cannot delay the failsafe poll.

CLI: --rollup.interop-http is now repeatable and --rollup.interop-min-responses
sets the quorum (defaults to the endpoint count, i.e. unanimity / fail-closed).
Single-endpoint configs behave as before. Updates OpPoolBuilder and the
op-rbuilder callers for the new with_interop signature.

* feat(op-reth): detect interop failsafe by dedicated RPC code -320602

Switch failsafe detection in from_json_rpc from matching the error message
to the dedicated JSON-RPC error code -320602 the op-interop-filter server
emits, replacing the previously overloaded -32602. Detection is now by code
only, never by message text. The query_failsafe OR poll and the
check_access_list hard short-circuit on any-endpoint failsafe are unchanged.

This is a hard cutover: detection requires the filter to emit -320602, a
prerequisite server change that must deploy first.

* feat(op-reth): a received failsafe beats a met quorum, deterministically

When the valid+invalid quorum is reached, non-blocking-drain the endpoint
futures that are already ready before returning Ok, and reject if any is
FailsafeEnabled. This makes "a failsafe that has arrived rejects even when the
minimum valids are in hand" deterministic instead of arrival-order dependent.
Endpoints that have not responded are still never awaited (fast-accept is
preserved); dropping the futures cancels them.

Make failsafe_on_any_endpoint_hard_rejects deterministic by requiring all
endpoints to resolve before the decision, and add a test proving a slow
non-failsafe endpoint does not delay accept.

* fix(op-reth): classify filter verdicts — definitive rejections vs soft out-of-sync

Two related classification fixes for the multi-endpoint interop aggregator.

Definitive rejections: a fabricated access list entry is rejected by the filter
with a generic -32602 "failed to parse access entry" (not a SuperchainDAError
code). is_definitive_invalid only counted InvalidEntry, so this legitimate
rejection was mis-classified as a non-response — with a single endpoint (min=1)
the aggregator collected 0 definitive verdicts and returned QuorumNotReached
instead of the filter's real rejection, regressing
TestInteropFilter_IngressRejectsInvalid. Now any JSON-RPC error response from
the filter is a definitive verdict (new Rejected { code, message } variant,
preserving the real reason) except the JSON-RPC internal error -32603, which
stays a non-response.

Soft out-of-sync failures: codes meaning "this node does not have the data yet"
— FutureData (-321401) and Uninitialized (-320400) — are soft, non-response
failures (new DataUnavailable variant; neither definitive_invalid nor failsafe).
A single out-of-sync node is ignored as long as the quorum is met by other
nodes; if every node is out of sync the aggregator fails closed
(QuorumNotReached). FutureData is a SuperchainDAError variant, so the soft check
precedes the SuperchainDAError mapping.

Classification order in from_json_rpc: no error response → Other (transport);
-320602 → FailsafeEnabled; (-321401|-320400) → DataUnavailable; SuperchainDAError
→ InvalidEntry; -32603 → Other; else → Rejected.

Verified with the op-acceptance-tests interop/filter suite:
TestInteropFilter_IngressRejectsInvalid and TestInteropFilter_FailsafeLifecycle
both pass.

* fix(op-reth): address interop-filter multi-endpoint review feedback

- query_failsafe no longer clears the failsafe gate on partial replies:

- Spell out in --rollup.interop-min-responses help that the unanimity default

fix(txinclude): budget operator fees with the Jovian formula (#17817)

txinclude estimated and reconciled operator fees with the Isthmus formula
(gasUsed * scalar / 1e6 + constant), which under-budgets on Jovian chains
where the formula is gasUsed * scalar * 100 + constant.

(all production chains) and is >= the Isthmus result for any inputs, so on a
pre-Jovian chain it only over-reserves budget and never under-budgets.

fix(ci): remove the rust target-dir build cache (was serving stale binaries)

Acceptance jobs (e.g. memory-all-opn-op-reth) failed deterministically with
"op-reth proofs init: unexpected argument '--proofs-history.skip-backfill'":
the Go sysgo harness passed a new op-reth CLI flag while CI ran a stale op-reth.

Root cause was the rust target-dir cache. It was keyed only on Cargo.lock and
save_cache is immutable per key, so a source-only change that adds a CLI flag
(without touching Cargo.lock) never rotated the key and the cache kept serving
the pre-change binary. The rust-build job then skipped cargo build on non-
develop branches whenever the PR didn't touch rust/, reusing that stale binary.

Rather than add more machinery to detect staleness, drop the target-dir cache
entirely. Rust builds now always run cargo build; the dependency cache (keyed
on Cargo.lock) and sccache keep that fast. Toolchain and vendored-binary caches
are unaffected (the vendored cache is keyed on the directory's git tree hash, so
it can't go stale the same way).

- Remove the "rust target cache" restore/save from rust-restore-build-cache and
  rust-save-build-cache (deps + toolchain caches kept).
- Remove the rust_files_changed skip from rust-build and all its plumbing
  (params, call sites, the c-rust_files_changed pipeline parameter and its
  detection/forwarding in config.yml).
- Pin the sysgo acceptance job to RUST_BINARY_PATH_OP_RETH (the var rustbin
  actually reads); OP_RETH_EXEC_PATH was dead for the Go path.
- rustbin now selects the newest binary by mtime instead of alphabetically,
  which previously preferred a stale target/debug over a fresh target/release.

The now-unused profile/features/prefix params on the cache commands are left in
place to keep this change focused; a follow-up can strip them.

fix(op-acceptance-tests): deflake TestReorgUnsafeHead batcher race

TestReorgUnsafeHead intermittently failed at the first ReorgExact with
"expected head to reorg <hash>, but got <same hash>": the EL never kept
the conflicting block at the divergence height.

Root cause: the batcher was restarted (L2BatcherA.Start) right after the
test-sequencer committed the conflicting block, i.e. during the reorg
window where op-node's reported sync status and the EL's canonical chain
disagree. The batcher picks the *range* of blocks to load from op-node's
syncStatus.unsafeL2 (the conflicting head) but loads each block's
*content* by number directly from the EL (BlockByNumber), which at that
instant still returned the ORIGINAL block — op-node's lagging forkchoice
had transiently swapped it back. The batcher then anchored the original
block to L1; once derivation made it safe, the original chain was pinned
and the unsafe reorg could never stick.

Fix: move L2BatcherA.Start() to after the existing wait that confirms
op-node's sync status matches the test-sequencer's committed head, so the
batcher's range and content reads both reflect the conflicting chain and
it anchors the conflicting block instead of the original.

perf(op-interop-mon): query interop-filter once per terminal job

Re-checking every terminal job on each 1s cycle issued one RPC per in-flight
job per second. The observer now queries each job once (marking it checked only
after a real verdict, so transport errors retry), which also makes the
divergence counter fire at most once per job.

fix(op-interop-mon): re-check interop-filter when monitor verdict changes

The filter observer gated its divergence check on a one-shot "already checked"
flag, which stopped re-issuing the per-job RPC every cycle but also skipped the
job permanently. A terminal job can flip verdict (e.g. valid->invalid after an
initiating-chain reorg, which UpdateStatus appends), so divergences appearing
after a flip went unrecorded.

Track the monitor status last compared against the filter (encoded so the zero
value means "never checked") and re-query only when that status changes. This
keeps RPCs bounded in the steady state while preserving divergence detection
across status flips. Adds a regression test.

feat(kona-executor): make StatelessL2Builder/KonaExecutor generic over receipt builder

Parameterizes `StatelessL2Builder`, `KonaExecutor`, `BlockBuildingOutcome`,
and `Executor::Receipt` over a receipt builder `R: OpReceiptBuilder`.
In-tree call sites pass `OpAlloyReceiptBuilder::default()` so the OP path
is byte-for-byte identical.

## Motivation

Celo (a downstream OP-Stack fork) needs to produce blocks whose receipts
include a CIP-64 variant. The stateless executor currently pipes
`OpReceiptEnvelope` through everywhere, so the only way to ship Celo's
receipt envelope is to fork the entire builder + executor. This change
swaps the concrete type for a single generic parameter.

## Trait extensions

`OpReceiptBuilder` gains:

* `strip_deposit_nonce(&self, receipt: &mut Self::Receipt)` — required
  (no default). Drives the Regolith receipts-root fixup that was
  previously inlined in `compute_receipts_root`. Required so any
  downstream implementor whose receipt envelope carries a deposit nonce
  is forced to confront the fixup at compile time rather than silently
  inherit a no-op.
* `type Receipt: TxReceipt<Log = Log> + Clone` — moves a bound bundle off
  every kona-executor impl site. `Encodable2718` stays as a call-site
  bound because not every impl's `Receipt` implements it.

## Compatibility

* No generic default on `R` — every caller is updated explicitly.
* Out-of-tree `OpReceiptBuilder` implementors need to add a
  `strip_deposit_nonce` impl.
* Out-of-tree `Executor` implementors need to add
  `type Receipt = ...;`.
* Wire formats are unchanged.

## Follow-up

The transaction side is still concrete (`Transaction = OpTxEnvelope`);
parameterizing it is a separate change.

fix(op-acceptance-tests): deflake TestReorgUnsafeHead batcher race (#21307)

TestReorgUnsafeHead intermittently failed at the first ReorgExact with
"expected head to reorg <hash>, but got <same hash>": the EL never kept
the conflicting block at the divergence height.

Root cause: the batcher was restarted (L2BatcherA.Start) right after the
test-sequencer committed the conflicting block, i.e. during the reorg
window where op-node's reported sync status and the EL's canonical chain
disagree. The batcher picks the *range* of blocks to load from op-node's
syncStatus.unsafeL2 (the conflicting head) but loads each block's
*content* by number directly from the EL (BlockByNumber), which at that
instant still returned the ORIGINAL block — op-node's lagging forkchoice
had transiently swapped it back. The batcher then anchored the original
block to L1; once derivation made it safe, the original chain was pinned
and the unsafe reorg could never stick.

Fix: move L2BatcherA.Start() to after the existing wait that confirms
op-node's sync status matches the test-sequencer's committed head, so the
batcher's range and content reads both reflect the conflicting chain and
it anchors the conflicting block instead of the original.

fix(ci): remove the rust target-dir build cache (was serving stale binaries) (#21310)

Acceptance jobs (e.g. memory-all-opn-op-reth) failed deterministically with
"op-reth proofs init: unexpected argument '--proofs-history.skip-backfill'":
the Go sysgo harness passed a new op-reth CLI flag while CI ran a stale op-reth.

Root cause was the rust target-dir cache. It was keyed only on Cargo.lock and
save_cache is immutable per key, so a source-only change that adds a CLI flag
(without touching Cargo.lock) never rotated the key and the cache kept serving
the pre-change binary. The rust-build job then skipped cargo build on non-
develop branches whenever the PR didn't touch rust/, reusing that stale binary.

Rather than add more machinery to detect staleness, drop the target-dir cache
entirely. Rust builds now always run cargo build; the dependency cache (keyed
on Cargo.lock) and sccache keep that fast. Toolchain and vendored-binary caches
are unaffected (the vendored cache is keyed on the directory's git tree hash, so
it can't go stale the same way).

- Remove the "rust target cache" restore/save from rust-restore-build-cache and
  rust-save-build-cache (deps + toolchain caches kept).
- Remove the rust_files_changed skip from rust-build and all its plumbing
  (params, call sites, the c-rust_files_changed pipeline parameter and its
  detection/forwarding in config.yml).
- Pin the sysgo acceptance job to RUST_BINARY_PATH_OP_RETH (the var rustbin
  actually reads); OP_RETH_EXEC_PATH was dead for the Go path.
- rustbin now selects the newest binary by mtime instead of alphabetically,
  which previously preferred a stale target/debug over a fresh target/release.

The now-unused profile/features/prefix params on the cache commands are left in
place to keep this change focused; a follow-up can strip them.

feat(sdm): enforce block gas limit on pre-refund EVM gas (#21250)

* feat(sdm): enforce MAX_GAS_LIMIT on pre-refund EVM gas

SDM (post-exec) refunds let canonical, post-refund gas fall arbitrarily
below the real work performed, so the operational block-gas-limit rate
limit no longer bounds real compute once refunds appear. Cap the
pre-refund sum of evm_gas_used per block at MAX_GAS_LIMIT (500M, mirroring
SystemConfig.MAX_GAS_LIMIT) so a sequencer can never make a block prove
more computation than the system is designed to prove, even at 100%
refund.

Layer 1 (consensus, alloy-op-evm OpBlockExecutor): accumulate pre-refund
evm_gas_used and reject a tx whose declared gas limit would push the sum
past the ceiling, mirroring the existing block-gas-limit admission check.
This single change covers op-reth verifier replicas and the kona fault
proof, both of which verify through OpBlockExecutor.

Layer 2 (producers): op-rbuilder and the op-reth standard builder
self-limit before feeding txs to the executor, so honest blocks always
verify. The binding cumulative persists across flashblocks (each
flashblock gets a fresh executor whose internal accumulator resets).

re-added here with a real consumer. Producers read it through the new
PreRefundGasUsed trait since the generic BlockExecutor::Result associated
type is otherwise opaque.

feat: support Tenderly's new ?draft= simulation link format

Tenderly shipped a breaking change to how the Simulator hydrates a
pre-filled form from a URL. The old query-param format
(network/contractAddress/from/stateOverrides/rawFunctionInput) no longer
applies state overrides or gas — signers had to re-enter everything by
hand, defeating the purpose of the printed link.

The new format encodes the whole simulation as a single JSON payload,
base64url-encoded (no padding), in a ?draft= query parameter:

  https://dashboard.tenderly.co/<org>/<project>/simulator/new?draft=<b64url(json)>

Changes:
- MultisigTaskPrinter.getTenderlySimulationLink builds the draft payload
  (v/network.id/row with contractAddress, from, inputDataType, gas,
  rawFunctionInput, stateOverrides) and encodes it with solady Base64
  (fileSafe + noPadding). printTenderlySimulationData uses it.
- Length fallback: the new format caps usable links at ~2000 chars, so
  when calldata is too large to embed, the link is built without
  rawFunctionInput and the calldata is printed separately for manual
  paste into the Simulator's "Raw input data" field (mirrors prior
  long-URL behavior).
- Unit tests covering the inline, no-raw-input, and no-gas paths.
- Docs updated to the new format.

feat(op-reth): evict pooled interop txs on a permanently-invalid filter verdict; configurable validity window

Two changes to the interop txpool:

1. Act on the filter verdict when revalidating a pooled interop tx.
   Previously a filter rejection on revalidation was silently ignored:
   maintain.rs evicted only when is_bad_transaction(), which is false for
   every InvalidCrossTx::ValidationError, so the filter's verdict on an
   already-pooled tx was never acted on. Eviction now goes through
   InvalidCrossTx::should_evict_on_revalidation ->
   InteropTxValidatorError::is_message_permanently_invalid, matching only
   ConflictingData / IneffectiveData / DataCorruption. This is
   deliberately narrower than is_definitive_invalid() (which includes
   OutOfScope): transient / out-of-sync verdicts (OutOfScope, FutureData,
   QuorumNotReached, Disagreement, Timeout) keep the tx, so a
   momentarily-lagging filter never drops a valid transaction.

2. Make the interop validity window configurable. The hardcoded
   CHECK_ACCESS_LIST_TIMEOUT_SECS (the pool interop_deadline and the
   ExecutingDescriptor timeout sent to the filter) becomes
   --rollup.interop-validity-window, default
   DEFAULT_INTEROP_VALIDITY_WINDOW_SECS = 120, threaded through the
   validator and the interop maintenance task.

Revalidation cadence is unchanged (the existing OFFSET_TIME stale gate).

fix(op-rbuilder): append trailing SDM PostExec tx in the standard builder

The standard builder threaded the post-exec mode into its ctx — so in
Produce mode the executor applied SDM refund settlement to state and
post-refund gas to receipts — but never materialized the trailing
PostExec (0x7D) tx carrying the refund entries. A verifier re-executes
the block with the mode derived from its transactions, finds no 0x7D,
runs with SDM disabled, and computes a different state root: every
block built by an opted-in standard-mode builder was consensus-invalid.

Materialize the tx at the end of OpBuilder::execute with the same
produce-side rules as op-reth's try_include_post_exec_tx and the
flashblocks builder's materialize_post_exec (shared via the new
context::build_current_post_exec_tx): empty entries produce no tx, the
sender is the zero address, and the tx is appended last. Derived
blocks (no_tx_pool) never append — they must reproduce exactly the
attribute transactions.

The new integration test runs both builder variants on a chain with
Interop (Lagoon) at genesis and pins the operator opt-in contract:
no PostExec tx without the opt-in, exactly one trailing anchored
PostExec tx with non-empty entries under a repeated-slot workload with
it, and none again after opting out. The driver round-trips every
payload through newPayload, so the missing-append bug fails it with a
state-root mismatch (verified against the unfixed builder). The test
framework now registers SdmAdminExt like the production launcher and
exposes an IPC rpc_client() for extension namespaces.

alloy-op-evm: reject user txs in fork-activation blocks

A fork-activation block (the first L2 block at/after a fork >= Jovian) must
contain only deposit transactions. op-geth enforces this at the executor /
consensus-validity layer (CalcDAFootprint); the shared Rust executor
(alloy-op-evm, used by both op-reth and kona-client) did not — a latent
consensus-validity divergence where op-reth / kona-client would accept an
activation block with user txs that op-geth rejects.

Add a guard to OpBlockExecutor that rejects any non-deposit (user) tx on a
fork-activation block. The block is detected from a new required
OpBlockExecutionCtx::parent_timestamp via OpHardfork::Jovian.forks_from(), so the
rule covers Jovian, Karst, Lagoon and any future fork automatically.
parent_timestamp is populated where the parent header is available (kona
StatelessL2Builder — the fault-proof path — and op-reth block building); op-reth's
block-import / engine-newPayload paths pass None and defer to the derivation
layer (op-node + kona drop user-tx batches in fork-activation blocks).

Also adds OpHardfork::forks_from() to alloy-op-hardforks (a go-ethereum
forks.From analogue).

fix(op-reth): verify embedded PostExec tx when rebuilding derived blocks

When a node rebuilds an externally-derived block via FCU-with-attributes
(no_tx_pool=true) — sequencer-window expiry, reorg recovery, or a verifier with
no unsafe block to consolidate against — the payload builder chose its post-exec
mode purely from the local SDM production opt-in (Produce when on, Disabled when
off) and never Verify. op-node embeds the block-level PostExec tx (0x7D) into the
batch, so it arrives in the derived attributes:

- opt-in off (the normal verifier case): the executor runs in Disabled mode and
  fatally rejects the embedded 0x7D ("unexpected post-exec tx ... SDM not
  active"), aborting the build, so the node cannot reproduce the block and its
  safe head stalls.
- opt-in on: the embedded 0x7D is accepted in Produce mode and a second PostExec
  tx is then appended, diverging from the canonical block.

The opt-in is a sequencer-only control over whether to produce; verifiers must
reproduce the canonical block regardless of it. Centralize the decision in
OpPayloadBuilderCtx::post_exec_mode():

- no_tx_pool (rebuilding a derived block): parse the attributes for an embedded
  0x7D and Verify against it (Disabled if absent), ignoring the opt-in; never
  produce.
- otherwise (local sequencing): produce iff SDM is protocol-active and the
  operator opted in.

Also gate the post-exec-tx append so it only runs when locally producing, which
prevents the double-append on the no_tx_pool path.

Covered by TestSDMPostExecBlockDerivesOnIsolatedVerifier and the
reth-optimism-payload-builder unit tests, both of which fail without this change.

fix(rollup-boost): materialize SDM post_exec_tx in flashblock payloads

Each flashblock carries the current trailing SDM PostExec transaction in
diff.post_exec_tx, which replaces the previous one rather than
accumulating in the append-only diff.transactions list. rollup-boost's
FlashblockBuilder dropped it when materializing the execution payload,
so the materialized block no longer hashed to the builder's
diff.block_hash, the sequencer EL rejected it via newPayload, and
op-node fell back to the EL's independently-built block.

- rollup-boost: materialize the block as base + concat(all
  diff.transactions) + latest(diff.post_exec_tx), with unit tests for
  the append/replace/omit cases on V3 and V4 payloads.
- op-rbuilder: accumulate receipt cumulative gas from the committed
  (post-SDM-refund) gas instead of the pre-refund EVM result gas, which
  caused a receipt-root mismatch on canonical verification.
- acceptance test: assert the canonical block hash equals the builder's
  diff.block_hash, pinning the test to the rollup-boost materialization
  path instead of passing under the EL fallback.

fix(op-devstack): fail fast when kona-node exits before its RPC is ready

A kona-node that launched but exited before binding its RPC (e.g. a crash on
boot, or a stand-in binary that exits immediately) left KonaNode.Start blocked
on the RPC-readiness channel until the test's context deadline — turning a quick
boot failure into a multi-minute timeout.

Give SubProcess a single owned cmd.Wait() that runs in a goroutine and closes a
new Exited() channel, and have Stop consume that result instead of calling Wait
a second time (behavior-preserving for all SubProcess users). KonaNode.Start now
selects on Exited() alongside the RPC channel and fails immediately with
"kona-node exited before its RPC server became ready" when the process dies first.

fix(op-interop-mon): treat not-ready/failsafe filter errors as non-verdicts

filterValid := err == nil treated every structured rpc.Error as an "invalid"
verdict and latched it. But the filter returns non-verdict codes: failsafe
rejects all calls (flooding false divergences during the exact incident the
monitor observes), and future/out-of-scope/uninitialized mean the filter has
not yet caught up to the monitor, which decides validity off raw receipts and
runs ahead. Classify those codes as non-verdicts: log and leave the job
unmarked so it retries, recording a divergence only on a real validity verdict.

The failsafe now lives in op-interop-filter. Drop the legacy supervisor

read-only interop_filter_failsafe gauge still observes the filter's state.

* chore(op-interop-mon): remove local design/plan docs from PR

* refactor(op-interop-mon): address PR review feedback

- Reuse op-service sources.InteropFilterClient.CheckAccessList instead of
  re-implementing interop_checkAccessList; keep admin_getFailsafeEnabled as a
  direct call (admin namespace, not the interop query API).
- Reuse op-service sources.SuperNodeClient; drop the separate heartbeat probe
  and derive supernode_up from whether syncStatus succeeds.
- Count initiating_reorgs_total, filter_divergence_total and
  cross_safety_violations_total once per job (atomic flags) instead of once per
  1s collection cycle, so they are true event counters.
- Treat only structured JSON-RPC errors as a filter verdict; skip transport/
  timeout errors rather than recording a false divergence.
- Verify the executing block is still canonical (by hash) before flagging a
  cross-safety violation, avoiding false positives during reorgs.
- Thread the service's cancelable context into the observers so in-flight RPCs
  are cancelled on shutdown.

* perf(op-interop-mon): query interop-filter once per terminal job

Re-checking every terminal job on each 1s cycle issued one RPC per in-flight
job per second. The observer now queries each job once (marking it checked only
after a real verdict, so transport errors retry), which also makes the
divergence counter fire at most once per job.

* fix(op-interop-mon): re-check interop-filter when monitor verdict changes

The filter observer gated its divergence check on a one-shot "already checked"
flag, which stopped re-issuing the per-job RPC every cycle but also skipped the
job permanently. A terminal job can flip verdict (e.g. valid->invalid after an
initiating-chain reorg, which UpdateStatus appends), so divergences appearing
after a flip went unrecorded.

Track the monitor status last compared against the filter (encoded so the zero
value means "never checked") and re-query only when that status changes. This
keeps RPCs bounded in the steady state while preserving divergence detection
across status flips. Adds a regression test.

* perf(op-interop-mon): skip canonical-block re-fetch for counted violations

A confirmed cross-safety violation persists in the job map until finalization,
so the supernode observer re-fetched the canonical block (InfoByNumber) for it
on every 1s cycle even though the metric only fires once. Skip jobs whose
violation has already been counted, before issuing the fetch.

* fix(op-interop-mon): default metric collector context

CollectMetrics passes m.ctx to the observers; if it were ever invoked before
Start (which sets the cancelable context), that would nil-deref in
context.WithTimeout. Default the field to context.Background() in the
constructor; Start still replaces it with the cancelable child.

* fix(op-interop-mon): reject unsupported interop-filter min-safety at startup

The interop-filter only checks access lists at unsafe or cross-unsafe; safe and
finalized error on every call, which (combined with verdict classification)
would flag every job as a divergence. Validate the configured level against the
filter-supported set at startup and fix the flag usage text.

* fix(op-interop-mon): treat not-ready/failsafe filter errors as non-verdicts

filterValid := err == nil treated every structured rpc.Error as an "invalid"
verdict and latched it. But the filter returns non-verdict codes: failsafe
rejects all calls (flooding false divergences during the exact incident the
monitor observes), and future/out-of-scope/uninitialized mean the filter has
not yet caught up to the monitor, which decides validity off raw receipts and
runs ahead. Classify those codes as non-verdicts: log and leave the job
unmarked so it retries, recording a divergence only on a real validity verdict.

* refactor(op-interop-mon): drop constant level label from cross_safety_violations

The level label was always the literal "cross_safe", so it added a metric
dimension with a single value. Remove it; it can be reintroduced if finalized
violations are tracked later.

* fix(kona-executor): pin BLOBBASEFEE to 1 on the OP Stack

The fault-proof executor derived the EIP-4844 blob env from the parent
header via maybe_next_block_excess_blob_gas. Post-Jovian the header
blobGasUsed field is repurposed to carry the block's DA footprint, so
feeding it into the excess-blob-gas update rule produced a blob base fee
greater than 1 once the parent footprint exceeded ~4.26M, diverging from
the canonical chain (op-geth/op-reth always pin BLOBBASEFEE to 1) and
breaking dispute-game soundness.

matching op-reth's evm_env_for_op. The next_block_base_fee path, which
correctly consumes the DA footprint for the Jovian EIP-1559 update, is
unchanged.

Adds a unit test asserting blob_gasprice == 1 for a large parent DA
footprint, and a fault-proof action test that reproduces the state
divergence end-to-end via a BLOBBASEFEE-reading contract.

* feat(op-reth): consolidate interop filter metrics into labeled counters

Collapse the per-reason and per-quorum-outcome counters into one labeled
decision counter, and add quorum-margin observability:

- filter_decisions_total{result, reason}: one increment per tx reaching the
  filter. `result` is the outcome (allowed, rejected_pre_interop,
  rejected_failsafe, rejected_invalid, rejected_disagreement,
  rejected_no_quorum, errored); `reason` carries the DA reason for

  counters: `sum by (result)` is the outcome breakdown and
  `sum by (reason)(...{result="rejected_invalid"})` the DA breakdown.
- endpoint.verdicts_total{endpoint, verdict}: folds the per-endpoint
  valid/invalid/unavailable counters into one labeled counter.
- quorum_verdicts_collected (histogram) + quorum_min_responses (gauge):
  definitive verdicts collected per check vs the configured threshold, the
  leading indicator for how close the filter runs to failing closed.

Decision/label logic lives in pure functions (validation_reason,
decision_for_error) with exhaustive unit tests. Behavior unchanged.

* feat(op-reth): address interop metrics review feedback

  endpoint.up gauge (1/0 = answered its last completed check, stale on
  fast-accept cancellation). sum(endpoint.up) vs quorum_min_responses is
  the fail-closed headroom and is leading, not coincident: fast-accept
  pinned the histogram at the threshold so it could never warn early.

`validation_reason` and `decision_for_error` via intra-doc links, which fails

feat(kona-executor): make StatelessL2Builder/KonaExecutor generic over receipt builder (#21275)

Parameterizes `StatelessL2Builder`, `KonaExecutor`, `BlockBuildingOutcome`,
and `Executor::Receipt` over a receipt builder `R: OpReceiptBuilder`.
In-tree call sites pass `OpAlloyReceiptBuilder::default()` so the OP path
is byte-for-byte identical.

## Motivation

Celo (a downstream OP-Stack fork) needs to produce blocks whose receipts
include a CIP-64 variant. The stateless executor currently pipes
`OpReceiptEnvelope` through everywhere, so the only way to ship Celo's
receipt envelope is to fork the entire builder + executor. This change
swaps the concrete type for a single generic parameter.

## Trait extensions

`OpReceiptBuilder` gains:

* `strip_deposit_nonce(&self, receipt: &mut Self::Receipt)` — required
  (no default). Drives the Regolith receipts-root fixup that was
  previously inlined in `compute_receipts_root`. Required so any
  downstream implementor whose receipt envelope carries a deposit nonce
  is forced to confront the fixup at compile time rather than silently
  inherit a no-op.
* `type Receipt: TxReceipt<Log = Log> + Clone` — moves a bound bundle off
  every kona-executor impl site. `Encodable2718` stays as a call-site
  bound because not every impl's `Receipt` implements it.

## Compatibility

* No generic default on `R` — every caller is updated explicitly.
* Out-of-tree `OpReceiptBuilder` implementors need to add a
  `strip_deposit_nonce` impl.
* Out-of-tree `Executor` implementors need to add
  `type Receipt = ...;`.
* Wire formats are unchanged.

## Follow-up

The transaction side is still concrete (`Transaction = OpTxEnvelope`);
parameterizing it is a separate change.

feat: support Tenderly's new ?draft= simulation link format (#1458)

* feat: support Tenderly's new ?draft= simulation link format

Tenderly shipped a breaking change to how the Simulator hydrates a
pre-filled form from a URL. The old query-param format
(network/contractAddress/from/stateOverrides/rawFunctionInput) no longer
applies state overrides or gas — signers had to re-enter everything by
hand, defeating the purpose of the printed link.

The new format encodes the whole simulation as a single JSON payload,
base64url-encoded (no padding), in a ?draft= query parameter:

  https://dashboard.tenderly.co/<org>/<project>/simulator/new?draft=<b64url(json)>

Changes:
- MultisigTaskPrinter.getTenderlySimulationLink builds the draft payload
  (v/network.id/row with contractAddress, from, inputDataType, gas,
  rawFunctionInput, stateOverrides) and encodes it with solady Base64
  (fileSafe + noPadding). printTenderlySimulationData uses it.
- Length fallback: the new format caps usable links at ~2000 chars, so
  when calldata is too large to embed, the link is built without
  rawFunctionInput and the calldata is printed separately for manual
  paste into the Simulator's "Raw input data" field (mirrors prior
  long-URL behavior).
- Unit tests covering the inline, no-raw-input, and no-gas paths.
- Docs updated to the new format.

payload builder tracks the cumulative EIP-2718 encoded size of every
transaction included in the block (sequencer/deposit txs and mempool
txs) and stops pulling further mempool transactions once including the
next one would push the total past the configured limit. Unset (the
default) disables the cap, preserving existing behavior.

feat(kona-protocol): construct L2BlockInfo from a sealed header and raw first tx

Add L2BlockInfo::from_header_and_first_tx, a constructor for callers
that hold a sealed header and the raw EIP-2718-encoded transactions of
a block rather than a fully decoded OpBlock. Compared to
from_block_and_genesis it:

- takes the block hash from the seal instead of recomputing it with
  hash_slow(); the caller must guarantee that the seal is the header's
  true hash (debug-asserted),
- decodes at most the first transaction -- the L1-info deposit -- and
  classifies it by its EIP-2718 type byte first, so a typed non-deposit
  first tx is reported as FirstTxNonDeposit without being decoded,
- uses strict decode_2718_exact, rejecting trailing bytes,
- skips the first transaction entirely at the genesis block, matching
  from_block_and_genesis, which never inspects transactions there.

The L1-origin and sequence-number extraction is shared with
from_block_and_genesis through a private from_block_info_and_first_tx
core, so the two constructors cannot drift apart.

perf(kona-driver): decode only the L1-info deposit when computing L2BlockInfo

executor's sealed header and attributes.transactions.first(). The O(n)

proof program.

the returned header's seal must be its true hash: the driver now relies
on it for the derived L2BlockInfo as well as for the safe-head cursor.

OpTxEnvelope-decodable (e.g. Celo's CIP-64) can use kona-driver
unmodified, since only the first (deposit) transaction is decoded.

* fix(txinclude): budget operator fees with the Jovian formula (#17817)

txinclude estimated and reconciled operator fees with the Isthmus formula
(gasUsed * scalar / 1e6 + constant), which under-budgets on Jovian chains
where the formula is gasUsed * scalar * 100 + constant.

estimate and the post-inclusion actual cost. Jovian is exact on Jovian chains
(all production chains) and is >= the Isthmus result for any inputs, so on a
pre-Jovian chain it only over-reserves budget and never under-budgets.

op-reth's payload builder can produce blocks whose uncompressed
(EIP-2718 encoded) size exceeds the ~10 MiB JSON payload limit that
many consensus-layer clients assume for engine_getPayload responses.
op-geth enforces an equivalent cap via the non-configurable

payload builder tracks the cumulative EIP-2718 encoded size of every
transaction included in the block (sequencer/deposit txs and mempool
txs) and stops pulling further mempool transactions once including the
next one would push the total past the configured limit. Unset (the
default) disables the cap, preserving existing behavior.

fix(rollup-boost): append trailing SDM PostExec tx when materializing flashblocks (#21320)

* fix(rollup-boost): materialize SDM post_exec_tx in flashblock payloads

Each flashblock carries the current trailing SDM PostExec transaction in
diff.post_exec_tx, which replaces the previous one rather than
accumulating in the append-only diff.transactions list. rollup-boost's
FlashblockBuilder dropped it when materializing the execution payload,
so the materialized block no longer hashed to the builder's
diff.block_hash, the sequencer EL rejected it via newPayload, and
op-node fell back to the EL's independently-built block.

- rollup-boost: materialize the block as base + concat(all
  diff.transactions) + latest(diff.post_exec_tx), with unit tests for
  the append/replace/omit cases on V3 and V4 payloads.
- op-rbuilder: accumulate receipt cumulative gas from the committed
  (post-SDM-refund) gas instead of the pre-refund EVM result gas, which
  caused a receipt-root mismatch on canonical verification.
- acceptance test: assert the canonical block hash equals the builder's
  diff.block_hash, pinning the test to the rollup-boost materialization
  path instead of passing under the EL fallback.

Use `flashblocks.last().and_then(...)` (O(1)) instead of a reverse scan,
relying on the protocol guarantee that once a flashblock carries post_exec_tx
all subsequent ones do too. Also drop the redundant `payload_id` field in the
test helper and remove the now-impossible "preserves when later delta omits"

fix(MultisigTask): treat EIP-7702 delegated EOA owners as EOAs

Safe owners are classified as contract owners (child Safes) whenever they
have code. An EIP-7702 delegated EOA carries the 23-byte delegation
designator (0xef0100 ++ address) as code, so the harness treated it as a
Safe and called nonce() on it, which reverts when the delegation target
does not expose a Safe interface. This broke simulation for any task
signed by a Safe with a 7702-delegated owner (e.g. the Ink SystemConfig
owner Safe on mainnet).

Add Utils.isEip7702DelegatedEOA and exclude such owners from the
owner-Safe nonce checks in _overrideState and from the Safe branch of
_incrementOwnerNonce.

U19 upgrade tasks for Mainnet (#1441)

* fix(OPCMUpgradeV700): support standard chains in U19 upgrade template

Three fixes discovered while simulating U19 upgrades on standard superchain-registry
chains for the first time (all prior V700 use was betanet-only):

1. SuperchainAddressRegistry._fetchAndSaveInitialContracts: register EthLockboxProxy
   per-chain from the registry JSON when present. Standard chain discovery (via
   _processAddresses) didn't include EthLockboxProxy, so it was missing from the
   allowed storage accesses allowlist, causing the state-diff validator to reject
   valid OPCM upgrade state changes.

2. OPCMUpgradeV700._setAllowedStorageAccesses: use try/catch when fetching
   ProtocolVersions per-chain. Standard chains store ProtocolVersions on the sentinel
   chain (via addresses.toml), not per L2 chainId, so getAddress("ProtocolVersions",
   chainId) reverted for any non-betanet chain.

3. OPCMUpgradeV700._getCodeExceptions: only include true EOAs (no code). Some chains
   (e.g. Ink) use a multisig Safe as SystemConfig.owner(). Adding a contract address
   to the EOA exceptions list caused "unexpected code" validation failures when the
   OPCM re-initializes SystemConfig and writes the owner to storage slot 0x33.

4. OPCMUpgradeV700._build: skip upgradeSuperchain() if SuperchainConfig is already
   at the v7.1.17 implementation. Chains with non-standard L1PAOs (e.g. Unichain)

The rust-build-vendored job caches the release op-rbuilder and rollup-boost
binaries used by the sysgo acceptance jobs (memory-all-*). Its content hash was
`git ls-tree -r HEAD <directory>` over only the build directory (rust/op-rbuilder
or rust/rollup-boost). But both are their own Cargo workspaces that path-depend
on sibling crates under rust/ — op-reth, op-revm, op-alloy, alloy-op-evm,
alloy-op-hardforks (and each other). A change to one of those siblings did not
change the cache key, so CI restored a STALE binary: e.g. an alloy-op-evm fix
never made it into the op-rbuilder binary the acceptance jobs ran, producing a
false red (and, in the dangerous direction, could produce a false green).

Add a `hash_paths` parameter (defaults to `directory`) and key both vendored
builds on the full vendored-crate closure they compile. Over-hashing only ever
forces an extra rebuild; it never serves stale content. A guard fails fast if a
hash_paths entry doesn't exist at HEAD (git ls-tree silently emits nothing for a
bogus path, which would otherwise re-open this hole). Bump the key v8 -> v9 to

fix(alloy-op-evm): roll back SDM block-warming for declined op-rbuilder candidates

SDM block-warming refunds are recorded by an inspector during EVM execution —
before the commit decision — and are not journaled, so discarding a tx's changes
does not roll them back. The op-rbuilder payload builder selects txs via
execute_transaction_with_commit_condition and declines candidates
(CommitChanges::No) that exceed a builder gas/DA/address limit or are
reverted-and-excluded; those declined candidates still warmed the maps, so a
later committed tx could claim a block-warming refund attributed to a tx that
never entered the block. Commit-only paths (block import, debug_replaySDMBlock
derivation) never observe that warmth, so the producer's payload diverged from
derivation. With Osaka active (#21337) this surfaced as
TestFlashblocksSDMMaterializesPostExecBlock failing, so the test was skipped.

Fix: override execute_transaction_with_commit_condition on OpBlockExecutor to
snapshot the block-scoped warming state before execution and restore it whenever
the tx is not committed. The snapshot (a clone of the warming maps) is taken only
in Producing mode, so there is no clone cost when SDM is off or verifying.

- alloy-op-evm: the override plus a unit test for the declined-candidate rollback.
- op-rbuilder: comment at the decline site noting the rollback dependency.
- flashblocks_sdm_phantom_test.go: TestFlashblocksSDMPhantomWarmingDivergence
  drives a persistently-declined poisoner alongside committed victims and, per
  victim block, compares the producer-baked SDM payload against the commit-only
  derivation. FAILS pre-fix (divergent_blocks=6, refund 18400 vs 0), PASSES after.
- flashblocks_sdm_test.go: re-enable TestFlashblocksSDMMaterializesPostExecBlock
  (remove the t.Skip) and match the streamed flashblock to the sealed block by
  canonical hash instead of a "final flashblock" guess, fixing the 9-vs-15 flake.

Fixes: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21354

Fixes reproducing the trailing SDM PostExec tx (0x7D) when rebuilding a
derived block. OP consensus requires at most one PostExec tx, and it must
be last.

alloy-op-evm: reject user txs in fork-activation blocks (forks ≥ Jovian) (#21326)

* alloy-op-evm: reject user txs in fork-activation blocks

A fork-activation block (the first L2 block at/after a fork >= Jovian) must
contain only deposit transactions. op-geth enforces this at the executor /
consensus-validity layer (CalcDAFootprint); the shared Rust executor
(alloy-op-evm, used by both op-reth and kona-client) did not — a latent
consensus-validity divergence where op-reth / kona-client would accept an
activation block with user txs that op-geth rejects.

Add a guard to OpBlockExecutor that rejects any non-deposit (user) tx on a
fork-activation block. The block is detected from a new required
OpBlockExecutionCtx::parent_timestamp via OpHardfork::Jovian.forks_from(), so the
rule covers Jovian, Karst, Lagoon and any future fork automatically.
parent_timestamp is populated where the parent header is available (kona
StatelessL2Builder — the fault-proof path — and op-reth block building); op-reth's
block-import / engine-newPayload paths pass None and defer to the derivation
layer (op-node + kona drop user-tx batches in fork-activation blocks).

Also adds OpHardfork::forks_from() to alloy-op-hardforks (a go-ethereum
forks.From analogue).

Fixes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism-private/issues/553

feat(op-reth): build OP Mainnet/Sepolia chainspecs from the superchain registry

The well-known OP chains (`--chain optimism` / `optimism-sepolia`) were built from
hand-coded fork schedules (`OP_MAINNET_HARDFORKS` / `OP_SEPOLIA_HARDFORKS`) that lagged
the embedded superchain registry. The registry already schedules Karst (and therefore
the L1 Osaka feature set), but the hand-coded lists stopped at Jovian, so a node would
not have activated Karst at the registry-scheduled time and would have diverged from the
network at the fork boundary (op-sepolia: 2026-06-17, op-mainnet: 2026-07-08).

Build these specs from the embedded registry instead — the same `from_genesis` path the
long-tail superchain chains already use — so fork activations track the registry and a
new hardfork only needs a registry bump rather than a hand-edited fork list.

OP Mainnet's Bedrock genesis ships an empty `alloc` plus a precomputed state root, which
`from_genesis` cannot reconstruct (it derives the state root from `alloc`). Restore the
state root explicitly and re-seal the genesis header, then assert the canonical genesis
hash — mirroring op-geth's `stateHash` handling in core/superchain.go. OP Sepolia ships a
full `alloc`, so it reconstructs directly; its genesis hash is verified the same way.

Base stays on its hand-coded spec: its genesis/config are not bundled in the embedded
registry archive. A `not(superchain-configs)` fallback keeps the hand-coded specs for
builds without the registry archive.

fix(mise): resolve just via default registry, not github/ubi alias

The reproducible cannon prestate build (cannon-repro.dockerfile) runs
`mise install ... just` inside the pinned cannon-builder:v2.0.0 image,
whose old mise maps `github:casey/just` to the deprecated ubi backend.

just's release tags have no `v` prefix. While the pinned version is recent
enough to appear in GitHub's releases listing, ubi matches it directly. Once
it ages out of that listing (just 1.52.0 landed 2026-06-08), ubi falls back
to direct-fetching a `v`-prefixed tag (`v1.46.0`) that doesn't exist and the
build 404s — breaking develop-fault-proofs at the cannon-prestate job, before
op-e2e-cannon-tests even runs.

Drop the alias so just resolves through the default registry (aqua), which
fetches the exact pinned tag regardless of recency. The version pin is
unchanged; aqua is already proven in this image (jq resolves via it).

fix(FeeVaultUpgradeTemplate): configure vaults via setters, not initialize

The template upgraded each fee-vault proxy with
`ProxyAdmin.upgradeAndCall(proxy, impl, initialize(recipient, min, network))`.
On any chain whose fee vaults are already initialized in L2 genesis (OpenZeppelin
v5 `_initialized == 1`), `initialize` carries the `initializer` modifier
(version 1, not a bumped `reinitializer`), so it reverts with
`InvalidInitialization()`. The OP `Proxy` masks the inner revert as
"delegatecall to new implementation contract failed", `upgradeAndCall` rolls
back, and the L1 task tx still succeeds — so the recipient silently never
changes on L2. The pre-flight only checks L2 ProxyAdmin ownership, not the
already-initialized case, making this fail confusingly.

Fix: deposit `ProxyAdmin.upgrade(proxy, impl)` (no initializer call) followed by
the v1.6.0 storage setters setRecipient / setMinWithdrawalAmount /
setWithdrawalNetwork, each gated by the L2 ProxyAdmin owner (the aliased
rootSafe these deposits run as). Works whether or not the proxy was previously
initialized — same approach as RevShareCommon.configureVaultsForRevShare. Per
vault: 1 upgrade + 3 setters (was 1 upgradeAndCall); _validate updated.

Regenerated the FeeVaultUpgradeTemplate regression fixtures (expectedCallData +
nested-multisig data-to-sign) for the new deposit pattern.

fix(op-reth): evict definitively-invalid interop txs on revalidation

The interop txpool revalidation sweep gated eviction on reth's
`is_bad_transaction()`, which is true only for `CrossChainTxPreInterop`
and false for `ValidationError(_)`. A definitive invalid verdict from the
interop filter (`InvalidEntry`/`Rejected`) therefore stayed buildable
until its ~2h cached deadline expired.

`is_bad_transaction()` answers reth's peer-penalization question, a
different concern from "is this tx now invalid and must be evicted". Add a
dedicated `InvalidCrossTx::is_now_invalid()` predicate and use it in the
revalidation sweep: evict on a decisive invalid verdict, retain on
transient/non-decisive outcomes (quorum miss, timeout, data-unavailable,
disagreement) so a flapping or unreachable interop filter cannot drain the
pool. Failsafe stays handled by the whole-pool eviction. reth's
peer-penalization predicate is left unchanged.
